# Exit codes

A command ends with the code of its outcome. Codes 0, 1 and 2 keep their usual meaning, 130 is the POSIX code of an interrupted process, and the codes from 10 name the category of the failure. An exception that a command does not catch ends with the code of its class: Exceptions and error codes lists the classes and their `HMPY.Exxx` codes.

| Code | Name | Raised for | Set directly by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | `EXIT_OK` | Nothing: the command succeeded. | 15 commands `hmp workspace list`, `hmp workspace register`, `hmp workspace search`, `hmp workspace forget`, `hmp workspace prune`, `hmp example add`, `hmp catalog gc`, `hmp audit`, `hmp privacy`, `hmp site-selection plan`, `hmp site-selection select-catchments`, `hmp site-selection build-observed`, `hmp site-selection build-generated`, `hmp site-selection report`, `hmp install-binaries` |
| `1` | `EXIT_GENERIC` | Any exception that no other row maps. | 3 commands `hmp catalog query`, `hmp data import`, `hmp doctor` |
| `2` | `EXIT_USAGE` | `JobUsageError` | 8 commands `hmp catalog delete`, `hmp catalog tag`, `hmp catalog rerun`, `hmp export`, `hmp viz show`, `hmp config`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp test` |
| `10` | `EXIT_NOT_FOUND` | `FileNotFoundError`, `SimulationNotFoundError` | 47 commands `hmp workspace register`, `hmp workspace clean`, `hmp project new`, `hmp project list`, `hmp project show`, `hmp project delete`, `hmp example list`, `hmp example show`, `hmp example add`, `hmp catalog ls`, `hmp catalog query`, `hmp catalog show`, `hmp catalog point`, `hmp catalog gc`, `hmp catalog delete`, `hmp catalog restore`, `hmp catalog trash`, `hmp catalog tag`, `hmp catalog note`, `hmp catalog rename`, `hmp catalog diff`, `hmp catalog watch`, `hmp catalog import`, `hmp catalog rerun`, `hmp data add`, `hmp data import`, `hmp viz list`, `hmp viz show`, `hmp viz gallery`, `hmp config`, `hmp dev run-script`, `hmp dev schema`, `hmp dev lock`, `hmp dev rank`, `hmp dev manage`, `hmp audit`, `hmp privacy`, `hmp run`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp spinup`, `hmp site-selection plan`, `hmp site-selection select-catchments`, `hmp site-selection build-observed`, `hmp site-selection build-generated`, `hmp site-selection report`, `hmp report`, `hmp doctor` |
| `11` | `EXIT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` | `CapabilityVersionMismatchError`, `SchemaVersionMismatchError` | |
| `12` | `EXIT_WRITE_CONFLICT` | `ImportConflictError`, `WriteConflictError` | |
| `13` | `EXIT_READ_ONLY` | `ReadOnlyError` | |
| `14` | `EXIT_CONFIG` | `ConfigError`, `ConfigMissingError` | 54 commands `hmp workspace init`, `hmp workspace register`, `hmp workspace clean`, `hmp project new`, `hmp project list`, `hmp project show`, `hmp project delete`, `hmp catalog ls`, `hmp catalog query`, `hmp catalog show`, `hmp catalog point`, `hmp catalog gc`, `hmp catalog reindex`, `hmp catalog delete`, `hmp catalog restore`, `hmp catalog trash`, `hmp catalog tag`, `hmp catalog note`, `hmp catalog rename`, `hmp catalog diff`, `hmp catalog watch`, `hmp catalog import`, `hmp catalog rerun`, `hmp data ls`, `hmp data get`, `hmp data check`, `hmp data add`, `hmp data remove`, `hmp data prune`, `hmp data archive`, `hmp data restore`, `hmp data import`, `hmp export`, `hmp viz list`, `hmp viz show`, `hmp viz gallery`, `hmp config`, `hmp dev schema`, `hmp dev examples`, `hmp dev lock`, `hmp dev manage`, `hmp audit`, `hmp privacy`, `hmp run`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp spinup`, `hmp site-selection plan`, `hmp site-selection select-catchments`, `hmp site-selection build-observed`, `hmp site-selection build-generated`, `hmp site-selection report`, `hmp report`, `hmp doctor`, `hmp install-binaries` |

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/export.html -->
# `hmp export`

Uses hmp.open(), hmp.export().

```
$ hmp export [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--list] [--time TIME [TIME ...]] [--period START END] [--format {netcdf,geotiff,csv,geopackage,shapefile,vtu,package,stac,rocrate,prov}] [--folder FOLDER] [--file FILE] [--crs CRS] [--resolution RESOLUTION] [--layer LAYER] SIM_REF [VARIABLE ...]
```

Export data of a run: fields, series, layers, the budget, or the whole run

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SIM_REF` | Full sim_id, unique hex prefix, name, or an @-selector (@last, @best:METRIC, @worst:METRIC, @running) |
| `VARIABLE` | What to export: names from --list, or "all" for everything the run holds, each in its natural format |
| `--list` | Print what this run can export, by kind, and write nothing |
| `--time``TIME [TIME ...]` | Instants to write: dates (2002-10-15), "first" or "last". A date takes the stress period that holds it. Default: the whole simulation |
| `--period``START END` | A window of the simulation, two dates. Every period it overlaps is written |
| `--format``FORMAT` | File format. Default: the natural format of each data, or the --file extension one of `netcdf` | `geotiff` | `csv` | `geopackage` | `shapefile` | `vtu` | `package` | `stac` | `rocrate` | `prov` |
| `--folder``FOLDER` | Folder to write into, with automatic names (default: share/<run>/) |
| `--file``FILE` | One exact file; its extension gives the format |
| `--crs``CRS` | Output CRS of rasters and vector layers, e.g. EPSG:4326 (default: the model CRS) |
| `--resolution``RESOLUTION` | Pixel size of a GeoTIFF, in units of the output CRS (default: from the mesh) |
| `--layer``LAYER` | Model layer of a field of several layers (0 is the top one) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp export my_run --list
$ hmp export my_run all
$ hmp export my_run head watertable_depth --time 2002-10-15
$ hmp export my_run discharge discharge_obs --period 2001-01-01 2002-12-31
$ hmp export my_run watershed hydrographic_network_reference
$ hmp export my_run watertable_depth --time last --file watertable.tif --crs EPSG:4326
$ hmp export my_run all --format package
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 14. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.

| `REPORT_CONFIG` | Catchment report TOML configuration. |
| `--run-overview`, `--no-run-overview` | Run the configured overview before building report artifacts. |
| `--run-simulation`, `--no-run-simulation` | Run the configured simulation before building report artifacts. |
| `--context-only` | Build only the context artifacts, not the final HTML report. |
| `--report-only` | Build only the final HTML report from existing context artifacts. |
| `--with-lock` | Do not pass --no-lock to the optional hydromodpy run steps. |
| `--stream-run-logs`, `--no-stream-run-logs` | Stream logs from optional hydromodpy run steps. |
| `--strict-figure-postflight`, `--no-strict-figure-postflight` | Fail when post-render figure completeness checks find missing figures. |
| `--preset``PRESET` | Override the catchment report preset declared in the TOML. one of `generic` | `generic_catchment_report` |

Also takes the shared options `--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp report catchment report.toml
$ hmp report catchment report.toml --report-only
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/run.html -->
# `hmp run`

Uses hmp.run().

```
$ hmp run [-h] [--profile [HTML_PATH]] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--resume REF] [--from STEP] [--until STEP] [--dry-run] [--frozen] [--force] [--no-lock] [--no-display] [--no-parallel] [--overlay OVERLAY] [--set PATH=VALUE] [config]
```

Run a workflow from a TOML config

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `config` | Path to a TOML config (omit when using --resume REF) |
| `--resume``REF` | Resume a simulation from its last journalled checkpoint. With a TOML config, REF is the run name/id to resume; without a config, REF is a catalog reference and the run replays its own runs/<name>/config.toml. |
| `--from``STEP` | Resume from a specific pipeline step (name or index). |
| `--until``STEP` | Stop after the specified pipeline step (name or index). |
| `--dry-run` | Print the resolved workflow plan without executing it. |
| `--frozen` | Reject any fresh download when hydromodpy.lock is present; every artefact must already be in the catalog and match its SHA-256. |
| `--force` | Recompute even when a completed run with an identical resolved config and the same name already exists. Without it such a run is not recomputed: the command stops and names it. The comparison hashes the resolved config, so an edit, or a hydromodpy version that resolves the same TOML differently, makes it a new run. Simulation workflow only. |
| `--no-lock` | Skip the post-run hydromodpy.lock write (default: write). |
| `--no-display` | Skip auto-rendering of the figures listed in [display].figures. |
| `--no-parallel` | Force the Pipeline to run cohorts sequentially. Useful for debugging or to keep deterministic step ordering. |
| `--overlay``OVERLAY` | TOML overlay applied after base_config inheritance. Repeatable. How overlays merge into the file |
| `--set``PATH=VALUE` | Dotted TOML override applied after overlays, e.g. workspace.project_root=out. The grammar of a key path and a value |

Also takes the shared options `--profile``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp run run.toml
$ hmp run run.toml --dry-run
$ hmp run run.toml --set simulation.name=my_run
$ hmp run run.toml --overlay daily.toml
$ hmp run run.toml --from setup_process --until run_solver
$ hmp run --resume ab12cd34
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14 130. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.

# `hmp test`

```
$ hmp test [-h] [--list] [--fast] [--slow] [--extensive] [--nwt] [--mf6] [--intercomparison] [--steady] [--transient] [--analytical] [--short] [--update-goldens] [-j JOBS] {unit,regression,validation} [name]
```


Render one figure for a simulation

| Argument | What it does |

| `SIM_REF` | Full sim_id, unique hex prefix, name, or an @-selector (@last, @best:METRIC, @worst:METRIC, @running) |


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/data-sources.html -->
# Data sources

Every data section of the file, and the sources its `source` key accepts, with who publishes each one and under which licence. Read from the configuration models and from the source registry of the code (`hydromodpy.schema.sources`), which carries one entry per source. A field added to an entry shows up here on its own.

A source marked “licence not determined” has no licence recorded in the code. The reason sits in the details of the source, and a run that reads it does not claim a licence for its outputs.

The keys that declare the data of a project are in [data]. A new provider is added by registering a source: Add a data source.

By section

| Section | Accepted values of `source` |
| --- | --- |
| `[data.crossings]` |
- `custom`: a file of the project
- `bdtopo`: downloads from `data.geopf.fr` · IGN · licence etalab-2.0 assumed Roads and railways of the IGN BD TOPO, from the Geoplateforme WFS. Details
  - Attribution Source: IGN, BD TOPO roads and railways
  - Hosts contacted `data.geopf.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bd-topo-r, https://cartes.gouv.fr/cgu
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bd-topo-r, https://cartes.gouv.fr/cgu
  - Coverage Metropolitan France and several overseas territories. The adapter reads the road and railway layers over a box in EPSG:2154.
  - Resolution 3D vector objects of metric precision.
  - Period Editions from 2008-03-18 to 2026-09-15; the code pins no edition.
  - Update Quarterly editions, with a weekly BDTOPO Express edition since May 2025.
  - Authentication None sent by the adapter.
  - Limits cartes.gouv.fr terms: WFS 30 requests/s, WMS-Raster 40 requests/s, download 5 requests per 5 s with a 5 minute ban; over the limit the service answers 429.
  - Cache folder: data/crossings, pattern: crossings_bdtopo_*.gpkg, format: GeoPackage, note: crossings_bdtopo_<bbox hash>.gpkg. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence IGN, publishing on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation, gives BD TOPO the 'Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0'. The WFS capabilities point to the cartes.gouv.fr terms and state 'Fees: none'.
- `roe`: downloads from `services.sandre.eaufrance.fr` · Sandre / OFB · licence etalab-2.0 assumed Obstacles to flow of the Sandre ROE (dams, weirs, bridge sills), from the Sandre WFS. Details
  - Attribution Source: Sandre (OFB), ROE obstacles to flow
  - Hosts contacted `services.sandre.eaufrance.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.sandre.eaufrance.fr/atlas/srv/api/records/070df464-73d3-4c00-be2f-93f2a97ef8f5
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://www.sandre.eaufrance.fr/atlas/srv/api/records/070df464-73d3-4c00-be2f-93f2a97ef8f5, https://services.sandre.eaufrance.fr/geo/obs?SERVICE=WFS&VERSION=2.0.0&REQUEST=GetCapabilities
  - Coverage Metropolitan France (layer sa:ObstEcoul_FXX), one point per obstacle.
  - Resolution Points, equivalent scale 1:50 000.
  - Period The record gives no temporal extent; it was revised on 2026-10-08 at the check.
  - Update Weekly.
  - Authentication None: free access.
  - Cache folder: data/crossings, pattern: crossings_roe_*.gpkg, format: GeoPackage, note: crossings_roe_<bbox hash>.gpkg. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence The Sandre atlas record 'Obstacles à l'écoulement - Métropole' lists 'Licence Ouverte Etalab' as its use limitation and 'Pas de restriction d'accès public'. The WFS capabilities state 'Fees: no conditions apply'.
 |
| `[data.dem]` |
- `custom`: a file of the project
- `ign_geoplateforme_dem`: downloads from `data.geopf.fr` · IGN · licence etalab-2.0 assumed Recommended IGN DEM source: BD ALTI from archives, RGE ALTI from WMS-Raster. Details
  - Attribution Source: IGN, Geoplateforme elevation data
  - Hosts contacted `data.geopf.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bd-alti-r-1, https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/rge-alti-r, https://cartes.gouv.fr/cgu
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bd-alti-r-1, https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/rge-alti-r, https://cartes.gouv.fr/cgu
  - Coverage BD ALTI and RGE ALTI cover metropolitan and overseas France except French Polynesia, New Caledonia and Wallis and Futuna. RGE ALTI holds nodata over the zones closed to aerial capture. The adapter takes a box in EPSG:2154.
  - Resolution BD ALTI: regular grid, 25 m (75 m also published); the adapter assembles 25 m ASC archives. RGE ALTI: regular grid, 1 m or 5 m, fetched by extent from the WMS-Raster service.
  - Period BD ALTI: records from 2011-01-01 to 2023-10-04. RGE ALTI: from 2009-01-01 to 2024-11-26; its updates stopped in 2024, pending the LiDAR HD survey.
  - Update BD ALTI: irregular, from RGE ALTI. RGE ALTI: irregular, stopped in 2024.
  - Authentication None sent by the adapter. The cartes.gouv.fr terms say some APIs may need an account, according to their documentation.
  - Limits cartes.gouv.fr terms: WFS 30 requests/s, WMS-Raster 40 requests/s, download 5 requests per 5 s with a 5 minute ban; over the limit the service answers 429.
  - Cache folder: data/dem/processed, pattern: dem_ign_geoplateforme_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: dem_ign_geoplateforme_bdalti_25m_<hash>.tif and dem_ign_geoplateforme_rgealti_<resolution>_<hash>.tif. The BD ALTI department archives stay in data/dem/raw_ign and data/dem/extracted_ign.
  - Why this licence IGN, publishing on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation, gives BD ALTI and RGE ALTI the 'Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0'. The cartes.gouv.fr terms add that a Geoplateforme dataset without another licence falls under the Licence Ouverte Etalab.
 |
| `[data.etp]` |
- `custom`: a file of the project
- `sim2`: downloads from `api.geosas.fr` · Meteo-France, served by GeoSAS · licence etalab-2.0 assumed Details
  - Attribution Source : Météo France
  - Hosts contacted `api.geosas.fr`
  - Licence pages https://geosas.fr/geonetwork/apps/api/records/4ee133fa-d4cb-44d8-b708-46946573ba5f, https://api.geosas.fr/edr/collections/safran-isba?f=json, https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/donnees-changement-climatique-sim-quotidienne
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://api.geosas.fr/edr/collections/safran-isba?f=json, https://geosas.fr/geonetwork/apps/api/records/4ee133fa-d4cb-44d8-b708-46946573ba5f, https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/donnees-changement-climatique-sim-quotidienne
  - Coverage Metropolitan France, on the SAFRAN grid. The service CRS is IGNF:LAMBE (Lambert II extended); the adapter asks for EPSG:2154.
  - Resolution Daily values on a regular 8 km grid (0.072 degrees).
  - Period From 1958-08-01. The service reported an end of 2026-09-17 on 2026-10-09.

Stream flow state: more than 10 years. Groundwater quality: over 100 million analyses at the start of 2021. The other APIs state no start date.
- Update Hydrometry: every 5 minutes for real-time values, daily for elaborated ones. Groundwater levels: daily. Groundwater and river quality: synchronised with their source databases.
- Authentication None: the terms ask for no registration and the adapters send no key.
- Limits No limit stated on the terms page, which asks users to minimise resource use by filtering and compressing.
- Cache folder: data/hydrometry, pattern: hydrometry_hubeau_*.csv, format: CSV, note: hydrometry_hubeau_<station>_<start>_<end>_<frequency>.csv, one per station; hydrometry_hubeau_LOC.csv lists the station locations. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/piezometry, pattern: piezometry_hubeau_*.csv, format: CSV, note: Same naming as hydrometry, with the prefix piezometry., folder: data/intermittency, pattern: intermittency_hubeau_*.csv, format: CSV, note: Same naming as hydrometry, with the prefix intermittency., folder: data/water_quality, pattern: waterquality_hubeau_*.csv, format: CSV, note: Same naming as hydrometry, with the prefix waterquality (no underscore).
- Why this licence The Hub'Eau terms of use state: 'La réutilisation des Jeux de données est régie par la licence ouverte Etalab' and ask the user to cite the author of the datasets. They call the APIs 'libres d'accès et d'utilisation'.
 |

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/figures.html -->
# Figures

Every figure HydroModPy can draw, read from the figure registry of the code: what it reads, when it can be drawn, the options it takes with their type and default, and the class that draws it. Open a figure for its card. A preview image shows beside the name when one has been rendered for it.

To write a new figure, see Add a figure.

70 figures. A run draws the ones named in `display.figures`; `display.overrides` sets their options. `hmp viz show <run> <name>` draws one figure of a stored run.

## Balance

`flux_timeseries` Water-balance components

Signed domain fluxes per stress period.

- Reads tables `budgets`
- In the code `hydromodpy.display.figures.flux_timeseries.FluxTimeseries`
Options

| Option | Type | Default | Unit | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `figsize` | `tuple[float, float] | None` | `None` | `in` | Width and height of the figure. Left out, the figure's own size. For this figure: `(8.5, 4.5)`. |
| `include_storage` | `bool` | `False` | | Draw the storage change as well. Off by default: it is the residual. |
| `show_run_name` | `bool` | `True` | | Write the run name in the titles and in the card rows that name the run. Turn it off for a figure shown outside the project, where the run name means nothing to the reader. |
| `title` | `str | None` | `None` | | Text that replaces the main title of the figure. An empty string removes the title. Left out, the figure writes its own title. |
| `units` | `str` | `'m3/s'` | | "m3/s", or "mm/period" for the depth equivalent over the model domain, which is how a recharge is compared to a discharge. |

`mass_balance_error` Mass-balance closure error

Percent closure error of one balanced quantity over the run.

- Reads tables `mass_balance`
- In the code `hydromodpy.display.figures.mass_balance_error.MassBalanceError`
Options

| Option | Type | Default | Unit | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `figsize` | `tuple[float, float] | None` | `None` | `in` | Width and height of the figure. Left out, the figure's own size. For this figure: `(7.5, 4.0)`. |
| `quantity` | `str` | `'water'` | | Balanced quantity: "water" for the flow budget, "solute" for a transport run. |
| `show_run_name` | `bool` | `True` | | Write the run name in the titles and in the card rows that name the run. Turn it off for a figure shown outside the project, where the run name means nothing to the reader. |
| `title` | `str | None` | `None` | | Text that replaces the main title of the figure. An empty string removes the title. Left out, the figure writes its own title. |
| `tolerance` | `float` | `1.0` | `%` | Half-width of the band drawn around zero error; 0 draws no band. |

`water_budget` Water budget

Per-component IN/OUT bar chart, over the delineated catchment or the domain.

- Reads tables `budgets`
- In the code `hydromodpy.display.figures.water_budget.WaterBudget`
Options

| Option | Type | Default | Unit | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `figsize` | `tuple[float, float] | None` | `None` | `in` | Width and height of the figure. Left out, the figure's own size. For this figure: `(7.0, 4.5)`. |
| `show_run_name` | `bool` | `True` | | Write the run name in the titles and in the card rows that name the run. Turn it off for a figure shown outside the project, where the run name means nothing to the reader. |
| `title` | `str | None` | `None` | | Text that replaces the main title of the figure. An empty string removes the title. Left out, the figure writes its own title. |

`conditioning_impact_map` Top difference between two runs

Per-cell top difference between two runs on one mesh (`sim` minus `reference`).

| `direction` | `Literal['to_mapped', 'to_simulated']` | `'to_mapped'` | | "to_mapped" draws D_so, how far each simulated stream cell descends before it reaches the mapped network; "to_simulated" draws D_os, the reverse. |
| `extent` | `Literal['catchment', 'mesh']` | `'catchment'` | | "catchment" crops to the delineated watershed and counts the cells inside it; "mesh" keeps the whole modelled domain. |
| `figsize` | `tuple[float, float] | None` | `None` | `in` | Width and height of the figure. Left out, the figure's own size. For this figure: `(7.0, 6.6)`. |
| `show_run_name` | `bool` | `True` | | Write the run name in the titles and in the card rows that name the run. Turn it off for a figure shown outside the project, where the run name means nothing to the reader. |
| `tau_specific_ratio` | `float | None` | `None` | `-` | Seepage threshold as a fraction of the recharge a cell receives. Left out, the setting the run's network output scored with, else the criterion's default. |
| `time` | `date, "first" or "last"` | | | The instant drawn: a date ("2002-10-15"), "first" or "last". The figure draws the stress period that holds the date. Left out, the state the run's network output scored, else the last period. |
| `title` | `str | None` | `None` | | Text that replaces the main title of the figure. An empty string removes the title. Left out, the figure writes its own title. |

| `sides` | `int` | `2` | | Banks that drain into the stream: 2 for a reach drained from both sides, 1 for a single hillslope, which halves the coefficient. |
| `skip` | `int` | `0` | | Values dropped at the head of the series, where the forcing that built the mound still acts. |
| `station` | `str` | `'_catchment'` | | Station whose series is drawn: a gauge id, or "_catchment" for the series at the catchment outlet. |

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/aggregate.html -->
# `[calibration.aggregate]`

How several scored targets become one cost.

- `calibration.aggregate`[table] · optional · 4 user keys
[calibration.aggregate]

`# weighting = "manual"` : How the members are made comparable before the weights apply.
**Path**: `calibration.aggregate.weighting`
**More**: 'manual' takes the declared 'weight' of each block as the whole story, which is honest as long as the costs are already commensurable. 'error' divides each residual by what its instrument resolves, so the members become pure numbers first; it needs a residual criterion and an observation carrying an error model, and is refused without both.
**Values**:
- `"manual"`
- `"error"`
**Accepted**: "manual" | "error"

`# nested_gauges = "total"` : How two gauges on imbricated catchments are read.
**Path**: `calibration.aggregate.nested_gauges`
**More**: 'total' scores each against its own full drained area, which is what a gauge measures; the residuals are then statistically dependent, and no standard correction exists for that. 'incremental' scores the downstream one on what its own reach adds, downstream minus upstream, which is the only mechanisable way to make the two independent. Neither is inferred: the overlap is measured and reported whichever is chosen.
**Values**:
- `"total"`
- `"incremental"`
**Accepted**: "total" | "incremental"

`# min_samples = 1` : Fewest paired samples a member may be scored on. - >= 1
**Path**: `calibration.aggregate.min_samples`
**More**: An alignment that collapses to three days still returns a number, and a weight of 65 per cent resting on three days is not what the file says it is.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# on_member_failure = "veto"` : What one unscorable member does to the total.
**Path**: `calibration.aggregate.on_member_failure`
**More**: 'veto' makes the whole trial fail, which is the default because a partial cost is not comparable to a full one. 'drop' scores the survivors and records which member was left out, which has to be asked for explicitly.
**Values**:
- `"veto"`
- `"drop"`
**Accepted**: "veto" | "drop"


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/objective_blocks.html -->
# `[[calibration.objective_blocks]]`

Weighted metric block used by a composite objective.

- `calibration.objective_blocks`[[array of tables]] · optional · 6 user keys, 1 dev or expert

Repeat the table: one `[[calibration.objective_blocks]]` block per item.

Connections found in the code (1)
- The code says `calibration.outputs`: ... asks a model for the outputs [calibration.outputs] declares and scores them with [[calibration.objective_blocks]]; this document declares ... output(s) and ... block(s). Both are what this evaluator is for: without them there is nothing to ask for and nothing to weigh.

[[calibration.objective_blocks]]

`name = ‹string›` : Unique block identifier used in logs and persistence. required
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.name`
**Accepted**: string

`uses_outputs = ‹list of string›` : Outputs (by name) consumed by this block. required at least 1 item
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.uses_outputs`
**Accepted**: list of string
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)

`# metric = "rmse"` : Metric that scores this block against its observations.
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.metric`
**Values**:
- `"rmse"` : Root-mean-square error, in the observed unit; penalizes large misfits most.
- `"nse"` : Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency against the observed mean; the standard choice for a level or discharge series.
- `"kge"` : Kling-Gupta efficiency; separates correlation, variability and bias when NSE alone is ambiguous.
- `"mae"` : Mean absolute error, in the observed unit; less sensitive to outliers than RMSE.
- `"nse_log"` : NSE on log-transformed series; weights low flows as heavily as peaks, good for recessions.
- `"nse_delta"` : NSE on the increments of the series rather than its level; a level is an integral and can hide flux errors that compensate, which only its increments show.
- `"nse_seasonal"` : NSE against the seasonal cycle rather than the overall mean; asks whether the model beats climatology.
- `"reservoir"` : Half nse_seasonal plus half nse_delta, built for an impounded level: a plain NSE there is beaten by the seasonal cycle, and the increments are what carry the flux errors.
- `"distance_gap"` : Balances the simulated stream network against the mapped one; zero marks the crossing.
- `"distance_mean"` : Mean spatial offset between simulated and mapped streams; a diagnostic, not a substitute for distance_gap.
**Accepted**: "rmse" | "nse" | "kge" | "mae" | "nse_log" | "nse_delta" | "nse_seasonal" | "reservoir" | "distance_gap" | "distance_mean"

`# weight = 1.0` : Weight of this block in the sum of the block costs. - > 0
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.weight`
**More**: Only the ratios between weights matter.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# normalize_cost = false` : When True, divide the block cost by a reference scale, so it adds to other blocks as a pure number and a share means a share.
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.normalize_cost`
**More**: On a residual metric (rmse, mae) the scale is the standard deviation of the observations, their mean absolute value when that is zero. On a network distance (distance_gap, distance_mean) it is the output's validity_length, 2 h_obs under 'auto': a gap of one validity length costs 1, as much as an NSE of 0 on nse_log. Refused on an efficiency score, already a pure number.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# transform = "identity"` : Per-block cost transform applied before weighting.
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.transform`
**More**: Note that transform='log' takes the logarithm of the cost, which is not the same thing as metric='nse_log', an NSE computed on log-transformed series.
**Values**:
- `"identity"` : Uses the block cost as computed, with no transform.
- `"log"` : Takes log10 of the cost plus a small epsilon, compressing large costs before weighting.
- `"inverse"` : Takes -1 / (cost + epsilon), sharpening the gradient near a cost of zero.
**Accepted**: "identity" | "log" | "inverse"

`# warmup = ‹integer›` : Burn-in samples dropped from this block only, overriding [calibration].warmup_periods. >= 0 expert
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.warmup`
**More**: A count of samples, so twelve means a year at a monthly step and twelve days at a daily one. Write scoring_window.start instead, a date that means the same span at any step and bounds a network state too. Kept so older files load unchanged.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

# `[calibration.outputs]`

Named observables extracted from each candidate run.

- `calibration.outputs`{ name = table } · optional · 35 user keys, 3 dev or expert

One table per name you choose: `[calibration.outputs.<name>]`. The name is free text.

`support` selects the shape of this table. One tab per shape, the default first.

“point”
[calibration.outputs.<name>]

`support = "point"` : Observable extracted at a planar `(x, y)` point. chosen shape
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.support`
**More**: 'point' reads the variable at (x, y).
**Values**:
- `"point"` : Observable extracted at a planar `(x, y)` point.
- `"boundary"` : Observable extracted from a boundary package.
- `"cell"` : Observable extracted at one structured cell.
- `"lake"` : Observable extracted from a MODFLOW 6 LAK lake state.
- `"network"` : The mapped stream network as a calibration target.
**Accepted**: "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake" | "network"

`variable = "head"` : Simulated variable to extract (e.g. 'head', 'outlet_discharge'). required example value
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.variable`
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"head"`

`# observes = ‹string›` : Station whose loaded record this output is scored against.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observes`
**More**: The record is aligned on the simulated timestamps, so a weighted block scores dated observations rather than a vector typed into the file. The data family follows 'variable': discharge from hydrometry, head from piezometry, stage from lake_levels. Mutually exclusive with 'observed_values'. The station is located by its own record and not by coordinates written beside it, so this output and the single-metric route read the same cell and their costs are comparable; a station the project cannot locate is refused by name rather than scored on another quantity.
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: support = "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake"

`# geometry = ‹table { key = any value }›` : GeoJSON point geometry.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.geometry`
**More**: Coordinates are in metres.
**Accepted**: table { key = any value }
**Only if**: support = "point"

`# x = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : X coordinate. m
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.x`
**More**: Accepts a bare number (metres) or a pint string like '100 m'. Beside 'observes' it is not read, and loading warns so, unless snap_radius is set and the station's record carries no coordinate.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "point"

`# y = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Y coordinate. m
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.y`
**More**: Accepts a bare number (metres) or a pint string like '100 m'. Beside 'observes' it is not read, as for 'x'.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "point"

`# time = "all"` : 'all' keeps every time step; 'last' / 'first' selects one; a list of ISO timestamps selects specific steps.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.time`
**Values**:
- `"all"`
- `"last"`
- `"first"`
**Accepted**: "all" | "last" | "first" or list of string

`# reducer = "none"` : How the values kept by time are reduced before they are scored.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.reducer`
**Values**:
- `"mean"` : Scores one value: the mean of the kept values.
- `"sum"` : Scores one value: the sum of the kept values.
- `"last"` : Scores one value: the last kept value.
- `"none"` : Scores every kept value against its observation.
**Accepted**: "mean" | "sum" | "last" | "none"
**Only if**: support = "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake"

`# observed_values = ‹list of number›` : Hard-coded observed values, positional and dateless.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observed_values`
**More**: Name a station in 'observes' to score a record the project loaded instead.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Only if**: support = "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake"

`# snap_radius = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Opt-in. m
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.snap_radius`
**More**: Move this gauge onto the cell that drains the most within this radius, before it is scored. Accepts a bare number (metres) or a pint string like '150 m'; it is a maximum displacement, measured from the gauge coordinate to the cell centres. The drained area is the one the solver routes on the mesh, along the descent D of the build. Only for 'variable' = 'discharge'. With 'observes', a discharge station is then located by the coordinate of its record, which it otherwise is not, and snapped from there. Off by default: a gauge otherwise stays in the cell it resolves to, which may drain a small share of the catchment, and the run logs that share.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "point" | "cell"

`# observed_network = ‹"data.hydrography" | "geographic.river_network"›` : Where the mapped network comes from when it is not an explicit file.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observed_network`
**More**: Exactly one of this and 'stream_geometry_path' must be set.
**Values**:
- `"data.hydrography"` : Reuses the network the hydrography data family already loaded (a local file or an osm / bdtopage / euhydro download), clipped to the delineated catchment. Costs nothing new to configure but ties the criterion to whatever that section resolved.
- `"geographic.river_network"` : Derives the network from the DEM by a drainage-area threshold. K/R shapes both where the water table reaches the surface and the accumulation the threshold is cut on, so the criterion partly fits a seepage density onto a geomorphological one; warned once and recorded on every run that uses it.
**Accepted**: "data.hydrography" | "geographic.river_network"
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# stream_geometry_path = ‹path›` : Vector file holding the mapped stream network, read only from here: the criterion resolves no geometry of its own and does not reuse the one the hydrography data family loaded.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.stream_geometry_path`
**More**: The way out of 'observed_network' when neither of its two sources is the one you want scored.
**Accepted**: path
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# minimal_stream_geometry_path = ‹path›` : Vector file holding the minimal map: the permanent network, which the map named by 'observed_network' or 'stream_geometry_path' (the maximal map, every mapped reach) contains.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.minimal_stream_geometry_path`
**More**: Read as it is, never filtered by attribute. The maximal map scored is the union of the two, and the share of the minimal map outside the maximal one is published. In one state, the state is compared to this map and the maximal map is scored beside it as a validation outside the cost, as Abherve et al. (2025) do; with 'extent', it is the minimal bound. At most one of this and 'minimal_observed_network'.
**Accepted**: path
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# minimal_observed_network = ‹"data.hydrography"›` : Where the minimal map comes from when it is not an explicit file.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.minimal_observed_network`
**More**: 'data.hydrography' reads the permanent reaches the hydrography data family wrote beside its network, which it does only when its source says which reaches flow all year. Same role as 'minimal_stream_geometry_path'; at most one of the two.
**Values**:
- `"data.hydrography"`
**Accepted**: "data.hydrography"
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# tau_specific_ratio = 0.0001` : A cell releasing less than this fraction of its own recharge is not a seepage face. - >= 0
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.tau_specific_ratio`
**More**: Zero reproduces the purely geometric criterion of the paper. Frozen over the whole search: a threshold moving with the trial would cost the criterion its monotonicity.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# weighting = "cell"` : Average one cell one vote (the paper) or weighted by cell area.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.weighting`
**More**: Both values are always reported; use 'area' on a mesh refined along the streams, where cell density is highest exactly where distances are smallest.
**Values**:
- `"cell"` : Every cell counts once in the average, as in the paper.
- `"area"` : Every cell counts in proportion to its area.
**Accepted**: "cell" | "area"
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# diagonal_neighbors = true` : Descend over shared nodes, the eight D8 neighbours of a quad mesh.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.diagonal_neighbors`
**More**: True is the paper: its distances are traced by WhiteboxTools on a D8 pointer, and the delineation that produced the catchment uses one too. False descends over shared edges only, four neighbours (D4), and departs from the paper. It is not a second-decimal choice: on a synthetic valley whose talweg runs along the grid diagonal, the most accumulated cell collects 100 per cent of the domain over shared nodes and 6.6 per cent over shared edges. On a mesh whose faces are not all quadrilaterals no cell has a diagonal and the descent walks shared edges either way; on a Voronoi mesh the two graphs are the same one.
**Accepted**: true | false
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# observed_rasterization = "heads"` : How the mapped network is drawn on the mesh cells.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observed_rasterization`
**More**: 'crossing' keeps the cell holding each point where a line crosses the segment joining two edge-sharing cell centres. On a structured grid it reproduces WhiteboxTools VectorLinesToRaster, the paper's tool, and draws the map one cell wide like the simulated network, so a model that matches the map scores J = 0. 'touch' keeps every cell the line touches, corners included, and replays a session made before 2026-09; it thickens every diagonal step of the map and departs from the paper. 'heads' keeps only the free ends of the map whose largest drained area within heads_snap_radius does not exceed that of the other end of their reach, lands each on a nearby cell and draws the rest down the criterion's own descent: the field ditches and rectified reaches below a head stop counting as model error, and the drawn map reaches the outlet. Keep 'crossing' for a map that is not a tree: canals, braids, polders, karst.
**Values**:
- `"heads"`
- `"crossing"`
- `"touch"`
**Accepted**: "heads" | "crossing" | "touch"
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# heads_snap_radius = 100.0` : Under observed_rasterization = 'heads', the largest distance, a length (a bare number is in metres), between a mapped stream head and the centre of the cell it lands on. m only if observed_rasterization = "heads"
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.heads_snap_radius`
**More**: A head with no landing cell that close is lost, draws nothing and is counted in n_heads_lost. Read only under 'heads'.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "network" and observed_rasterization = "heads"

`# heads_min_drained_area_km2 = 0.02` : Under observed_rasterization = 'heads', the drained area in km2 a cell needs before a head may land on it, so a head next to its valley lands in the valley and not on the ridge cell beside it. km2 >= 0 only if observed_rasterization = "heads"
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.heads_min_drained_area_km2`
**More**: Read only under 'heads'.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: km2
**Only if**: support = "network" and observed_rasterization = "heads"

`# observed_position_accuracy = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Positional accuracy of the mapped network. m
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observed_position_accuracy`
**More**: It enters the automatic validity length only: the cell size h there is max(h_obs, this), because a map is not placed better when the mesh is refined. roptim stays Doptim / h_obs, the paper's Eq. 3. Unset is the literal reading of the paper.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# validity_length = "auto"` : Validity bound of Eq. 4, a length: the calibration is valid when Doptim <= this. m
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.validity_length`
**More**: 'auto' is 2 h, the paper's two cells, where h is h_obs, the cell size on the mapped network, raised to 'observed_position_accuracy' when one is declared. A length such as '150 m' is used as it is. The bound qualifies the result and never penalises the cost.
**Values**:
- `"auto"`
**Accepted**: "auto" or number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# on_roptim_violation = "warn"` : What a violation of Eq. 4 does: Doptim above 'validity_length'.
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.on_roptim_violation`
**More**: The bound is read once, on the trial the search returns, as the paper reads it at the optimum, and on each bound in the cost of the two-bound mode; every trial still records 'roptim', 'roptim_valid' and 'validity_length_m'. 'warn' logs it and returns the value, because a calibration is asked for a number. 'error' raises after the session is saved, so a staged calibration freezes nothing and runs no phase that depends on this one.
**Values**:
- `"warn"`
- `"error"`
**Accepted**: "warn" | "error"
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# max_unreachable_fraction = 0.05` : Bound on 'frac_unreachable_so' alone: the share of the simulated network whose descent never meets the mapped one, whose target does not move between trials. - [0, 1]
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.max_unreachable_fraction`
**More**: Beyond a few per cent the routing surface is not conditioned and D_so would be a fiction. The reciprocal share, 'frac_unreachable_os', is reported and deliberately left unbounded: its target is the simulated network, which the search itself retracts.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# alpha_warning_threshold = 0.9` : Below this value of 'alpha_obs_closure_catchment' the run warns that its distances carry a top-versus-map disagreement on top of the hydrogeology. alpha is the share of the downstream closure of the mapped network the network itself covers, measured on the MODEL TOP and on the catchment. ]0, 1] expert
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.alpha_warning_threshold`
**More**: It changes nothing that is computed: the criterion is scored the same way above and below it.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: ]0, 1] (refused outside)
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# clipping_warning_share = 0.1` : Share of the mapped stream cells lying outside the delineated catchment above which the whole-mesh alpha is reported as unreadable. [0, 1] expert
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.clipping_warning_share`
**More**: Those reaches trace through the buffer, where no cell is required to descend into the network, so they inflate the closure without adding to the numerator. Reported together with clipping_warning_gap, never alone.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Only if**: support = "network"

`# clipping_warning_gap = 0.05` : Minimum absolute gap between the whole-mesh and the catchment alpha for the clipping report to fire. [0, 1] expert
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.clipping_warning_gap`
**More**: A linework spilling out of the catchment over ground that routes the same way leaves the two ratios equal, and reporting it there would be noise on every ordinary project.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Only if**: support = "network"

## `[calibration.outputs.<name>.extent]`

The transient two-bound mode of a network output.

Only with `support = "network"`.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.extent]

`# maximal_flowing_steps = 1` : Timesteps a cell has to flow in a year to enter the maximal mask. - >= 1
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.maximal_flowing_steps`
**More**: At most the timestep count of the shortest complete year, checked on the run.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# minimal_dry_steps = 1` : Timesteps a cell may be dry in a year and stay in the minimal mask. - >= 0
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.minimal_dry_steps`
**More**: The year's timestep count minus this has to stay at least maximal_flowing_steps, checked on the run, so the minimal mask sits inside the maximal one.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# year_quorum = 0.5` : Share of the scored years in which a cell has to meet a bound's rule to enter it: ceil(year_quorum * n_years) years. - ]0, 1]
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.year_quorum`
**More**: Warned under three scored years, where one half is a union of two.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: ]0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# visible_flow = "1 L/s"` : Routed discharge a cell of the downstream closure has to carry to flow: a discharge with its unit ('1 L/s') or a share of the outlet discharge at the same timestep ('1%').
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.visible_flow`
**More**: '0 L/s' is the geometric definition. Never scaled with the cell size. No value is agreed: Zanetti et al. (2024) threshold a simulated discharge at 10 L/s, field zero-flow thresholds of 1 to 3 L/s are in use.
**Accepted**: string

### `[calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.weights]`

How the two bounds of a network output share one calibrated value.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.weights]

`# minimal = 0.5` : Weight of the minimal (permanent) bound. - [0, 1]
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.weights.minimal`
**More**: 1 with maximal = 0 calibrates on the permanent map alone, the practice of Abherve et al. (2025).
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# maximal = 0.5` : Weight of the maximal (complete) bound. - [0, 1]
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.extent.weights.maximal`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

# `[calibration.parameters]`

User declaration for one calibrated parameter.

- `calibration.parameters`{ name = table } · optional · 7 user keys

One table per name you choose: `[calibration.parameters.<name>]`. The name is free text.

[calibration.parameters.<name>]

`# bounds = ‹list of number›` : [low, high] physical bounds, in the unit the target declares. exactly 2 items
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`
**More**: Falls back to what the field annotates when the file omits it, which most fields deliberately leave unset because a range belongs to the site.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Valid range**: exactly 2 items (refused outside)

`# transform = "identity"` : Transform applied before sampling.
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.transform`
**More**: 'log' for strictly-positive quantities spanning orders of magnitude. Unset, the target's own field decides: a hydraulic conductivity declares 'log' where it is defined, so a file states this only to depart from it.
**Values**:
- `"identity"` : Searches the value as written.
- `"log"` : Searches the logarithm of the value: for a positive quantity that spans orders of magnitude.
- `"logit"` : Searches log(x / (1 - x)): for a share strictly between 0 and 1. Both bounds must lie inside (0, 1).
**Accepted**: "identity" | "log" | "logit"

`# prior = "uniform"` : Distribution, between the bounds, that starting points, random draws and Bayesian samplers take values from.
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.prior`
**Values**:
- `"uniform"` : Every value between the bounds is equally likely.
- `"log_uniform"` : Every decade between the bounds is equally likely.
- `"normal"` : A normal law centred between the bounds, with a standard deviation of a sixth of their span, cut at the bounds.
**Accepted**: "uniform" | "log_uniform" | "normal"

`# path = ‹string›` : Dotted TOML path of the value to move, such as 'flow.param.K.field.value'.
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.path`
**More**: Optional, and the way out rather than the way in: when omitted, the section name is resolved against the project catalogue ('hmp config targets' lists it). Write one to reach a value the catalogue does not carry, or to settle a name two targets answer to. A path written here wins without a lookup, and a parameter that writes one inherits nothing from the field it points at.
**Accepted**: string

`# target = ‹string›` : Readable alias for 'path'.
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.target`
**More**: When both are set, 'target' wins.
**Accepted**: string

`# mode = "replace"` : 'replace' writes the sampled value as-is; 'scale' multiplies the base TOML value at the target path by the sample.
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.mode`
**Values**:
- `"replace"`
- `"scale"`
**Accepted**: "replace" | "scale"

`# units = "m/s"` : Unit the bounds are written in, such as 'm/s'. example value
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.units`
**More**: The bounds are checked against the physical range of the target in this unit. Unset, the unit the target declares applies.
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"m/s"`

# `[calibration.persistence]`

Orthogonal switch governing every persistence sink.

- `calibration.persistence`[table] · optional · 4 user keys, 2 dev or expert

Connections found in the code (1)
- Same name `[simulation.results.persistence]` Simulation-run persistence switch passed to the result catalog (DuckDB rows, Zarr fields, Parquet tables).

[calibration.persistence]

`# save_catalog = true` : Persist DuckDB rows (simulations, parameters, metrics, calibration_iterations).
**Path**: `calibration.persistence.save_catalog`
**More**: When False, catalog writes are skipped.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# save_zarr = true` : Persist per-simulation field arrays (head, concentration, derived) into the Zarr store.
**Path**: `calibration.persistence.save_zarr`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# field_precision = "compact"` : Precision of the time-varying field arrays of fields.zarr: heads, per-cell budget terms, derived fields, concentrations.
**Path**: `calibration.persistence.field_precision`
**More**: 'compact' stores float32 with the mantissa rounded to nearest at 16 bits: each value moves by at most 2**-17 of itself (7.6e-6 relative, so at most 1 mm on a 130 m head and 7.6e-9 m3/s on a 1e-3 m3/s cell flux), and a daily run takes about a third of the disk. 'exact' keeps every value as computed, float64. Mesh geometry, topography, layer thickness, indices, coordinates and timestamps are never rounded.
**Values**:
- `"compact"`
- `"exact"`
**Accepted**: "compact" | "exact"

`# save_parquet = true` : Persist per-simulation tabular outputs (timeseries, budgets, mass_balance) as Parquet files.
**Path**: `calibration.persistence.save_parquet`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# compression = "zstd"` : Codec DECLARED for Zarr field arrays and Parquet tables. dev
**Path**: `calibration.persistence.compression`
**More**: The writers carry their own codec (zstd) and do not read this field, so changing it changes nothing today; it records the intent and is the field a writer would read once the choice is threaded through.
**Values**:
- `"none"`no explanation
- `"zstd"`no explanation
- `"lz4"`no explanation
- `"gzip"`no explanation
- `"snappy"`no explanation
**Accepted**: "none" | "zstd" | "lz4" | "gzip" | "snappy"

`# compression_level = 5` : Compression level DECLARED for those writers. [0, 22] dev
**Path**: `calibration.persistence.compression_level`
**More**: Same as the codec: core/io/parquet.py and core/io/geoparquet.py hold level 5 and do not read this field. The default says 5 rather than 3 so the declaration at least matches the bytes actually written.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: [0, 22] (refused outside)

# `[[calibration.phases]]`

One stage of a calibration that runs in several.

- `calibration.phases`[[array of tables]] · optional · 26 user keys

Repeat the table: one `[[calibration.phases]]` block per item.

Connections found in the code (1)
- The code says `calibration.parameters`: [calibration.parameters....] points at ..., which is a stage boundary and not a dimension a search may move: it says which model the stage runs, not a property of that model. Declare it in a phase's [calibration.phases.overrides] instead, which is how a two-stage method makes one stage steady and the next transient.

[[calibration.phases]]

`name = ‹string›` : Phase identifier, unique in the calibration and used in the session directory and in the report. required
**Path**: `calibration.phases.name`
**Accepted**: string

`parameters = ‹list of string›` : Names of the calibration parameters this phase may move. required at least 1 item
**Path**: `calibration.phases.parameters`
**More**: Every other parameter keeps the value it entered the phase with.
**Accepted**: list of string
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)

`# description = ""` : What this phase calibrates and against what, in one sentence.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.description`
**Accepted**: string

`# method = ‹string›` : Optimization method for this phase only.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.method`
**More**: Unset, it follows from what the phase scores: 'bisection' when the phase moves one parameter in log space and every one of its blocks is signed (distance_gap), since the answer is then a zero to find; 'scipy_nelder_mead' otherwise, a cost to minimise. hmp calibrate --list-phases prints the method and why. Write it to depart from that choice, and whenever method_options are given. Built-ins: 'grid' (regular sweep, sized by method_options.points_per_dim), 'lhs' (stratified Latin hypercube, sized by method_options.n_samples), 'random_search', 'bisection' (root of a signed criterion on one parameter, the stream-network stage), 'optuna' (TPE), 'cma_es', 'scipy_de', 'scipy_nelder_mead', 'gp_mapping', 'da_mh_gp'. An unknown name is refused when the optimizer is built, with the list installed here.
**Accepted**: string

`# max_iter = "auto"` : Maximum number of evaluations for this phase. > 0
**Path**: `calibration.phases.max_iter`
**More**: 'auto' lets an engine that counts its evaluations size it: the bisection budgets its worst case, and refuses before the first solve a number below its nominal count (see [calibration].max_iter). Any other engine gets 100 from 'auto', and no extension when it spends them before its stopping rule.
**Values**:
- `"auto"`
**Accepted**: integer or "auto"
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

`# tolerance = ‹number›` : How precisely the search has to pin a parameter before it stops, as a relative precision on the parameter itself: 0.01 asks for one per cent, 0.1 for ten. - > 0
**Path**: `calibration.phases.tolerance`
**More**: On a log-transformed parameter that is a ratio, which is how a conductivity is known in the first place, and it holds wherever the value sits; on any other transform there is no scale on the value to be relative to before the search has one, so it reads as a fraction of the declared interval. Each engine's own stopping option is written from it, so the same number survives a change of engine, and the engine's own option stays available for reproducing a published call verbatim. Unset, the engine's default applies. An engine that stops on its budget rather than on a precision refuses this rather than ignore it.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# batch_size = ‹integer›` : Suggestions drawn per ask, at least `parallel`. - >= 1
**Path**: `calibration.phases.batch_size`
**More**: Unset, the phase takes the `batch_size` of `[calibration]`.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# parallel = ‹integer›` : Trials of this phase solved side by side, each in its own folder. - >= 1
**Path**: `calibration.phases.parallel`
**More**: Unset, the phase takes the `parallel` of `[calibration]`, which also reaches the phases a protocol writes.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# outputs = []` : Names of the calibration outputs this phase scores on.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.outputs`
**More**: Empty means every declared output.
**Accepted**: list of string

`# objective_blocks = []` : Objective blocks this phase evaluates.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.objective_blocks`
**More**: Empty means every declared block. A list names them and keeps their declared weight. A table gives each named block the phase's own share instead, {block = share}, normalised to sum to one like a block's weight already is; every key must be a declared block, and every share must be positive.
**Accepted**: list of string or table { key = number }

`# variable = ‹string›` : Name of the simulated variable, or of a [calibration.outputs] entry, that objective scores when this phase uses no objective block.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.variable`
**More**: Unset, the variable of [calibration] applies.
**See**: calibration.outputs
**Accepted**: string

`# objective = ‹"rmse" | "nse" | "kge" | "mae" | "nse_log" | "nse_delta" | "nse_seasonal" | "reservoir" | "distance_gap" | "distance_mean"›` : Metric scoring this phase's single simulated series, when the phase does not use objective blocks.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.objective`
**More**: Same vocabulary as a block's 'metric'.
**Values**:
- `"rmse"` : Root-mean-square error, in the observed unit; penalizes large misfits most.
- `"nse"` : Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency against the observed mean; the standard choice for a level or discharge series.
- `"kge"` : Kling-Gupta efficiency; separates correlation, variability and bias when NSE alone is ambiguous.
- `"mae"` : Mean absolute error, in the observed unit; less sensitive to outliers than RMSE.
- `"nse_log"` : NSE on log-transformed series; weights low flows as heavily as peaks, good for recessions.
- `"nse_delta"` : NSE on the increments of the series rather than its level; a level is an integral and can hide flux errors that compensate, which only its increments show.
- `"nse_seasonal"` : NSE against the seasonal cycle rather than the overall mean; asks whether the model beats climatology.
- `"reservoir"` : Half nse_seasonal plus half nse_delta, built for an impounded level: a plain NSE there is beaten by the seasonal cycle, and the increments are what carry the flux errors.
- `"distance_gap"` : Balances the simulated stream network against the mapped one; zero marks the crossing.
- `"distance_mean"` : Mean spatial offset between simulated and mapped streams; a diagnostic, not a substitute for distance_gap.
**Accepted**: "rmse" | "nse" | "kge" | "mae" | "nse_log" | "nse_delta" | "nse_seasonal" | "reservoir" | "distance_gap" | "distance_mean"

`# observed_station_id = ‹string›` : Observed station whose cost the optimizer minimises.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.observed_station_id`
**More**: Every loaded gauge is already scored at its own mesh cell, on the discharge routed to that cell, and every cost is reported; naming one says which of them drives the search. Required when several stations are loaded, optional with one. Overrides the calibration-level value for this phase.
**Accepted**: string

`# method_options = {}` : Options of this phase's method, named as that method names them: sweep_points for 'bisection', points_per_dim for 'grid', sampler for 'optuna'.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.method_options`
**More**: They belong to one method, so a phase that gives them writes method beside them. A key the method does not take is refused when the file loads. hmp calibrate --check names the phase.
**Accepted**: table { key = any value }
**Was**: `calibration.phases.optimizer_kwargs`

`# regime = ‹"steady" | "transient"›` : Flow regime this phase runs, a property of the model and not of the search.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.regime`
**More**: 'steady' is one period over steady_window, by default the extent of [simulation.time]. 'transient' is the project's own time grid. Unset, the phase runs the model as the project and its overrides declare it.
**Values**:
- `"steady"` : One period over steady_window, so the recharge over it averages to its mean. A steady solve carries no storage.
- `"transient"` : The project's time grid, with only the regime restated.
**Accepted**: "steady" | "transient"

`# steady_window = ‹table { key = string }›` : Dates the steady period spans, as {start, end}, when regime = 'steady'. only if regime = "steady"
**Path**: `calibration.phases.steady_window`
**More**: Unset takes the whole [simulation.time] window.
**Accepted**: table { key = string }
**Only if**: regime = "steady"

`# overrides = {}` : Configuration values this phase runs with, as dotted paths into the project configuration.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.overrides`
**More**: A phase that gives regime may not write here a path regime writes: that would say the same thing twice.
**Accepted**: table { key = any value }

`# depends_on = ‹string›` : Name of the phase that must run first.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.depends_on`
**More**: The values it passes on enter this one fixed, except those this phase lists and moves again.
**Accepted**: string

`# freeze_on_success = true` : Pass the values this phase found to the phases after it.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.freeze_on_success`
**More**: A later phase holds them fixed, unless it lists the parameter: it then moves it again, starting from the passed value when its method accepts a start point. When two phases pass on the same parameter, the later one wins. Success means the phase converged, not that its validity indicator is good.
**Accepted**: true | false

## `[calibration.phases.scoring_window]`

Dates bounding the samples a metric is computed on.

Connections found in the code (1)
- Same name `[calibration.scoring_window]` Dates bounding the samples every metric is computed on: the way to leave a spin-up out, with start = the first date scored.

[calibration.phases.scoring_window]

`# start = ‹string›` : First date scored, ISO 8601.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.scoring_window.start`
**More**: Unset means from the first sample.
**Accepted**: string

`# end = ‹string›` : Last date scored, ISO 8601.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.scoring_window.end`
**More**: Unset means up to the last sample.
**Accepted**: string

## `[calibration.phases.uncertainty]`

How wide one phase says its answer is, key by key over `[calibration.uncertainty]`.

Connections found in the code (1)
- Same name `[calibration.uncertainty]` How wide the search reports its own answer to be. `mode` = `"relative"` | `"absolute"`

[calibration.phases.uncertainty]

`# method = ‹"cost_profile" | "multistart" | "linearized"›` : How this phase's interval is obtained: 'cost_profile', 'multistart' or 'linearized', read as in [calibration.uncertainty] method.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.uncertainty.method`
**See**: calibration.uncertainty
**Values**:
- `"cost_profile"` : Reads the range of sampled values whose cost stayed within tolerance of the best, off the trace of the search. No extra model run.
- `"multistart"` : Repeats the whole search restarts times from different starting points and reports the spread of the optima. It can see a second basin.
- `"linearized"` : Linearizes the model about the optimum: one extra run per parameter gives a first-order covariance, and with it which parameters trade off.
**Accepted**: "cost_profile" | "multistart" | "linearized"

`# restarts = ‹integer›` : How many times method='multistart' repeats this phase's search. - >= 2
**Path**: `calibration.phases.uncertainty.restarts`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 2 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# perturbation = ‹number›` : Relative step of method='linearized' for this phase, as a fraction of each calibrated value. - > 0
**Path**: `calibration.phases.uncertainty.perturbation`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# tolerance = ‹number›` : Width of this phase's interval: a fraction of the best cost when mode='relative', a number in the unit of the cost (metres for a network distance) when mode='absolute'. - or cost unit > 0
**Path**: `calibration.phases.uncertainty.tolerance`
**More**: Unset here and in [calibration.uncertainty], one mesh cell for a phase scored only by network distances, five per cent of the best cost otherwise.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: - or cost unit

`# mode = ‹"relative" | "absolute"›` : How this phase's tolerance is read.
**Path**: `calibration.phases.uncertainty.mode`
**More**: Unset here and in [calibration.uncertainty], 'absolute' for a phase scored only by network distances, 'relative' otherwise.
**Values**:
- `"relative"`
- `"absolute"`
**Accepted**: "relative" | "absolute"


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/protocol.html -->
# `[calibration.protocol]`

What a file may say about the protocol beyond naming it.

- `calibration.protocol`[table] · optional · 19 user keys

Connections found in the code (2)
- The code says `calibration.outputs`: [calibration.outputs] declares several network outputs (...); name the one the protocol is scored on in [calibration.protocol].network_output.
- The code says `simulation.time`: a steady phase averages the record over one steady period and reads its span from [simulation.time], which declares no start_datetime/end_datetime here. Write them, or name the span in the phase's steady_window ([calibration.protocol].steady_window when a protocol writes the phase).

[calibration.protocol]

`name = "matching_hydrographic_network"` : Name of the protocol to run. required example value
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.name`
**More**: 'matching_hydrographic_network' is the only one: a steady stage fits K on the stream network, then a transient stage fits the storage on a gauge.
**Values**:
- `"matching_hydrographic_network"`
**Accepted**: "matching_hydrographic_network"
**Example**: `"matching_hydrographic_network"`

`# version = ‹string›` : Recipe version this file was written against.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.version`
**More**: Unset runs the version this installation carries; pinned, a mismatch is refused rather than approximated, so a result that informed a decision stays replayable.
**Accepted**: string

`# conductivity = "K"` : Name of the calibration parameter stage one moves, as the file declares it under [calibration.parameters].
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.conductivity`
**See**: calibration.parameters
**Accepted**: string

`# storage = "Sy"` : Name of the calibration parameter stage two moves.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.storage`
**More**: Null runs the network stage alone, which is a method in its own right: it identifies the conductivity without any discharge record.
**Accepted**: string

`# network_output = ‹string›` : Name of the network output stage one is scored on.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.network_output`
**More**: Unset picks the single output declared with support='network'.
**Accepted**: string

`# steady_metric = "distance_gap"` : Criterion of stage one.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.steady_metric`
**More**: 'distance_gap' is the signed difference of Eq. 1, whose zero is the balance the paper solves for. 'distance_mean' is the mean offset: a diagnostic, and the estimator of the reference script, whose interior minimum sits nowhere in particular.
**Values**:
- `"distance_gap"`
- `"distance_mean"`
**Accepted**: "distance_gap" | "distance_mean"

`# steady_method = "bisection"` : Engine of stage one.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.steady_method`
**More**: The signed criterion crosses zero once over several decades, which is what a root search wants; any registered engine is accepted.
**Accepted**: string

`# steady_max_iter = "auto"` : Evaluation budget of stage one. > 0
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.steady_max_iter`
**More**: 'auto' lets an engine that counts its evaluations size it: the bisection budgets its worst case, S + 2E + ceil(log2(1 / t)) for a root found after its E bracket expansions, 23 on [1e-7, 1e-3] m/s with seven sweep points and one per cent; any other engine gets 100. A number below the bisection's nominal count, S + ceil(log2(s / t)) for a root inside the bounds (15 there), is refused before the first solve.
**Values**:
- `"auto"`
**Accepted**: integer or "auto"
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

`# steady_tolerance = ‹number›` : How precisely stage one has to pin the conductivity before it stops, as a relative precision on the conductivity: 0.01 is the paper's one per cent. - > 0
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.steady_tolerance`
**More**: Unset takes the engine's default, which for the bisection is that same one per cent.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# steady_method_options = {}` : Options of the stage-one method, named as that method names them: for the bisection, sweep_points, bracket_expand, rel_tol and signed_component.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.steady_method_options`
**More**: Which ones exist depends on steady_method; a key the method does not know is refused when the file loads. Used to reproduce a published call; a precision is said once, in steady_tolerance.
**Accepted**: table { key = any value }
**Was**: `calibration.protocol.steady_engine_options`

`# steady_window = ‹table { key = string }›` : Dates the steady stage averages, as {start, end}, both ISO 8601 and both required.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.steady_window`
**More**: A date that does not parse is refused when the file is read. Unset takes the whole [simulation.time] window.
**Accepted**: table { key = string }

`# transient_metric = "nse_log"` : Criterion of stage two.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.transient_metric`
**More**: The default weights recessions as heavily as peaks, which is where storage shows.
**Accepted**: string

`# transient_method = "scipy_nelder_mead"` : Search method of stage two, named as calibration.method names one, such as 'scipy_nelder_mead'.
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.transient_method`
**See**: calibration.method
**Accepted**: string

`# transient_max_iter = 120` : Evaluation budget of stage two. - >= 1
**Path**: `calibration.protocol.transient_max_iter`
**More**: The simplex cannot count what it needs, so it gets no extension: a stage two that spends this before its tolerance is reported as not converged, and a re-run with a larger budget replays the trials already solved from the cache.
**Accepted**: integer

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/uncertainty.html -->
# `[calibration.uncertainty]`

How wide the search says its own answer is.

- `calibration.uncertainty`[table] · optional · 5 user keys

Connections found in the code (1)
- Same name `[calibration.phases.uncertainty]` How wide this phase says its answer is, with the keys of [calibration.uncertainty]. `mode` = `"relative"` | `"absolute"`

[calibration.uncertainty]

`# method = "cost_profile"` : How the interval around each calibrated value is obtained.
**Path**: `calibration.uncertainty.method`
**More**: 'cost_profile' reads the range of sampled values whose cost stayed within 'tolerance' of the best, off the trace the search already produced, and costs no extra model run. 'multistart' runs the whole search 'restarts' times from 'restarts' different starting points and reports the spread of the optima it reaches, which is the only one of the two that can see a second basin; it costs that many times the runs. The calibrated value never moves either way: with 'multistart' it is the best of the restarts.
**Values**:
- `"cost_profile"` : Reads the range of sampled values whose cost stayed within tolerance of the best, off the trace of the search. No extra model run.
- `"multistart"` : Repeats the whole search restarts times from different starting points and reports the spread of the optima. It can see a second basin.
- `"linearized"` : Linearizes the model about the optimum: one extra run per parameter gives a first-order covariance, and with it which parameters trade off.
**Accepted**: "cost_profile" | "multistart" | "linearized"

`# restarts = ‹integer›` : How many times the search is repeated by method='multistart'. - >= 2
**Path**: `calibration.uncertainty.restarts`
**More**: Required by it and refused by any other method, because a number of restarts that nothing restarts is a statement about a run that did not happen. Each one is a full search: eight restarts of a hundred-evaluation phase is eight hundred model runs.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 2 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# perturbation = ‹number›` : Relative step the derivatives of method='linearized' are taken with, as a fraction of each calibrated value: 0.01 moves it by one per cent. - > 0
**Path**: `calibration.uncertainty.perturbation`
**More**: Required by it and refused by any other method. Too small and the difference is solver noise; too large and it is no longer a derivative. One per cent is the usual starting point, and the honest check is to move it and see whether the reported width moves with it. 'linearized' costs one model run per parameter, reads derivatives around the answer instead of searching again, and is the only declared method that also reports which parameters trade off against which. It is first-order: exact where the model is linear about the optimum, approximate in proportion to the curvature, and not a posterior.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# tolerance = ‹number›` : Width of the interval. - or cost unit > 0
**Path**: `calibration.uncertainty.tolerance`
**More**: A fraction of the best cost when mode='relative' (0.05 = five per cent), and a number in the unit of the cost when mode='absolute'. Unset, it follows what the search scores: one mesh cell, in metres, for a search scored only by network distances (distance_gap, distance_mean), because a stream cannot move by less than a cell; 0.05 otherwise, five per cent of the best cost. The cell is the median distance between the centres of neighbouring cells, measured by the network criterion on the mesh it scores. A phase may write its own, which wins.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: - or cost unit

`# mode = ‹"relative" | "absolute"›` : How 'tolerance' is read.
**Path**: `calibration.uncertainty.mode`
**More**: 'relative' is a fraction of the best cost and is the usual choice for an efficiency score. A criterion solved at zero, such as the stream-network gap, has no fraction of itself to take: state the width in the unit of the cost with 'absolute', for example 25 metres. Unset, 'absolute' for a search scored only by network distances and 'relative' otherwise. hmp calibrate --check refuses 'relative' on a search scored only by network distances.
**Values**:
- `"relative"`
- `"absolute"`
**Accepted**: "relative" | "absolute"
