<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/display.html -->
# `[display]`

Display behaviour resolved from the `[display]` TOML section.

- `display`[table] · optional · 10 user keys, 2 dev or expert
- Start a file: `hmp config template --modules display` (download it), then `hmp config check file.toml`. Minimal file
[display]

`# enabled = true` : Master switch.
**Path**: `display.enabled`
**More**: When False, no figure is rendered or saved.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# preset = "default"` : Named theme applied before rendering any figure.
**Path**: `display.preset`
**Values**:
- `"default"` : Uses a colorful sans-serif palette on a white background, for screen viewing.
- `"print"` : Uses a grayscale serif palette sized for black-and-white print output.
- `"dark"` : Uses a bright palette on a dark background, for dark-themed displays.
**Accepted**: "default" | "print" | "dark"

`# show = false` : Open an interactive window via `matplotlib.pyplot.show`.
**Path**: `display.show`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# save = true` : Write rendered figures to disk under `output_dir`.
**Path**: `display.save`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# output_dir = "figures"` : Name of the figures directory inside the run directory (<project>/runs/<run>/<output_dir>/).
**Path**: `display.output_dir`
**More**: Declared as a name, not a path, so it stays anchored to the run it describes.
**Accepted**: string

`# cmap = "viridis"` : Force ONE colormap onto every spatial figure.
**Path**: `display.cmap`
**More**: Writing it at all is the decision, not the value: each figure otherwise picks a scale suited to what it shows, reversed for a depth, diverging for a difference, discrete for an indicator, and this replaces all of them. Writing the default spelled out is therefore NOT a no-op, unlike everywhere else. Leave it out unless one scale for everything is what you want.
**Accepted**: string

`# figures = []` : Names of registered figures to auto-render at the end of `hmp run` (and consumed by `hmp viz gallery`).
**Path**: `display.figures`
**More**: Every name must exist in the figure registry; list them with `hmp viz list`. A figure whose requirements the run does not meet is skipped with an explicit reason. Empty list disables auto-rendering. Disable per-run via `hmp run --no-display` or for an entire Python Project via `Project(..., no_display=True)`.
**Accepted**: list of string

`# on_error = "warn"` : Behaviour when a figure that IS applicable fails while rendering.
**Path**: `display.on_error`
**More**: 'warn' logs and continues (default, keeps a long run alive); 'raise' propagates, which is what example and CI configs want so a broken figure cannot pass unnoticed.
**Values**:
- `"warn"`
- `"raise"`
**Accepted**: "warn" | "raise"

`# time = ‹string or integer›` : The instant every figure that draws one instant shows: a date ("2002-10-15"), "first" or "last".
**Path**: `display.time`
**More**: Each such figure draws the stress period that holds the date, so the same date names the same month on a monthly, a daily or a one-period steady run. A `time` in `[display.overrides.<figure>]` wins over it. Unset, each figure picks its own instant: the last period, or for the stream-network maps the state their calibration criterion read. A date outside a run skips the figure with the reason.
**Accepted**: string or integer

`# overrides = {}` : Per-figure options, keyed by figure name (e.g. `{'piezometric_map': {'cmap': 'cividis', 'vmin': 0}}`).
**Path**: `display.overrides`
**More**: A key the figure does not take is refused at load, with the list of the keys it takes. A figure that draws one instant takes `time`.
**Accepted**: table { key = dict }

`# backend = "auto"` : Matplotlib backend. dev
**Path**: `display.backend`
**More**: 'auto' selects Agg in headless mode and a GUI backend when `show` is enabled.
**Values**:
- `"agg"`no explanation
- `"qt5agg"`no explanation
- `"auto"`
**Accepted**: "agg" | "qt5agg" | "auto"

`# dpi = 150` : DPI used when saving raster figures. >= 1 dev
**Path**: `display.dpi`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)

# `[[export]]`

One export: what to write, when, in which format, where.

- `export`[[array of tables]] · optional · 8 user keys, 2 dev or expert
- Start a file: `hmp config template --modules export` (download it), then `hmp config check file.toml`. Minimal file

Repeat the table: one `[[export]]` block per item.

[[export]]

`variables = "head"` : What to export: a name, a list of names, or "all" for everything the run holds. required example value
**Path**: `export.variables`
**More**: One namespace covers the mesh fields (head, watertable_depth, seepage_mask...), the series (discharge, discharge_obs...), the vector layers (watershed, hydrographic_network_reference...), the raster layers (watershed_dem...) and the table budget; 'hmp export <run> --list' prints what a run holds. A name no run can hold is refused before the solve.
**Accepted**: string or list of string
**Example**: `"head"`, `["head", "discharge"]`, `"all"`

`# time = ‹string or integer or list of string or integer›` : The instants to write: a date "YYYY-MM-DD", "first", "last", or a list of them.
**Path**: `export.time`
**More**: A date takes the stress period that holds it. A format that holds one instant (GeoTIFF, Shapefile, GeoPackage, VTU) writes one file per date. Left out, the whole simulation is written. Cannot be given with period.
**Accepted**: string or integer or list of string or integer

`# period = ‹list of string›` : A window of the simulation, [start, end], two dates "YYYY-MM-DD".
**Path**: `export.period`
**More**: Every stress period it overlaps is written. Cannot be given with time.
**Accepted**: list of string

`# format = ‹"netcdf" | "geotiff" | "csv" | "geopackage" | "shapefile" | "vtu" | "package" | "stac" | "rocrate" | "prov"›` : The file format.
**Path**: `export.format`
**More**: Left out, each data takes its natural format, or the one the extension of 'file' names. 'package' writes the portable .hmp archive of the run; 'stac', 'rocrate' and 'prov' write its metadata. Those four describe the whole run and take variables = "all" only.
**Values**:
- `"netcdf"` : A NetCDF file (.nc): fields and series over time.
- `"geotiff"` : A GeoTIFF raster (.tif), one file per date.
- `"csv"` : A CSV table (.csv): series and tables.
- `"geopackage"` : A GeoPackage vector file (.gpkg), one file per date.
- `"shapefile"` : An ESRI Shapefile (.shp), one file per date.
- `"vtu"` : A VTK unstructured grid (.vtu) of the mesh, one file per date.
- `"package"` : The portable .hmp archive of the run.
- `"stac"` : The STAC metadata of the run.
- `"rocrate"` : The RO-Crate metadata of the run.
- `"prov"` : The PROV provenance record of the run.
**Accepted**: "netcdf" | "geotiff" | "csv" | "geopackage" | "shapefile" | "vtu" | "package" | "stac" | "rocrate" | "prov"

`# folder = ‹path›` : The folder the files are written to, with automatic names.
**Path**: `export.folder`
**More**: A relative folder is read from the project's share/ directory. Defaults to share/<run>/.
**Accepted**: path

`# file = ‹path›` : One exact file to write; its extension gives the format.
**Path**: `export.file`
**More**: A relative file is read from 'folder'. Only for a request that writes one file: several files need 'folder' and automatic names.
**Accepted**: path

`# crs = ‹string›` : Output CRS, e.g. 'EPSG:4326'.
**Path**: `export.crs`
**More**: Rasters and vector layers are reprojected from the model CRS. NetCDF, VTU and CSV do not reproject and refuse it. Left out, the model CRS is kept.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/bc.html -->
# `[flow.bc]`

Mapping of flow boundary-condition payloads parsed from `[flow.bc]`.

Supported TOML sections

- `[flow.bc.<id>]`, one block per boundary, keyed by what it is. Canonical ids: `drainage`, `ocean`, `stream`, `north_side`, `south_side`, `east_side`, `west_side`
- a boundary the registry describes entirely needs NO block: listing it in `flow.active_bc` is enough

Common keys

- `kind`: optional, the registry supplies it; write it only to depart from the default, and only within a family (`cauchy` and `robin` may be swapped, a prescribed head may not)
- `value`: optional on a drainage, where leaving it out derives the conductance from K; required for a prescribed head
- `application_domain`: optional, the registry supplies it, and a value contradicting it is refused

Allowed application_domain values: `top`, `north side`, `south side`, `east side`, `west side`.

Default units: `m` for dirichlet, `m2/s` for cauchy/robin.

Cauchy vs Robin: both map to the same MODFLOW `DRN` package; the distinction only matters for the Boussinesq solver, which uses two different surface-interaction closures (`cauchy` for the linear formulation `q = C(h - h_ref)`, `robin` for the regularized partition / complementarity variants selected by `flow.surface_interaction_model`).

- `flow.bc`{ name = table } · optional · 8 user keys, 9 dev or expert

One table per name you choose: `[flow.bc.<name>]`. The name is free text.

Connections found in the code (1)
- The code says `solver.drain_bed_thickness_m`: flow.bc.drainage.value sets one conductance per cell (%.3g m2/s), and the drained cells range from %.3g to %.3g m2: the drained flux per unit area, C / cell_area, varies %.1f-fold over the mesh, so the result depends on the mesh. Leave the value out to derive C = K * cell_area / solver.drain_bed_thickness_m, whose leakance K / b is the same on every cell.

`kind` selects the shape of this table. One tab per shape, the default first.

“dirichlet”
[flow.bc.<name>]

`kind = "dirichlet"` : An imposed head: the boundary cells keep the head the boundary gives. chosen shape
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.kind`
**More**: Unset, the boundary's id decides.
**Values**:
- `"dirichlet"` : An imposed head: the boundary cells keep the head the boundary gives.
- `"cauchy"` : A drain with the linear exchange q = C (h - h_ref); MODFLOW builds a DRN.
- `"robin"` : A drain with the regularized exchange Boussinesq selects; MODFLOW builds a DRN.
**Accepted**: "dirichlet" | "cauchy" | "robin"

`id = "drainage"` : Canonical name of the boundary, the same one flow.active_bc lists: 'drainage', 'ocean', 'stream', 'north_side', 'south_side', 'east_side' or 'west_side'. required example value
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.id`
**More**: It fixes where the boundary applies.
**See**: flow.active_bc
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"drainage"`

`# value = ‹number or list of number›` : Boundary-condition value, scalar or one value per stress period.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.value`
**More**: On a drainage boundary it is a conductance in m2/s, and it may be left out: the run then derives it from the conductivity, C = K * cell_area / solver.drain_bed_thickness_m, which keeps the drain proportional to K and makes K/R the quantity a network calibration searches. A zero or negative number selects that same derivation, so it does NOT mean a closed boundary; write a positive conductance to impose one.
**Accepted**: number or list of number

`# description = ""` : Free text about the boundary, kept with the configuration.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.description`
**More**: Unset, a text naming its kind and where it applies is written.
**Accepted**: string

`# application_domain = ‹string›` : Boundary-application domain.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.application_domain`
**More**: Supported values are: top, north side, south side, east side, west side.
**Accepted**: string

`# support_label = ‹string›` : Name of a labelled group of cells or edges of a Gmsh mesh.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.support_label`
**More**: The boundary then applies there instead of on the group its id selects. MODFLOW 6 and Boussinesq read it.
**Accepted**: string

`# units = ""` : Boundary-condition units. dev
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.units`
**Accepted**: string

`# data_value = false` : If True, boundary-condition values are sourced from data. dev
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.data_value`
**Accepted**: true | false

[flow.bc.<name>]

`kind = "cauchy"` : A drain with the linear exchange q = C (h - h_ref); MODFLOW builds a DRN. chosen shape
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.kind`
**More**: Unset, the boundary's id decides.
**Values**:
- `"dirichlet"` : An imposed head: the boundary cells keep the head the boundary gives.
- `"cauchy"` : A drain with the linear exchange q = C (h - h_ref); MODFLOW builds a DRN.
- `"robin"` : A drain with the regularized exchange Boussinesq selects; MODFLOW builds a DRN.
**Accepted**: "dirichlet" | "cauchy" | "robin"

**More**: The boundary then applies there instead of on the group its id selects. MODFLOW 6 and Boussinesq read it.
**Accepted**: string

`# units = ""` : Boundary-condition units. dev
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.units`
**Accepted**: string

`# data_value = false` : If True, boundary-condition values are sourced from data. dev
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.data_value`
**Accepted**: true | false

“robin”
[flow.bc.<name>]

`kind = "robin"` : A drain with the regularized exchange Boussinesq selects; MODFLOW builds a DRN. chosen shape
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.kind`
**More**: Unset, the boundary's id decides.
**Values**:
- `"dirichlet"` : An imposed head: the boundary cells keep the head the boundary gives.
- `"cauchy"` : A drain with the linear exchange q = C (h - h_ref); MODFLOW builds a DRN.
- `"robin"` : A drain with the regularized exchange Boussinesq selects; MODFLOW builds a DRN.
**Accepted**: "dirichlet" | "cauchy" | "robin"

`id = "drainage"` : Canonical name of the boundary, the same one flow.active_bc lists: 'drainage', 'ocean', 'stream', 'north_side', 'south_side', 'east_side' or 'west_side'. required example value
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.id`
**More**: It fixes where the boundary applies.
**See**: flow.active_bc
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"drainage"`

`# value = ‹number or list of number›` : Boundary-condition value, scalar or one value per stress period.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.value`
**More**: On a drainage boundary it is a conductance in m2/s, and it may be left out: the run then derives it from the conductivity, C = K * cell_area / solver.drain_bed_thickness_m, which keeps the drain proportional to K and makes K/R the quantity a network calibration searches. A zero or negative number selects that same derivation, so it does NOT mean a closed boundary; write a positive conductance to impose one.
**Accepted**: number or list of number

`# description = ""` : Free text about the boundary, kept with the configuration.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.description`
**More**: Unset, a text naming its kind and where it applies is written.
**Accepted**: string

`# application_domain = ‹string›` : Boundary-application domain.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.application_domain`
**More**: Supported values are: top, north side, south side, east side, west side.
**Accepted**: string

`# support_label = ‹string›` : Name of a labelled group of cells or edges of a Gmsh mesh.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.support_label`
**More**: The boundary then applies there instead of on the group its id selects. MODFLOW 6 and Boussinesq read it.
**Accepted**: string

`# units = ""` : Boundary-condition units. dev
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.units`
**Accepted**: string

`# data_value = false` : If True, boundary-condition values are sourced from data. dev
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.data_value`
**Accepted**: true | false

# `[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers]`

Typed payload for one MODFLOW 6 horizontal flow barrier (HFB).

- `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers`{ name = table } · optional · 12 user keys

One table per name you choose: `[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>]`. The name is free text.

[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>]

`# auto = false` : Auto-place the dam cutoff wall (lakes only): the trace is derived at bind time as the chord across the reservoir at its downstream neck (the footprint point nearest the catchment outlet), perpendicular to the outlet-flow direction.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.auto`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line / line_path; the mesh dam refinement then follows this auto axis too.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# line = ‹list of list of number›` : Inline barrier-trace vertices [(x, y), ...] in the project CRS.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.line`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line_path and auto.
**Accepted**: list of list of number

`# line_path = ‹path›` : Barrier-trace file: a vector polyline (gpkg / shp / GeoJSON) or a CSV of ordered x,y (or lon,lat) vertices.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.line_path`
**More**: A bare filename resolves against <workspace>/data/cutoff_wall/. Alternative to line and auto.
**Accepted**: path

`# depths = ‹list of number›` : Barrier depth [m] below the top (or below crest_elevation). at least 1 item
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.depths`
**More**: One value is uniform; several are interpolated per vertex along the trace. The HFB blocks every layer down to this depth. Mutually exclusive with base_elevation.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)

`# crest_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute TOP elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]; defaults to the cell top (the DEM). m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.crest_elevation`
**More**: Set it when the barrier crest sits below the DEM top. Not calibratable: raising the crest and lowering hydchr both shrink the flow section the wall lets through, so a search cannot tell the two apart. It is a built structure, not a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# base_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute BOTTOM elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]. m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.base_elevation`
**More**: When set, the HFB spans [base_elevation, crest_elevation or top] and blocks EVERY layer in that band. Use it to make a full-height dam impervious: the concrete body plus the grout curtain block all flow from the crest down to the curtain foot (e.g. base_elevation = 41 m), so nothing seeps across the dam above that. Mutually exclusive with depths. Not calibratable: a deeper foot and a lower hydchr produce the same reduction of under-dam flow, so putting both in a search is equifinality by construction, the same mechanism that makes the second stage of the stream-network protocol pin the specific yield on its bound. When the foot is genuinely unknown, run mode = "comparison", one elevation per run, which also yields a defensible sensitivity instead of a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for an override.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# hydchr = ‹number›` : HFB hydraulic characteristic [1/T] = K_barrier / thickness_barrier. >= 0 calibrable · log
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.hydchr`
**More**: A near-zero value (e.g. 1e-9 1/s) is a quasi-impermeable wall. Mutually exclusive with k + thickness.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: 1/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, prior log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# hydchr_unit = "1/s"` : Unit of hydchr (1/T): 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min. Converted to 1/s for MF6.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.hydchr_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# k = ‹number›` : Barrier hydraulic conductivity [L/T]; used with thickness when hydchr is unset. > 0 calibrable · log
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.k`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, prior log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# k_unit = "m/s"` : Unit of k (L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h, m/min. Converted to m/s.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.k_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# thickness = ‹number›` : Thickness of the barrier, in the unit thickness_unit names (metres by default). m > 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.thickness`
**More**: With k it gives hydchr = k / thickness when hydchr is unset.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# thickness_unit = "m"` : Unit of thickness (L): m, cm, mm, km.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.thickness_unit`
**More**: Converted to m.
**Accepted**: string

[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>]

`bedleak = 1e-06` : Lake-bed leakance [1/T] = K_bed / thickness_bed. required >= 0 calibrable · log example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bedleak`
**More**: Resistance of the lake-aquifer interface; the under-dam leakage calibration parameter. 0 means a perfectly sealed lakebed (no leakage).

**Unit**: m

`# bedleak_unit = "1/s"` : Unit of bedleak (leakance, 1/T): one of 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min (aliases like 1/d accepted).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bedleak_unit`
**More**: HydroModPy converts it to 1/s for MF6, so a 1/day leakance is not silently taken as 1/s.

`# steady_stage_hold = false` : Hold the lake stage at stageinit during the steady warm-up period(s) (LAK status CONSTANT) and re-activate it on the first transient period.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.steady_stage_hold`
**More**: Use for a managed reservoir whose observed initial level is far from the natural steady equilibrium: the aquifer equilibrates around the observed stage instead of overriding it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# occupied_layers = 1` : Number of top grid layers the lake occupies in each of its columns. - >= 1
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.occupied_layers`
**More**: 1 is a surface lake; a deeper reservoir embedded over several layers uses a higher count. Must leave at least one active layer below the lake for the VERTICAL leakage connection. A count of layers.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# fill_enclosed_cells = false` : Fill cells enclosed by the lake footprint (the polygon's interior rings / islands) so the lake is contiguous.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.fill_enclosed_cells`
**More**: Off by default: interior rings stay active aquifer (real islands). Enable to drop sub-grid islands and classification pockets that would otherwise be isolated non-lake cells inside the lake.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# surfdep = ‹number›` : LAK surface depression depth [L] that smooths the dry/wet (marnage) transition for Newton. >= 0 expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.surfdep`
**More**: Default (None) uses 0.1 m. Raise it (e.g. 0.5 to 1.0 m) to stabilise and speed up the active-littoral steady solve when many lakebed cells toggle at once; it slightly fuzzes the shoreline.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

## `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction]`

Opt-in carving of the real lake bed from bathymetry into the grid.

[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction]

`# reconcile_to_abacus = true` : Re-map the regridded bed so the cell area-vs-elevation distribution matches the abacus (the abacus is the storage source of truth).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.reconcile_to_abacus`
**More**: When False, the raw regridded bathymetry is carved as-is.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# dynamic_area = false` : Active-littoral (marnage) representation.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.dynamic_area`
**More**: When True the lake-bed cells stay ACTIVE with the carved bathymetric bed as their cell top and one VERTICAL LAK connection each; MODFLOW 6 then toggles recharge/ET per cell (IWETLAKE) so a cell exchanges with the lake when submerged and recharges as land when the shoreline recedes below its bed. When False the footprint is deactivated (fixed-area reservoir, the classic inactive-footprint carve).
**Accepted**: true | false

`# bank_seepage = true` : Also emit HORIZONTAL (bank) LAK connections on the active-littoral footprint, in addition to the VERTICAL (bed) ones, so the lake exchanges with the aquifer through both the bed AND the banks (the physical case). only if dynamic_area = true
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.bank_seepage`
**More**: Sealed at the cutoff wall (dam) when one is declared. Only applies with dynamic_area = true; a fixed-area lake always emits both. Set False to keep the bed-only marnage representation (the bedleak then absorbs the bank contribution).
**Accepted**: true | false
**Only if**: dynamic_area = true

`# min_thickness = 0.5` : Minimum layer thickness, in metres, held by EVERY layer when re-grading a lake column around the carved bed, so no degenerate (near-zero) cell breaks the solver. m > 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.min_thickness`
**More**: The bed is clamped into the band the column can hold at that floor, i.e. [base + n_active * min_thickness, top - n_occupied * min_thickness]; a column too thin for it raises at build time. Raising this value moves the carved bed away from the bathymetry (the build logs the shift).
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# min_pixels = 1` : Minimum bathymetry pixels whose centre must fall inside a cell for the zonal mean to be used; below it a bilinear sample at the cell centroid is taken instead. - >= 1
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.min_pixels`
**More**: A count of pixels.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# exposed_band_runoff = false` : Shed the overland runoff of the exposed lakebed band directly to the lake, sized per timestep from the simulated stage via the MODFLOW 6 BMI API (runoff_rate * exposed_area). expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.exposed_band_runoff`
**More**: Requires dynamic_area and forces the in-process API runner (serial only). When False the catchment runoff already covers the footprint area in a lumped, stage-static way.
**Accepted**: true | false

## `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall]`

Typed payload for one MODFLOW 6 horizontal flow barrier (HFB).

[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall]

`# auto = false` : Auto-place the dam cutoff wall (lakes only): the trace is derived at bind time as the chord across the reservoir at its downstream neck (the footprint point nearest the catchment outlet), perpendicular to the outlet-flow direction.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.auto`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line / line_path; the mesh dam refinement then follows this auto axis too.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# line = ‹list of list of number›` : Inline barrier-trace vertices [(x, y), ...] in the project CRS.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.line`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line_path and auto.
**Accepted**: list of list of number

`# line_path = ‹path›` : Barrier-trace file: a vector polyline (gpkg / shp / GeoJSON) or a CSV of ordered x,y (or lon,lat) vertices.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.line_path`
**More**: A bare filename resolves against <workspace>/data/cutoff_wall/. Alternative to line and auto.
**Accepted**: path

`# depths = ‹list of number›` : Barrier depth [m] below the top (or below crest_elevation). at least 1 item
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.depths`
**More**: One value is uniform; several are interpolated per vertex along the trace. The HFB blocks every layer down to this depth. Mutually exclusive with base_elevation.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)

`# crest_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute TOP elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]; defaults to the cell top (the DEM). m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.crest_elevation`
**More**: Set it when the barrier crest sits below the DEM top. Not calibratable: raising the crest and lowering hydchr both shrink the flow section the wall lets through, so a search cannot tell the two apart. It is a built structure, not a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# base_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute BOTTOM elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]. m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.base_elevation`
**More**: When set, the HFB spans [base_elevation, crest_elevation or top] and blocks EVERY layer in that band. Use it to make a full-height dam impervious: the concrete body plus the grout curtain block all flow from the crest down to the curtain foot (e.g. base_elevation = 41 m), so nothing seeps across the dam above that. Mutually exclusive with depths. Not calibratable: a deeper foot and a lower hydchr produce the same reduction of under-dam flow, so putting both in a search is equifinality by construction, the same mechanism that makes the second stage of the stream-network protocol pin the specific yield on its bound. When the foot is genuinely unknown, run mode = "comparison", one elevation per run, which also yields a defensible sensitivity instead of a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for an override.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# hydchr = ‹number›` : HFB hydraulic characteristic [1/T] = K_barrier / thickness_barrier. >= 0 calibrable · log
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.hydchr`
**More**: A near-zero value (e.g. 1e-9 1/s) is a quasi-impermeable wall. Mutually exclusive with k + thickness.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: 1/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, prior log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# hydchr_unit = "1/s"` : Unit of hydchr (1/T): 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min. Converted to 1/s for MF6.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.hydchr_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# k = ‹number›` : Barrier hydraulic conductivity [L/T]; used with thickness when hydchr is unset. > 0 calibrable · log
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.k`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, prior log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# k_unit = "m/s"` : Unit of k (L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h, m/min. Converted to m/s.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.k_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# thickness = ‹number›` : Thickness of the barrier, in the unit thickness_unit names (metres by default). m > 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.thickness`
**More**: With k it gives hydchr = k / thickness when hydchr is unset.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# thickness_unit = "m"` : Unit of thickness (L): m, cm, mm, km.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.thickness_unit`
**More**: Converted to m.
**Accepted**: string

# `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge]`

Typed payload for diffuse recharge over the model domain.

- `flow.sinks_sources.recharge`[table] · optional · 12 user keys, 5 dev or expert

Connections found in the code (2)
- Read when `flow.active_sinks_sources` lists `"recharge"`.
- Same name `[data.recharge]` Recharge configuration (drainage / soil infiltration time series). Read when `data.types` lists `"recharge"`. `source` = `"custom"` | `"sim2"` | `"synthetic"`

[flow.sinks_sources.recharge]

`# values = 0.0` : Recharge rate: one number, one number per stress period, a table {period: value}, or the series loaded from [data.recharge], in the unit that 'units' names (mm/day by default). mm/day calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.values`
**More**: A calibration reads its bounds in that unit too. The 'matching_hydrographic_network' protocol calibrates conductivity against the ratio K/R in its steady stage and requires this value held frozen there.
**See**: data.recharge
**Accepted**: any value
**Unit**: mm/day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# units = "mm/day"` : Unit of 'values' and of the recharge data source.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.units`
**More**: Data-manager outputs use mm/day by convention; set it when you write 'values' in another unit. The run converts the rate to m/s.
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"mm/day"`, `"m/day"`, `"m/s"`

`# heterogeneous_source = ‹any value›` : Optional raw data source for heterogeneous (2D per-cell) recharge. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.heterogeneous_source`
**More**: When set, the solver adapter discretizes FieldRecords onto the MODFLOW grid instead of using the scalar 'values' field. Expected: LoadResult with FieldRecords.
**Accepted**: any value

`# first_clim = "mean"` : Recharge rate of every steady stress period: every period of a steady run, and the first period of a transient run when flow.first_period_steady is true. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.first_clim`
**More**: 'mean' is the mean of the per-period rates, one weight per period; 'first' is the rate of period 0; a number is that rate, in the units of values. A transient period keeps its own rate. The same rule holds for one value per period and for one grid per period, under every solver. With negative_to_evt, the steady period takes the rule on the recharge part and on the deficit part, so its net rate is the one stated here.
**See**: flow.first_period_steady
**Accepted**: string or number
**Example**: `"mean"`, `"first"`, `2.0`

`# negative_to_evt = true` : When true, negative recharge values are routed to the solver EVT package and RCH receives the non-negative clipped recharge. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.negative_to_evt`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# spatial_mode = "auto"` : How to interpret spatial data: 'auto' (points->homogeneous, fields->heterogeneous), 'homogeneous' (force spatial averaging), 'heterogeneous' (force per-cell discretization, including point-to-grid interpolation when stations have coordinates). dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.spatial_mode`
**Values**:
- `"auto"`
- `"homogeneous"`
- `"heterogeneous"`
**Accepted**: "auto" | "homogeneous" | "heterogeneous"

`# interpolation_method = "nearest"` : Spatial interpolation method for gridded/point data onto the MODFLOW grid. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.interpolation_method`
**More**: Options: 'nearest', 'linear', 'idw'.
**Values**:
- `"nearest"`
- `"linear"`
- `"idw"`
**Accepted**: "nearest" | "linear" | "idw"

## `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil]`

Daily soil reservoir that turns precipitation and ETP into recharge.

[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil]

`ru = "150 mm"` : Available water capacity of the soil, in mm of water: what the roots can draw between field capacity and wilting point. required mm [0, 1000] calibrable example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.ru`
**More**: A bare number is in mm; "120 mm" and "12 cm" also read. Between 0 and 1000 mm. Required, since it belongs to the site. In doubt, start from 150 mm and compare the recharge the soil alone prints for 50 to 250 mm with the gauged discharge (hmp run <file> --until load_data). With [data.soil_capacity], it is the mean capacity of the SAFRAN cells, and the raster spreads it over classes inside each cell. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.ru].
**Accepted**: number or "<n> mm" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 1000] (refused outside)
**Unit**: mm
**Example**: `"150 mm"`
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# alpha = 0.6` : Share of ru above which the soil evaporates at the full rate kc x ETP. ]0, 1] calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.alpha`
**More**: Below alpha x ru, ETR falls linearly with the stored water. It is 1 - p of FAO-56 and LP of HBV. Above 0, at most 1. Kept fixed by default: the discharge alone hardly constrains it.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: ]0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, default bounds [0.3, 1.0]

`# kc = 1.0` : Crop coefficient applied to the loaded ETP: the soil evaporates at most kc x ETP a day. [0, 2] calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.kc`
**More**: 1.0 takes the ETP as loaded, a reference grass. Between 0 and 2. Kept fixed by default: kc and ru move the same annual volume.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 2] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, default bounds [0.7, 1.3]

`# impervious_fraction = 0.0` : Share of the area that is sealed (roofs, roads). [0, 1[ calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.impervious_fraction`
**More**: The rain that falls on it runs off at once, with no infiltration and no evaporation, and reaches the streams, the lakes and the gauged discharge. The soil reservoir covers the rest of the area. From 0 up to, not including, 1. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.impervious_fraction]; the range belongs to the site, so a file has to state it.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1[ (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# bypass_fraction = 0.0` : Share of the rain on the unsealed area that skips the soil through macropores and joins the recharge the same day, even when the soil is dry. [0, 1[ calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.bypass_fraction`
**More**: From 0 up to, not including, 1. Keep it at 0 while K and Sy are calibrated: a bypass can rebuild the summer recharge the soil reservoir removes.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1[ (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, default bounds [0.0, 0.3]

`# transit_time = 0.0` : Mean time the water leaving the soil takes to cross the unsaturated zone down to the water table, in days. day [0, 30] calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.transit_time`
**More**: A linear reservoir with this time constant delays and smooths the recharge; 0 sends it the same day. A bare number is in days; "5 days" also reads. At most 30 days: a longer delay would rebuild the slow groundwater memory MODFLOW computes itself.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 30] (refused outside)
**Unit**: day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, default bounds [0.0, 30.0]

`# curve_number = ‹number›` : SCS curve number (AMC II), dimensionless, of a HELP-style surface runoff (Schroeder et al. 1994): the unsealed share of the rain above a daily retention loses some to a fast runoff, more as the soil is wetter. [30, 98] calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.curve_number`
**More**: None turns the term off, bit for bit as before. Between 30 and 98; the calibrated value tends to exceed the tabulated one, since SAFRAN rain is smoothed over 8 km cells. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.curve_number].
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [30, 98] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# runoff_time = 1.0` : Time constant of the linear reservoir that routes the curve-number runoff to the outlet, in days. day [0, 10] calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.runoff_time`
**More**: Read only when curve_number is set. 0 sends it the same day; "2 days" also reads. Between 0 and 10 days: a longer delay would smooth away the fast surface peak the term exists for.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 10] (refused outside)
**Unit**: day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, default bounds [0.0, 10.0]

`# runoff_lag = 0.0` : Pure delay applied to the routed curve-number runoff, after runoff_time, before it reaches the gauged discharge: the travel time to the outlet plus any lag between the forcing's daily step and the gauge's. day [0, 5] calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.runoff_lag`
**More**: Read only when curve_number is set. 0 adds no delay, bit for bit as before; "0.75 days" also reads, interpolated linearly between the neighbouring whole-day shifts. Between 0 and 5 days: a longer shift belongs to runoff_time's reservoir, not to a fixed travel time. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.runoff_lag].
**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 5] (refused outside)
**Unit**: day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, prior uniform, default bounds [0.0, 5.0]

`# spinup = "first_year"` : State of the soil on the first day.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.spinup`
**More**: "first_year" repeats the first 365 days of the run until the storage at the end of that year moves by less than 0.1 mm, 20 times at most; the run must last one year at least. "none" starts from a full soil, the state of a soil in a wet winter.
**Values**:
- `"first_year"` : Repeat the first year until the soil storage settles.
- `"none"` : Start from a full soil and an empty transit store.
**Accepted**: "first_year" | "none"

# `[flow.sinks_sources.sfr]`

Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 SFR stream network.

- `flow.sinks_sources.sfr`{ name = table } · optional · 115 user keys, 36 dev or expert

One table per name you choose: `[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>]`. The name is free text.

Connections found in the code (1)
- The code says `geographic.enforce_lakes.capture_radius_m`: stream capture moved the watershed divide: the catchment went from %.2f to %.2f km2 (%+.0f %%) after re-delineating on the carved DEM. The carved channel most likely breached the divide and annexed a neighbouring basin, so the model no longer covers the requested catchment. Lower geographic.enforce_lakes.capture_radius_m, reduce buffer_m, or drop the capture pass and raise flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<

`# min_slope = 0.0001` : Smallest slope a reach bed may take, in metres of drop per metre (floor of rgrd). - > 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.min_slope`
**More**: It also sets the drop the bed profile solve keeps between neighbouring reaches.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# bed_incision = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Depth [L] of the streambed top rtp below the top of the reach's OWN aquifer cell. m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.bed_incision`
**More**: A bed never sits above the ground of its own cell, whether this is set or not. None (default) only lifts the lower bound: the bed may then sink to the cell bottom instead of stopping at max_bed_sag. When set, each reach is solved inside [cell_top - bed_incision - max_bed_sag, cell_top - bed_incision], monotone downstream, and the build refuses when that band is empty. rtp is delineated on the model top, so this anchors a bed that a coarse DEM cannot resolve; it is not a correction for the descent D, which never reaches the bed. Pick it against the water table, not against the channel: MODFLOW 6 switches a reach between connected and disconnected at rtp minus streambed_thickness (gwf-sfr.f90:3973-3985), so a bed sitting near the seasonal water-table depth toggles at every outer iteration.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# connected_to_aquifer = true` : If False every reach uses cellid 'none' (routing only, no streambed leakage).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.connected_to_aquifer`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# route_drainage = false` : Route the hillslope drainage (DRN) discharge into the stream network: every remaining DRN cell of the basin hands its outflow, through an MVR record (FACTOR 1.0), to the first reach or lake cell met on its descent D, a filled copy of the model top.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.route_drainage`
**More**: A cell whose descent leaves the model first keeps a plain DRN. This is the surface re-infiltration / runon convergence of drained water towards the river; without it only the reach cells' streambed captures baseflow and the rest of the catchment discharge is lost.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# storage = false` : Enable the channel-storage term (transient first period / SIMPLE only).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.storage`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# outflow_to_lake = ‹integer›` : Number of the lake the last reach feeds through a mover (SFR -> LAK), counted from 1 in the order the lakes are declared. - >= 1
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outflow_to_lake`
**More**: Unset, the network outflow leaves the model.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# outflow_mvrtype = "FACTOR"` : How much of the network outflow the mover passes to the lake, given outflow_value.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outflow_mvrtype`
**Values**:
- `"FACTOR"` : Moves the share outflow_value (from 0 to 1) of the outflow.
- `"UPTO"` : Moves the outflow, capped at outflow_value.
- `"EXCESS"` : Moves only the part of the outflow above outflow_value.
- `"THRESHOLD"` : Moves outflow_value once the outflow exceeds it, and nothing below it.
**Accepted**: "FACTOR" | "UPTO" | "EXCESS" | "THRESHOLD"

`# outflow_value = 1.0` : Amount of the transfer rule: a share from 0 to 1 for FACTOR, a flow rate in m3/s for UPTO, EXCESS and THRESHOLD. - or m3/s >= 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outflow_value`
**More**: Not calibratable: it is a coupling rule, not a hydraulic property of the reach or the lake, so letting a search move it would buy fit by reshaping how water is split between them rather than resolve streambed_k or the lake bathymetry, the actual unknowns. path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: - or m3/s

`# max_bed_sag = "5 m"` : Only read when bed_incision is set. m expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.max_bed_sag`
**More**: How far [L] below cell_top - bed_incision the monotone-downstream solve may sink a reach. It bounds the cumulative descent that a traced channel climbing over a rise forces on everything downstream of it. Widening it never refuses the build on its own: a reach that cannot hold the descent is warned about and pinned to the floor.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# lake_feeder_snap = "300 m"` : Max distance from a lake shoreline within which a dead-end reach is snapped to that lake via MVR (a real feeder the DEM fell short of). m expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.lake_feeder_snap`
**More**: Scale it to the catchment: too large teleports an unrelated reach into the lake.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# outlet_keepout = "1000 m"` : Min distance from the model outlet a terminal reach must keep to count as a lake feeder. m expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outlet_keepout`
**More**: A terminal closer than this is the below-dam discharge reach (the lake feeds it and it leaves the model), so it is not routed into the lake.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# rectify_on_mesh = false` : Re-derive the delineated reach cells as a clean single-flow-direction (SFD) channel on the DISV mesh. expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.rectify_on_mesh`
**More**: From every delineated cell the descent D, a filled copy of the model top, is traced one neighbour at a time until it reaches a lake, the outlet of D, or an already-traced cell. The union of those paths is the channel: one cell wide (a single downstream per cell, so no braiding), continuous on the descent graph (shared faces, or shared nodes on a quad mesh), following the thalweg of D (so the surface flow follows the reach), and always reaching a real sink (no inland dead-end that leaks its flow out). The streambed top is read on the model top, never on D. D is a copy and never returns to the solver.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# rectify_stub_max_upstream = 2` : When rectify_on_mesh is set, demote a low-order parallel stub to hillslope drainage (DRN -> SFR) to thin braided bands: a reach cell with at most this many reach cells upstream of it that runs beside a reach carrying strictly more (the true channel) is dropped from SFR, keeping a one-thread channel; its water still reaches the network as routed drainage. expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.rectify_stub_max_upstream`
**More**: 0 demotes only headwater leaves, a negative value keeps every traced cell. Default 2 removes stubs up to ~3 cells.
**Accepted**: integer

`# rectify_min_component_cells = 2` : When rectify_on_mesh is set, drop a whole reach component smaller than this many cells (a lone one-cell stream that just touches a lake or the outlet is hillslope drainage, not a channel, and reads as a spurious SFR -> lake entry). expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.rectify_min_component_cells`
**More**: Its water still reaches the network as routed DRN. Default 2 drops single-cell components; 1 keeps every component.
**Accepted**: integer

## `[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions]]`

An SFR-to-SFR diversion: a controlled split from one reach to another.

Repeat the table: one `[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions]]` block per item.

[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions]]

`reach = 12` : Number of the reach the diversion leaves from, counted from 1. required - >= 1 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions.reach`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `12`

`to_reach = 13` : Number of the reach that receives the diversion, counted from 1. required - >= 1 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions.to_reach`
**More**: It must be a downstream connection of reach.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `13`

`# cprior = "FRACTION"` : How much of the flow leaving reach the diversion takes, given divflow.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions.cprior`
**Values**:
- `"FRACTION"` : Takes the share divflow (from 0 to 1) of the flow.
- `"EXCESS"` : Takes only the part of the flow above divflow.
- `"THRESHOLD"` : Takes divflow once the flow reaches it, and nothing below it.
- `"UPTO"` : Takes the flow, capped at divflow.
**Accepted**: "FRACTION" | "EXCESS" | "THRESHOLD" | "UPTO"

`length = "250 m"` : Length of the reach along the channel, in metres (rlen of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required m example value

**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"250 m"`

`width = "3 m"` : Width of the channel of the reach, in metres (rwid of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required m example value

**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"3 m"`

`slope = 0.002` : Slope of the reach bed, in metres of drop per metre of length (rgrd of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required - > 0 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.slope`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `0.002`

`top = "42 m"` : Elevation of the streambed top of the reach, in metres (rtp of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.top`

`# upstream = []` : 1-based ids of reaches whose downstream end feeds this reach.

`# downstream = []` : 1-based ids of reaches this reach feeds.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.downstream`
**Accepted**: list of integer

`# ustrf = 1.0` : Share of the flow of the upstream reach that this reach receives, from 0 to 1. - >= 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.ustrf`
**More**: The shares of reaches fed by the same reach must sum to 1.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

### `[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.cell]`

DISV cell the reach exchanges with (streambed leakage).

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/geographic.html -->
# `[geographic]`

Geographic configuration for watershed delineation.

- `geographic`[table] · required in every file · 51 user keys, 13 dev or expert
- Start a file: `hmp config template --modules geographic` (download it), then `hmp config check file.toml`. Minimal file
[geographic]

`# source_mode = "standard"` : Where the model domain comes from.
**Path**: `geographic.source_mode`
**More**: 'standard' delineates it from a DEM, an outlet or a polygon ([geographic.catchment]). 'synthetic' builds one analytical support from [geographic.synthetic].
**Values**:
- `"standard"`
- `"synthetic"`
**Accepted**: "standard" | "synthetic"

`# crs_project = ‹string›` : Target projected CRS for all outputs (e.g. 'EPSG:2154').
**Path**: `geographic.crs_project`
**More**: If not set, derived from the input DEM.
**Accepted**: string

`# dem_correc_type = "fill"` : How the DEM is conditioned before the catchment is delineated.
**Path**: `geographic.dem_correc_type`
**More**: 'fill' (default) only raises cells: each closed depression is raised to its spill level, then a small gradient on the flats lets every cell drain. 'breach' mostly lowers cells: it carves a path through the barrier that closes a depression, after raising single-cell pits to their lowest neighbour, with no limit on length or depth and no fill afterwards (least-cost breaching, Lindsay 2016); it changes far fewer cells than 'fill' and can dig deep. 'capped_breach' lowers and raises: it breaches only within the limits of [geographic.capped_breach] (a maximum cumulative lowering and a maximum length, in metres), then fills every depression the limits refused (the hybrid of Lindsay 2016). The depth limit is a sum over the cells of a path, so it does not give the same landscape at every grid resolution. 'fill' is the default because it is the tool of the paper behind the network criterion (FillDepressions, Abherve et al. 2023), and the criterion itself fills the model top on the mesh by a priority flood: one conditioning rule from the DEM to the score.
**Values**:
- `"breach"`
- `"fill"`
- `"capped_breach"`
**Accepted**: "breach" | "fill" | "capped_breach"

`# terrain_engine = ‹string›` : Flow-routing engine that conditions the DEM and delineates the catchment.
**Path**: `geographic.terrain_engine`
**More**: Unset uses the engine this build defaults to. A string and not an enumeration: the values that resolve depend on what is installed beside HydroModPy, which is how a third-party engine is named without a patch.
**Accepted**: string

`# domain_extent = "box"` : Selects the DEM surface used for the domain.
**Path**: `geographic.domain_extent`
**More**: 'box' (default) keeps the full buffered rectangular support. 'watershed' / 'watershed_buff' select the catchment (optionally with a buffer ring) surface. Note: the MODFLOW 6 mesh still covers the buffered box (the buffer stays active for inter-basin exchange); out-of-watershed drainage is kept out of the catchment discharge by the DRN watershed-routing, not by an idomain mask. Experimental.
**Values**:
- `"box"`
- `"watershed_buff"`
- `"watershed"`
**Accepted**: "box" | "watershed_buff" | "watershed"

`# reuse_existing_outputs = false` : If true, reuse previously generated geographic artifacts when the cached fingerprint matches the current DEM, outlet/polygon and geographic settings.
**Path**: `geographic.reuse_existing_outputs`
**More**: This is useful for profiling repeated simulation runs in the same workspace.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# reg_fold = ‹path›` : Folder with pre-computed regional flow rasters. dev
**Path**: `geographic.reg_fold`
**More**: When set, rasters are loaded instead of recomputed.
**Accepted**: path

`# write_intermediates = false` : Keep intermediate rasters and shapefiles on disk after geographic preprocessing. dev
**Path**: `geographic.write_intermediates`
**More**: When false (default), .hmp/scratch/<run>/_preprocessing/ is removed after ingestion into the run field store.
**Accepted**: true | false

## `[geographic.catchment]`

How the model domain is defined.

Connections found in the code (3)
- The code says `data.dem.sources`: geographic.catchment.catch_def is required when [[data.dem.sources]] is the DEM source. Add a [geographic.catchment] table with catch_def.
- The code says `data.dem`: [data.dem] rge-alti at resolution_m = 1 cannot bootstrap the project: the ... km box around the outlet would need billions of pixels. The 1 m grid is for an explicit extent (the fetch_rge_alti helper or `hmp data get`). Use resolution_m = 5, or give [geographic].dem_init_path a file.
- The code says `geographic.crossings.path`: A crossings API source can only feed the notch when geographic.catchment.x_outlet / y_outlet are declared, since the watershed that would otherwise give the download box is not delineated yet. Declare geographic.crossings.path explicitly instead.

`catch_def` selects the shape of this table. One tab per shape, the default first.

“dem”
[geographic.catchment]

`catch_def = "dem"` : Model domain defined directly from a DEM raster. chosen shape
**Path**: `geographic.catchment.catch_def`
**Values**:
- `"dem"` : Model domain defined directly from a DEM raster.
- `"txt"` : Model domain defined from an XYZ text grid plus a cell size.
- `"from_outlet_coord"` : Watershed delineated from an outlet coordinate.
- `"from_polyg_shp"` : Watershed delineated from a polygon shapefile.
**Accepted**: "dem" | "txt" | "from_outlet_coord" | "from_polyg_shp"

`dem_init_path = "dem.tif"` : Path to the DEM raster that is the model domain. required example value
**Path**: `geographic.catchment.dem_init_path`
**More**: A relative path is read from the folder of the TOML file; a bare file name is also looked up in the dem folder of the workspace data. May be left out only when [[data.dem.sources]] declares the DEM.
**Accepted**: path
**Example**: `"dem.tif"`

`# dem_resolution = "75 m"` : Cell size the DEM is aggregated to before anything is delineated, a length ('75 m', a bare number in metres). m example value
**Path**: `geographic.catchment.dem_resolution`
**More**: The routing surface, the catchment, the mesh and the model top all take it. Unset keeps the pixel of the DEM file, which is what the mesh follows otherwise: 25 m for a BD ALTI download. Aggregation only: each coarse cell is the mean of the fine pixels it covers, nodata left out, on a grid aligned on the upper-left corner of the DEM; a value finer than the DEM's own pixel is refused when the run starts. The DEM file is not changed, the aggregated copy lives in the geographic products of the run.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"75 m"`

## `[geographic.capped_breach]`

Limits of the `capped_breach` DEM conditioning, in metres.

[geographic.capped_breach]

`# max_depth = 0.5` : Largest cumulative lowering, in metres, of one breach path (the 'max_cost' of Whitebox): the lowering summed over the cells of the path, not the depth of one cell. m > 0
**Path**: `geographic.capped_breach.max_depth`
**More**: Measured on the Flume at 25 m with 8-cell paths, the realised maximum lowering of a cell follows it within 0.01 m. On a finer grid a thick embankment spreads the cost over more cells, so it is filled instead of dug: the same value does not give the same landscape at every resolution. A depression whose cheapest breach costs more is filled. Paths overlap, so the lowering of a cell can exceed it (Nancon 75 m: 0.56 m for 0.5 m). The realised depth is measured after the call, logged, and warned about when it exceeds this value. Accepts inline units (e.g. 0.5, '0.5 m').
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# max_distance = 200.0` : Longest breach path, in metres. m > 0
**Path**: `geographic.capped_breach.max_distance`
**More**: Translated to the DEM grid as ceil(max_distance / cell size) cells, at least one, and counted in cells along the path: a diagonal step counts one cell, so a diagonal breach can be up to 1.41 times longer than max_distance. A depression with no way out within this length is filled. Accepts inline units (e.g. 200, '0.2 km').
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m
