# The mesh

The solver does not see the DEM. It sees cells, and one top elevation, one bottom elevation and one centre for each of them. This page gives the rules that turn the DEM into those cells: how the cells are laid out, how the top of a cell is read from the DEM, how many cells a given size costs, and which checks the code runs on the result.

Note

Scope. The cell layout below is the one of MODFLOW 6, which reads every grid as a DISV grid. MODFLOW-NWT builds a structured grid only and ignores a runtime mesh. Boussinesq uses the triangles of the Gmsh mesh as its cells, so the Voronoi dual of 3. The Voronoi dual does not apply to it, and it ignores the top sampling of 5. The top of a cell. What the solver does with the cells is on The solvers of the aquifer. The extra terms XT3D adds on a non-orthogonal mesh are on XT3D on irregular meshes. To set up a mesh, see [mesh_catchment].

## The chain in one list

The code builds the cells in this order. Each step is a section below.

1. Two surfaces: the top from the DEM \(Z\) and the bottom from the depth model.
1. A planar support, from one of two sources: the pixels of the DEM (a structured grid, 1. A structured grid), or a Gmsh triangulation built at run time (2. A runtime mesh from Gmsh), which MODFLOW 6 turns into its Voronoi dual by default (3. The Voronoi dual).
1. One top elevation per cell (5. The top of a cell) and one bottom elevation per cell.
1. A check of the thickness (8. The checks the code applies), then the layers (6. Thickness and layers).
1. The export to MODFLOW 6 as a DISV grid. The cells that have no valid top or bottom are written inactive.

Example 04 uses the first source: its files declare neither a `[mesh_catchment]` section nor a `[modflow6.sgrid]` section, so every cell is one DEM pixel. The header of `step1_minimal.toml` counts 21406 cells of 75 m for this domain.

## 1. A structured grid

With `modflow6.sgrid.planar.mode` at its default, the cells are the pixels of the top raster, with the same size and the same extent. A cell \((i,j)\) takes the value of pixel \((i,j)\), with no interpolation:

\[ z_{\mathrm{top},ij} = Z_{ij}, \qquad N_S = n_{\mathrm{row}}\, n_{\mathrm{col}}, \qquad a_{ij} = \Delta_x \Delta_y . \]

A pixel that is nodata makes the cell inactive. The cell still exists in the grid, so \(N_S\) counts the active and the inactive cells.

With `modflow6.sgrid.planar.mode` set to resample the grid to a shape, top and bottom are resampled to \(n_{\mathrm{row}} \times n_{\mathrm{col}}\) cells over the same extent, with the rule of `modflow6.sgrid.planar.resampling` (`project_surfaces_to_planar_grid`). If a cell then covers at least two DEM pixels, the top of the cell is the zonal statistic of 5. The top of a cell instead of the resampled value (`_cells_cover_pixels`, `_zonal_structured_top`). A grid whose cells are the pixels is never touched by the zonal top.

MODFLOW 6 reads this grid as a DISV grid. MODFLOW-NWT reads it as a DIS grid.

## 2. A runtime mesh from Gmsh

A `[mesh_catchment]` section makes the run build a triangulation of \(\Omega\) with Gmsh before the solver is prepared (`run_mesh_phase`). The project refuses a file that has both a `[mesh_catchment]` and a `[mesh_input]` section (`Embedded [mesh_catchment] and external [mesh_input] are mutually`): they are two sources for the same mesh. A mesh that already exists is declared with `mesh_input.mesh_path` or `mesh_input.bundle_dir` instead, and goes through the steps below like a mesh the run built.

The triangle sizes come from a size field, in the sense of the Gmsh manual ([Geuzaine and Remacle, 2009], reference manual): a Distance field to some curves, a Threshold field on it, and the minimum of all fields. Around the interface curves (rivers, geology interfaces, the catchment boundary), when `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.refine_interfaces` is on, the code sets the lower distance of the Threshold to zero. With \(\xi\) the distance to the nearest interface, the wanted size is linear between the two limits:

(21)\[ \ell_0(\xi) = \ell_s + (\ell_g - \ell_s)\,\min\!\left(1, \frac{\xi}{\xi_s}\right). \]

When the refinement policy is on, there is one such field per family of curves, with its own \(\ell_s\) and \(\xi_s\) (`apply_family_refinement_fields`). The size actually used is bounded by Gmsh options the code sets from the three keys of the section (`apply_mesh_options`):

(22)\[\begin{split} \ell(\mathbf{x}) = \min\!\bigl(\ell_{\max}',\ \max(\ell_{\min}',\ \ell_0(\mathbf{x}))\bigr), \qquad \ell_{\min}' = \begin{cases}\ell_{\min} & \text{if set,}\\ \ell_g & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases} \qquad \ell_{\max}' = \begin{cases}\ell_{\max} & \text{if set,}\\ \ell_g & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases} \end{split}\]

The fields of the lakes, of the refinement zones and of the coarsening outside the catchment join the interface fields (`set_background_mesh_from_fields`). The upper bound is raised to the largest size of such a regional field when the section declares one (`compute_effective_max_size`). The lower bound has a consequence that the keys do not announce: with no `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.min_size`, \(\ell_{\min}' = \ell_g\), and every size below \(\ell_g\) is raised back to \(\ell_g\). An `interface_size\` below the background size then changes nothing (Limits).

Fig. 29 The size of (21) (dotted) and the size Gmsh keeps under the bounds that `apply_mesh_options` sets, for \(\ell_s = 20\) m, \(\ell_g = 100\) m and \(\xi_s = 300\) m. Look at the shaded band: without `min_size` the refinement near the interface is lost.

The 2D algorithm is the one named by `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.algorithm`. The code knows four names and maps them to the Gmsh codes. Gmsh does not give the same triangulation twice for the same input. `mesh_catchment.cache` keeps the first one and reuses it while the inputs that shape the mesh are unchanged.

## 3. The Voronoi dual

MODFLOW 6 does not take the triangles as cells by default. With `modflow6.sgrid.grid_dual` at its default, the code takes the vertices of the triangulation as seeds \(\mathbf{s}_i\) and builds the Voronoi (PEBI) cell of each seed, that is the set of points closer to it than to any other seed, clipped to the outline \(\Omega\) of the triangulation.

The cell centre written to the DISV file is the seed itself. Three rules complete the construction:

- A seed whose cell falls entirely outside \(\Omega\) is dropped.
- When the clip splits a cell, the piece that contains the seed is kept.
- If no piece contains the seed, the largest piece is kept and its representative point becomes the centre.

The outline \(\Omega\) is rebuilt from the edges that belong to exactly one triangle. The coordinates of the vertices are rounded to 1 mm so that the corners shared by two cells are one vertex, which assumes a projected CRS in metres.

Three consequences follow.

The number of cells. The dual has one cell per seed, so \(N_V = n_v\), the number of vertices. By Euler’s formula a triangulation of a region without holes has \(N_T = 2 n_v - n_b - 2\) triangles, \(n_b\) being the vertices on its outline, so \(N_V \approx N_T / 2\) when \(n_b\) is small against \(n_v\).

The faces. The face between two cells is the perpendicular bisector of the segment between their seeds. The faces are not the edges of the triangulation. A river that was a chain of triangle edges runs through the middle of a chain of Voronoi cells: it is no longer the boundary of any cell.

The orthogonality. The line between the two centres is perpendicular to the face, so \(\varphi_{nm} = 0\) on every connection whose two cells kept their seed as centre. 4. Flow between two cells, and the angle says why this matters. As a check, 36 seeds on a \(6 \times 6\) lattice (the 16 inner ones moved at random, \(n_b = 20\)) give 50 triangles, and `voronoi_dual_of_mesh` returns 36 cells with \(0^\circ\) on every connection.

The features. Wells and boundaries are placed on the dual cells, not on the triangles. A well goes in the cell that holds its point. A side boundary takes the cells whose seed lies on that side, so the head is held on the boundary and not in a clipped inner cell that only touches it; a corner cell belongs to both sides. A side with no seed on it falls back to the cells with a face on it, with a warning. The stream boundary takes the cells the river runs through.

With `modflow6.sgrid.grid_dual` set to `"triangle"`, the triangles are the cells and the centre of a cell is the mean of its three vertices.

## 4. Flow between two cells, and the angle

MODFLOW 6 writes the flow between two cells with the two-point finite-difference term \(G_{nm}\,(h_m - h_n)\) of (17) [Harbaugh, 2005, Langevin et al., 2017]. It is exact only when the conductivity is isotropic in the plane and the line between the centres is perpendicular to the shared face. HydroModPy measures the departure from that condition on every connection, as an angle. With \(\mathbf{d}_{nm}\) the vector between the two centres and \(\mathbf{n}_{nm}\) the unit normal of the shared edge:

(23)\[ \varphi_{nm} = \arccos\!\left(\frac{\lvert \mathbf{d}_{nm} \cdot \mathbf{n}_{nm} \rvert} {\lVert \mathbf{d}_{nm} \rVert}\right). \]

Only an edge shared by exactly two cells counts as a connection. The summary the code keeps is the median, the 95th and 99th percentiles, the maximum and the share of connections above 30 degrees. What the angle does to the flux, and when the code turns on the XT3D option that corrects it, is on XT3D on irregular meshes.

Two triangles. Cut a \(2 \times 1\) rectangle along its diagonal. The shared edge goes from \((2,0)\) to \((0,1)\), with a normal along \((1,2)\). The centres are the vertex means, \((2/3, 1/3)\) and \((4/3, 2/3)\), so \(\mathbf{d} = (2/3, 1/3)\) and

\[ \cos\varphi = \frac{\lvert (2,1)\cdot(1,2) \rvert}{\sqrt5\,\sqrt5} = \frac{4}{5}, \qquad \varphi \approx 36.9^\circ . \]

The same corners, as seeds. The four corners of the rectangle, taken as seeds, give four cells of \(1 \times 0.5\) with four connections, all at \(0^\circ\). Both results were checked with `connection_nonorthogonality_deg`, and the four cells with `voronoi_planar_mesh`.

Fig. 31 Left: the two triangles above, with \(\mathbf{d}_{nm}\) between the centres and \(\mathbf{n}_{nm}\) normal to the shared face; the angle comes from `connection_nonorthogonality_deg`. Right: the 36 seeds of the check of 3. The Voronoi dual, their 50 triangles (dotted) and the 36 cells of `voronoi_dual_of_mesh` (blue). Look at the title: the triangles reach 35°, every connection of the dual is at 0°.

## 5. The top of a cell

The top of a cell is one number, read from the DEM \(Z\). Two rules exist, set by `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.mode`. The bottom is always read by the first rule.

### Centroid

The DEM is sampled at the centre of the cell with a bilinear interpolation between the four pixel centres around it. The weights \(w_k\) are the bilinear ones, and a nodata pixel gets a weight of zero before the sum is normalised:

\[ \tilde z_c = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{4} w_k\, Z_k\, \mathbf{1}[Z_k \text{ valid}]} {\sum_{k=1}^{4} w_k\, \mathbf{1}[Z_k \text{ valid}]} . \]

The result is undefined, and the cell inactive, when the centre is outside the raster or the four pixels are nodata. On an incised channel the centre of a cell often falls on a bank, not on the thalweg, and the cell is then too high.

### Zonal

The zonal rule reduces every pixel whose centre falls in the cell. A pixel belongs to the cell that contains its centre: for a mesh, the code burns each cell polygon into a raster of the DEM; for a structured grid, it computes the row and column by arithmetic. A pixel is channel when the stream raster of the delineation says so, with the mask widened by `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_buffer_px` pixels. The raster is read only when `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_source` asks for it. Without a stream raster, every pixel is a hillslope pixel.

With \(\operatorname{stat}\) the statistic named by `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_stat` on the channel pixels, and by `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.hillslope_stat` on the others (`mean`, `median`, `min`, `max`, and the 10th and 25th percentiles):

(24)\[\begin{split} z_{\mathrm{top},c} = \begin{cases} \operatorname{stat}_{\mathrm{ch}}\{Z_p : p \in P_c^{\mathrm{ch}}\} & P_c^{\mathrm{ch}} \neq \emptyset, \\[0.5ex] \operatorname{stat}_{\mathrm{hill}}\{Z_p : p \in P_c\} & P_c^{\mathrm{ch}} = \emptyset \text{ and } \lvert P_c \rvert \ge n_{\min}, \\[0.5ex] \tilde z_c & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{split}\]

A channel cell needs one channel pixel. A hillslope cell needs \(n_{\min}\) pixels, and a cell finer than the DEM falls back to the centroid value. Two corrections follow, in this order:

\[ \text{if } \lvert z_{\mathrm{top},c} - \tilde z_c \rvert > \varepsilon_z \text{ on a hillslope cell:}\quad z_{\mathrm{top},c} \leftarrow \tilde z_c, \]
\[ z_{\mathrm{top},c} \leftarrow \max\bigl(z_{\mathrm{top},c},\ z_{\mathrm{bot},c} + b_{\min}\bigr) \quad \text{on every active cell.} \]

The first one guards against a nodata edge: channel cells are exempt, since they are lowered on purpose. It is off when \(\varepsilon_z = 0\). The second one keeps a lowered top above the bottom. Only the top is zonal; the bottom keeps its centroid value, so a lowered top thins every layer of that column. The code logs, once per build, how many cells took a zonal value, how many are channel cells, and how far the tops were lowered.

Fig. 33 A cell of 32 m radius over a DEM of 5 m pixels, its centre on a bank 18 m from a channel incised 2 m (blue). Right: the elevation of each pixel inside the cell, and the top three rules give, from `zonal_top` with `channel_stat = "min"` and `hillslope_stat = "median"`. Look at the gap: the centroid sample and the hillslope median sit on the bank, about 4 m above the channel minimum the cell takes when the stream raster is read.

The zonal rule falls back to the centroid value, with a message in the log, in three cases: a surface with no georeferencing (`Zonal top sampling needs a georeferenced surface; using centroid sample.`), a channel source with no stream raster (`Zonal channel_source=%s but no stream raster found`; the channel class is then off), and a structured grid whose cells cover fewer than two DEM pixels (`Zonal top sampling skipped: a grid cell`). In the code: `zonal_top`.

## 6. Thickness and layers

The column of each cell is cut into layers by shares of its thickness, the same shares in every cell, set by `modflow6.sgrid.vertical.genmtd_lay`. The rule, (14), and its three strategies are on The solver grid and its layers.

Every layer shares the cells of the plan: the mesh is a vertical extrusion. A cell is inactive in every layer when its top or its bottom is nodata, not finite, or at or below the nodata value.

## 7. How many cells a size costs

The cost of a run grows with the number of cells, so a structured grid and a mesh are compared at equal cell count. The ideal count below assumes cells of one uniform size over an area \(A_\Omega\).

For a structured grid of pixel side \(\Delta\):

\[ N_S = \frac{A_\Omega}{\Delta^2}. \]

For a triangulation of equilateral triangles of side \(\ell\), the triangle area is \(\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\ell^2\). The Voronoi cells are hexagons, whose area is \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\ell^2\) when two neighbouring seeds are \(\ell\) apart:

(25)\[ N_T = \frac{4}{\sqrt3}\,\frac{A_\Omega}{\ell^2} \approx 2.31\,\frac{A_\Omega}{\ell^2}, \qquad N_V = \frac{2}{\sqrt3}\,\frac{A_\Omega}{\ell^2} \approx 1.15\,\frac{A_\Omega}{\ell^2}. \]

Equal counts then give the edge length that costs the same as a grid of side \(\Delta\):

| Cells | Count for an area \(A_\Omega\) | Edge length at the cost of the grid of side \(\Delta\) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Square pixels | \(A_\Omega/\Delta^2\) | \(\Delta\) |
| Voronoi cells | \(\approx 1.15\,A_\Omega/\ell^2\) | \(\ell = \Delta \sqrt{2/\sqrt3} \approx 1.07\,\Delta\) |
| Triangles | \(\approx 2.31\,A_\Omega/\ell^2\) | \(\ell = \Delta \sqrt{4/\sqrt3} \approx 1.52\,\Delta\) |

Worked example. The 21406 cells of 75 m of the header of `step1_minimal.toml` (the file does not say if the count includes the inactive cells) cover \(21406 \times 75^2\ \mathrm{m^2} \approx 120\ \mathrm{km^2}\). The same count on a Voronoi mesh means seeds about \(81\ \mathrm{m}\) apart; on a triangle mesh, triangles of about \(114\ \mathrm{m}\) side. These are ideal figures: a real mesh refines near the interfaces, and the count of a run is the number of cells (\(\mathrm{ncpl}\)) of its DISV file.

Fig. 35 (25) for \(A_\Omega\) = 120 km². The three lines are parallel: halving the size multiplies the count by four for every layout. Look at the dots, 21406 cells each: 75 m pixels, Voronoi seeds 81 m apart, triangles of 114 m.

\(N_S\) counts the cells of the whole raster box, active or not (1. A structured grid); every cell of a mesh lies in \(\Omega\).

## 8. The checks the code applies

The code does not compute a minimum angle, an aspect ratio, a skewness or a ratio of the areas of two neighbours, and it refuses no mesh for its shape. The table lists what it does check. Where a limit is a number, the table names the constant that holds it.

| What is checked | Rule | What happens | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top and bottom overlap | at least one cell where both are valid | refused: `No finite overlapping valid cells found between top and bottom surfaces.` | `_assert_bottom_below_top` in `discretization_spatial.py`, and the same check in `sgrid_generation.py` |
| Bottom below top | strictly, on every valid cell | refused: `Bottom surface must be strictly below top surface on valid cells` | the same two functions |
| Cells much thicker than the rest | thickness above the larger of 10 times the median and 500 m | warning only, runtime mesh only: `Aquifer thickness outliers:` | `_warn_on_outlier_thickness`; constants `_THICKNESS_OUTLIER_FACTOR` and `_THICKNESS_OUTLIER_FLOOR_M` in `discretization_spatial.py` |
| Non-orthogonality | the trigger of XT3D on irregular meshes | XT3D switched on, not a refusal | `resolve_xt3d_decision` |
| Zonal top | \(n_{\min}\) pixels, \(\varepsilon_z\), \(b_{\min}\) | fallback or clamp, counted in the log | `zonal_top` in `zonal_stats.py`; the keys are on the cards below |
| Structured grid for the zonal top | each cell covers at least two DEM pixels | zonal top skipped, resampled top kept | `_cells_cover_pixels` (argument `min_pixels`) |
| Size keys of the mesher | \(\ell_s \leq \ell_g\), \(\ell_{\min} \leq \ell_{\max}\) | refused when the file is read: `interface_size must be <= global_size when refine_interfaces=true`, `min_size must be <= max_size` | `ZoneMeshingSettings` in `zone_meshing/config.py` |
| Geology | a geology section when the mode asks for geology | refused: `geology section is required when constraints_mode includes geology.` | `MeshCatchmentConfig` in `mesh/config/main.py` |
| Zones that overlap | priorities must settle every overlap | refused: `Overlapping zones detected without priority resolution` | `resolve_zone_overlaps` in `_polygon_cleaning.py` |
| Gap between the zones and the domain | the uncovered area is below a tolerance, and the constraint curves exist | recorded in the summary file of the mesh (`qa_checks`, `constraints_qa`), never enforced | `ZoneConformalQaChecks` in `_summary_sidecar.py`, `_build_constraints_qa_contract` in `reporting.py` |

The last row matters for the reading of a mesh: the summary file says whether the constraints were embedded, and no code of `hydromodpy` reads that verdict. A mesh whose summary says `overall_pass: false` still runs.

## Assumptions

- A cell has one top and one bottom. The surface inside the cell is flat.
- A mesh is fixed for the run. It does not move with the water table.
- The conductivity is isotropic in the plane. The code writes no input for horizontal anisotropy.
- The coordinates are in a projected CRS in metres. The merge of the vertices of the dual (1 mm) and every size of the mesher read this.
- The zonal rule treats a channel pixel as a pixel of the stream raster of the delineation. It does not read the observed network.

## Limits

- No refinement without `min_size`. With `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.refine_interfaces` on and `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.min_size` unset, the lower bound of the size is \(\ell_g\), and Gmsh raises every size to it (figure of 2. A runtime mesh from Gmsh). In a test with Gmsh 4.15.2, on a \(1000\ \mathrm{m}\) square refined along one side, the mesh had 250 triangles with the lower bound at \(\ell_g\) and 602 with it at 20 m. Set `min_size` at or below `interface_size`.
- The dual does not follow the constraints. It keeps the outline of the domain, not the river traces or the geology interfaces. A cell can hold both sides of an interface.
- A mesh bundle written for the triangles does not fit the dual. The bundle holds one conductivity per triangle, and the dual has about half as many cells. The code then logs a warning that ends with `Configure K in [flow] or set grid_dual='triangle' to reuse the bundle.` and ignores the bundle value.
- No shape check. A sliver, an abrupt change of size or a high non-orthogonality does not stop a run. The non-orthogonality is the only shape measure the code reads, and it decides about XT3D, not about the mesh. `connection_nonorthogonality_deg` and `nonorthogonality_summary` can be called on any planar `HydroMesh` for a closer look.
- MODFLOW-NWT is structured. Its zonal top needs `modflownwt.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_source` at `"none"`: the file is refused otherwise.
- Boussinesq ignores `grid_dual` and the top sampling. It works on the triangles.
- Gmsh is not reproducible. Two builds of the same input give meshes with different cell counts. The mesh cache, `mesh_catchment.cache`, pins the first one (`hydromodpy/spatial/mesh/mesh_cache.py`).
- Not a 3D mesh. The layers are an extrusion of the plan. A footprint that changes from one layer to the next, or a refinement in depth, is not represented.
- An outlier thickness only warns. A nodata value read as an elevation gives a cell that is kilometres deep, with a clean top, and the run converges. The warning of 8. The checks the code applies is the only sign, and a structured grid does not emit it.

The keys of the structured grid are in [modflow6] and those of the runtime mesh in [mesh_catchment].

## Parameters of this page

The keys that choose the layout, the size and the top. The cards show the defaults and the allowed values. The three keys of `[mesh_catchment.zone_meshing]` that bound the size are in the first group.

[mesh_catchment]

`constraints_mode = "rivers_only"` : Meshing compliance target, required in every [mesh_catchment] table. required example value
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.constraints_mode`
**More**: 'geology_only' conforms the mesh to geology interfaces only, 'rivers_only' conforms the mesh to river traces only, and 'geology_rivers' enforces both sets of constraints in one mesh.
**Values**:
- `"geology_only"`
- `"rivers_only"`
- `"geology_rivers"`
**Accepted**: "geology_only" | "rivers_only" | "geology_rivers"
**Example**: `"rivers_only"`, `"geology_rivers"`

`# cache = false` : If true, reuse a previously generated mesh when its inputs (domain geometry, river constraint, lake/dam refinement, mesh and delineation configuration) are unchanged, instead of regenerating it.
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.cache`
**More**: Gmsh is not reproducible run to run (it reseeds from the system clock), so regeneration yields a different mesh and makes results and calibration objectives irreproducible; caching pins the mesh. Default off (regenerate every run). See hydromodpy.spatial.mesh.mesh_cache.
**Accepted**: true | false

[mesh_catchment.zone_meshing]

`# algorithm = "delaunay"` : Planar Gmsh algorithm name.
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.algorithm`
**More**: In practice the examples use 'delaunay', which is a robust default for irregular geological and river-constrained domains.
**Accepted**: string

`# global_size = 250.0` : Baseline target cell size in projected metres over the full support domain. m >= 0
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.global_size`
**More**: Think of it as the coarse background resolution before local interface refinement is added.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# min_size = ‹number›` : Lower bound on local cell size in projected metres. m >= 0
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.min_size`
**More**: Use it to prevent extreme refinement from generating very small cells in narrow features.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# max_size = ‹number›` : Upper bound on local cell size in projected metres. m >= 0
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.max_size`
**More**: Use it when you want to cap the coarsening far from interfaces.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# refine_interfaces = false` : Enable a distance-based size field around geology or river interfaces.
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.refine_interfaces`
**More**: When false, the mesh uses only the global background size constraints.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# interface_size = ‹number›` : Target local size, in projected metres, close to constrained interfaces. >= 0 dev
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.interface_size`
**More**: When omitted and refine_interfaces=true, the schema derives a conservative default from global_size/min_size.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

`# interface_distance = ‹number›` : Influence distance, in projected metres, over which the local interface refinement fades back to the background size. >= 0 dev
**Path**: `mesh_catchment.zone_meshing.interface_distance`
**More**: Larger values spread refinement farther away from the interface network.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

[mesh_input]

`# mesh_path = ‹path›` : Path to the external planar mesh file (typically a `.msh`).
**Path**: `mesh_input.mesh_path`
**More**: Required when `bundle_dir` is not provided. Relative paths are resolved against the TOML directory.
**Accepted**: path

`# bundle_dir = ‹path›` : Path to the solver-exchange mesh bundle directory associated with the external mesh.
**Path**: `mesh_input.bundle_dir`
**More**: Required when `mesh_path` is not provided. Relative paths are resolved against the TOML directory.
**Accepted**: path

[modflow6.sgrid.planar]

`# mode = "keep_native"` : Planar solver-grid mode: keep the native domain support or resample to an explicit (ny, nx) target shape.
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.planar.mode`
**Values**:
- `"keep_native"` : Keeps the top raster's native shape and resolution, no resampling.
- `"resample_to_shape"` : Resamples top and bottom onto an explicit (ny, nx) grid, keeping the same extent.
**Accepted**: "keep_native" | "resample_to_shape"

`# nx = ‹integer›` : Target number of columns when planar mode is 'resample_to_shape'. - > 0
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.planar.nx`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# ny = ‹integer›` : Target number of rows when planar mode is 'resample_to_shape'. - > 0
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.planar.ny`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# resampling = "bilinear"` : Resampling rule applied when planar mode is 'resample_to_shape'. dev
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.planar.resampling`
**Values**:
- `"bilinear"`no explanation
- `"average"`no explanation
- `"nearest"`no explanation
**Accepted**: "bilinear" | "average" | "nearest"

[modflow6.sgrid]

`# grid_dual = "voronoi"` : Applies only to a MODFLOW 6 run on a Gmsh mesh built by the run; ignored for structured grids, MODFLOW-NWT and Boussinesq (which keeps its own triangulation).
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.grid_dual`
**More**: 'voronoi' uses the PEBI dual (exact CVFD orthogonality, ~half the cells) and is the default; 'triangle' keeps the triangulation cells as the DISV grid for simplex comparison runs.
**Values**:
- `"voronoi"`
- `"triangle"`
**Accepted**: "voronoi" | "triangle"

[modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling]

`# mode = "centroid"` : Top-sampling strategy.
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.mode`
**More**: 'centroid' samples the DEM at each cell generator, or resamples it to a structured grid (fast, the current behaviour, byte-identical default). 'zonal' reduces every DEM pixel inside a cell with per-class stats.
**Values**:
- `"centroid"`
- `"zonal"`
**Accepted**: "centroid" | "zonal"

`# hillslope_stat = "median"` : Zonal statistic over non-channel (hillslope) pixels inside a cell.
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.hillslope_stat`
**Values**:
- `"mean"` : Averages every hillslope pixel in the cell to set its top elevation.
- `"median"` : Uses the median hillslope pixel elevation, robust to outlier pixels.
- `"min"` : Uses the lowest hillslope pixel elevation found inside the cell.
- `"max"` : Uses the highest hillslope pixel elevation found inside the cell.
- `"p10"` : Uses the 10th percentile of hillslope pixel elevations inside the cell.
- `"p25"` : Uses the 25th percentile of hillslope pixel elevations inside the cell.
**Accepted**: "mean" | "median" | "min" | "max" | "p10" | "p25"

`# channel_stat = "min"` : Zonal statistic over channel pixels inside a cell (thalweg-preserving; 'min' keeps the incised low).
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_stat`
**Values**:
- `"min"` : Uses the lowest channel pixel elevation, keeping the incised thalweg low.
- `"p10"` : Uses the 10th percentile of channel pixel elevations, near the thalweg low.
- `"p25"` : Uses the 25th percentile of channel pixel elevations, above the thalweg low.
- `"median"` : Uses the median channel pixel elevation, less aggressive than the thalweg low.
- `"mean"` : Averages channel pixel elevations, smoothing over the incised thalweg.
**Accepted**: "min" | "p10" | "p25" | "median" | "mean"

`# channel_source = "streams_raster"` : Where channel pixels come from when mode='zonal'.
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_source`
**More**: 'streams_raster' uses the delineated river-network raster reprojected onto the DEM grid; 'none' disables the channel class (every pixel is hillslope).
**Values**:
- `"none"`
- `"streams_raster"`
**Accepted**: "none" | "streams_raster"

`# channel_buffer_px = 0` : Dilate the channel pixel mask by this many pixels before reducing, to capture a channel that grazes a cell without a pixel centre on it. >= 0 dev
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.channel_buffer_px`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

`# spike_guard_tol_m = 2.0` : Revert a hillslope cell's zonal value to the centroid sample when it deviates more than this many metres (guards nodata/edge spikes); channel cells are exempt since they are lowered on purpose. m >= 0 dev
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.spike_guard_tol_m`
**More**: 0 disables the guard.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# min_pixels = 3` : Minimum DEM pixels inside a cell to trust a hillslope zonal statistic; below this the cell falls back to the centroid sample. > 0 dev
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.min_pixels`
**More**: A channel cell uses its channel stat from a single thalweg pixel.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

`# min_thickness_m = 0.1` : Minimum layer-0 thickness (m) kept after zonal top lowering, so a carved channel top never collides with the aquifer bottom. m >= 0 dev
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.top_sampling.min_thickness_m`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

[modflow6.sgrid.vertical]

`# genmtd_lay = "constant"` : How the aquifer thickness is split into layers: equal layers, layers that thicken with depth, or the fractions you list.
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.vertical.genmtd_lay`
**Values**:
- `"constant"` : Splits local thickness into nlay equal-fraction layers at every cell.
- `"decay"` : Grows layer thickness geometrically with depth when lay_decay is above one.
- `"list"` : Uses the explicit per-layer thickness fractions given in lay_proportions.
**Accepted**: "constant" | "decay" | "list"

`# nlay = 1` : Number of layers for 'constant' and 'decay'. -
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.vertical.nlay`
**More**: With 'list', the number of fractions sets it.
**Accepted**: integer
**Unit**: -

`# lay_decay = 2.0` : Ratio of each layer's thickness to the thickness of the layer above it, above 1. - only if genmtd_lay = "decay" example value
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.vertical.lay_decay`
**More**: With 2, each layer is twice as thick as the one above.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `2.0`
**Only if**: genmtd_lay = "decay"

`# lay_proportions = [0.2, 0.3, 0.5]` : Share of the thickness each layer takes, from the top. only if genmtd_lay = "list" example value
**Path**: `modflow6.sgrid.vertical.lay_proportions`
**More**: The shares must sum to 1.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Example**: `[0.2, 0.3, 0.5]`
**Only if**: genmtd_lay = "list"

[modflow6.runtime]

`# mf6_enable_xt3d = ‹true | false›` : Enable MF6 NPF XT3D terms. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_enable_xt3d`
**More**: When left to None, XT3D is auto-enabled only when the mesh is significantly non-orthogonal or anisotropic K is configured; the default Voronoi/PEBI dual grid is near-orthogonal, so XT3D stays off there. It adds cost but improves accuracy on non-orthogonal or anisotropic grids.
**Accepted**: true | false

Lines generated from the models, as in the reference. Open one for its card.

# Notation

Every symbol of the theory pages, with its unit and the key that sets it. The tables are generated from one registry, `docs/source/theory/symbols.yaml`, and each theory page renders its own table from the same file.

The units are the ones the code stores: lengths in metres, hydraulic conductivity in m/s, rates in m/s. The soil reservoir is the exception, because it works in mm and days. A name that exists in the code or in an output file is given in `code font` in the meaning column, so a symbol can be matched with a column of a result file.

## Conventions

- Lengths are in metres, and elevation is positive up.
- A flux into the aquifer is positive. The residual of the Boussinesq solver is the one exception: it counts a loss as positive, and its page says so.
- Cells are \(n\) and \(m\) on the pages of the two MODFLOW solvers and of the mesh, and \(i\) on the Boussinesq page, which runs on triangles.
- A symbol with an overbar, such as \(\bar B\), is an average over the catchment. It is by area, unless the page says otherwise.
- A TOML value can carry its unit, such as `"500 m"` or `"1 month"`. The unit of a key is on its card.

## Space, time and heads

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| \(x, y\) | horizontal coordinates | m | the grid, The mesh |
| \(z\) | elevation, positive up | m | - |
| \(d\) | depth below the model top, the variable of the depth factor of a property | m | - |
| \(t\) | time; on the soil page, the day | s | `start_datetime` and `end_datetime` bound the run |
| \(\Delta t\) | length of a stress period, the stretch of time that gets one forcing value | s | `step_value` |
| \(\delta t\) | solver time step, \(\delta t = \Delta t / n_\mathrm{sub}\) | s | derived |
| \(n_\mathrm{sub}\) | number of solver time steps in a stress period |
-
 | `substeps_per_period` |
| \(h\) | hydraulic head, measured from a fixed datum | m | solved, not set |
| \(h_0\) | head at the start of the run | m | `type` |
| \(z_\mathrm{top}\) | model top, the land surface | m | `data.dem` |
| \(z'_\mathrm{top}\) | computational top MODFLOW 6 reads, \(z'_\mathrm{top} = z_\mathrm{top} + \max H_1 - H_1\) | m | derived |
| \(z_\mathrm{bot}\) | bottom of the aquifer | m | `kind` |
| \(H\) | aquifer thickness, \(H = z_\mathrm{top} - z_\mathrm{bot}\) | m | `kind` |
| \(H_1\) | thickness of the top layer under the ground | m | `nlay` |
| \(B\) | saturated thickness, \(B(h) = \min\bigl(\max(h - z_\mathrm{bot}, 0), H\bigr)\) | m | state, not a field |
| \(\bar B\) | saturated thickness averaged by area over the catchment (`d_sat_m`) | m | derived |
| \(A\) | catchment area | m² | `geographic.catchment` |
| \(L_h\) | horizontal length of a flow path, from a divide to the stream that drains it | m | derived |

# The daily soil reservoir

Each day, a soil store takes the rain, loses water to evapotranspiration, and sends the water it cannot hold down to the water table. This page gives the equations the code solves, what they assume, and where they stop being true. It does not say how to set up a run: for that, see step 6 of the staircase.

Note

Scope. The reservoir runs under MODFLOW 6 only. A file that declares `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil` with another flow solver is refused when it is read. The equations below are the ones of `hydromodpy/physics/hydrology/soil_reservoir/kernel.py`.

## The model in one picture

The numbers 1 to 8 are the steps of the next sections. The two thick boxes are the stores that the soil and transit equations update; the recharge is what MODFLOW 6 receives.

The state before the first day, \(S_0\), \(R_0\) and \(C_0\), comes from `spinup` (see The starting state).

## The daily balance

The code applies the steps below in this order, for every column and every day.

### 1. Curve-number runoff (optional)

Read only when `curve_number` is set, between 30 and 98. Without it, \(Q_t = 0\) and the step costs nothing: the result is the same, bit for bit, as without the term.

The runoff is the SCS curve-number runoff as the HELP model uses it [Schroeder and others, 1994]. The conversion of a class II number to the dry (class I) and wet (class III) numbers is the one of Chow et al. [1988], equations 5.5.6 and 5.5.7. The code makes these choices:

- The number in the file is the class II one. The code derives the other two.
- The wetness of the soil is the store at the end of the day before, as a share of its capacity (next equation).
- The retention \(\sigma_t\), in mm, moves linearly with \(w_t\) between its value at the dry number (\(w_t = 0\)) and its value at the wet number (\(w_t = 1\)) [Schroeder and others, 1994].
- The initial abstraction is \(0.2\,\sigma_t\), with no other choice.
- The rain that infiltrates is \(P_t - Q_t\). The runoff \(Q_t\) is taken before the soil sees the rain, so the soil gets less of it.
(6)\[ w_t = \min\!\left(1,\ \max\!\left(0,\ \frac{S_{t-1}}{\mathrm{RU}}\right)\right), \qquad w_t = 1 \text{ if } \mathrm{RU} = 0 . \]

### 2. Bypass

A constant share \(b\) of the infiltrating rain skips the soil. The rest is added to the store:

(7)\[ B_t = b\,(P_t - Q_t), \qquad W_t = S_{t-1} + (1 - b)\,(P_t - Q_t). \]

Here \(b\) is `bypass_fraction`. \(W_t\) is the water in the soil after the rain and before any evaporation.

### 3. Evapotranspiration

The soil evaporates at the full rate \(k_c E_t\) while it holds more than \(\alpha\,\mathrm{RU}\). Below that, the rate falls linearly with the store. It can never exceed what the soil holds:

(8)\[ \psi_t = \min\!\left(1,\ \frac{W_t}{\alpha\,\mathrm{RU}}\right), \qquad \mathrm{ETR}_t = \min\bigl(W_t,\ k_c\,E_t\,\psi_t\bigr), \]

with \(\psi_t = 1\) if \(\mathrm{RU} = 0\). The two symbols are `alpha` and `kc`, and `ru` is the capacity. \(\alpha\) is the \(1 - p\) of FAO-56 [Allen et al., 1998] and the \(LP\) of HBV [Seibert and Vis, 2012].

### 4. Overflow

What exceeds the capacity leaves the soil. Nothing else does:

(9)\[ X_t = \max\bigl(0,\ W_t - \mathrm{ETR}_t - \mathrm{RU}\bigr), \qquad S_t = W_t - \mathrm{ETR}_t - X_t . \]

### 5. Transit through the unsaturated zone

The overflow and the bypass enter one linear reservoir of time constant \(\tau\), `transit_time`. The inflow \(I_t = X_t + B_t\) is taken as constant over the day, and the reservoir is integrated exactly over that day:

(10)\[ R_t = \tau I_t + (R_{t-1} - \tau I_t)\,e^{-1/\tau}, \qquad O_t = I_t - (R_t - R_{t-1}). \]

\(O_t\) is the water that reaches the water table. If \(\tau = 0\), then \(O_t = I_t\) and \(R_t = R_{t-1}\).

### 6. Routing of the curve-number runoff

The runoff \(Q_t\) goes through the same exact reservoir, with the time constant \(\tau_q\), `runoff_time`, and its own store \(C_t\). The routed runoff is called \(Q^r_t\). If \(\tau_q = 0\), then \(Q^r_t = Q_t\).

### 7. Delay of the curve-number runoff

A pure delay of \(L\) days, `runoff_lag`, follows. Write \(L = n + \varphi\) with \(n\) a whole number of days and \(0 \le \varphi < 1\). The delayed runoff is a linear interpolation between two whole-day shifts:

(11)\[ Q^L_t = (1 - \varphi)\,Q^r_{t-n} + \varphi\,Q^r_{t-n-1} . \]

A day that falls before day 1 of the run reads zero, or, with `spinup = "first_year"`, the days at the end of the last repeated first year, which stand for the days before the run. The delay is not a store: it moves water in time and keeps its volume, except the part pushed beyond the last day of the run.

### 8. Fluxes per unit of column area

The stores above are per unit of unsealed area. The sealed share \(f\), `impervious_fraction`, gets no infiltration and no evaporation. The fluxes of the column are:

(12)\[\begin{split} \begin{aligned} N_t &= (1 - f)\,O_t,\\ \text{ETR}^{\text{col}}_t &= (1 - f)\,\mathrm{ETR}_t,\\ \text{residual ETP}_t &= (1 - f)\,\bigl(k_c\,E_t - \mathrm{ETR}_t\bigr),\\ \text{runoff}_t &= f\,P_t + (1 - f)\,Q^L_t . \end{aligned} \end{split}\]

\(N_t\) is the recharge MODFLOW 6 receives. The residual ETP is the demand \(k_c E_t\) that the soil could not meet.

In the code: `soil_step`.

## Three days, by hand

The numbers below come from one call of `soil_step`, (6) to (12), for each day, with \(\mathrm{RU} = 150\) mm, \(\alpha = 0.6\), \(k_c = 1\), \(f = b = \tau = 0\). The last day adds a curve number of 80 with \(\tau_q = 0\). Its store is full, so \(w = 1\) and \(\sigma\) is the retention at the wet number, \(\mathrm{CN}_\mathrm{III} = 90.2\).

| | Dry day | Overflow | Curve number |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| \(S_{t-1}\) (mm) | 40 | 145 | 150 |
| \(P_t\), \(E_t\) (mm/day) | 0, 4 | 30, 3 | 30, 3 |
| What happens | \(W = 40\) is below \(\alpha\,\mathrm{RU} = 90\), so \(\psi = 0.444\) | \(W = 175\), evaporation 3, \(175 - 3 - 150 = 22\) leaves | \(w = 1\), \(\sigma = 27.6\), \(Q = 11.50\), then \(W = 168.50\) |
| ETR (mm/day) | 1.78 | 3.00 | 3.00 |
| Recharge \(N_t\) (mm/day) | 0 | 22.00 | 15.50 |
| Runoff (mm/day) | 0 | 0 | 11.50 |
| \(S_t\) (mm) | 38.22 | 150 | 150 |
| Residual ETP (mm/day) | 2.22 | 0 | 0 |

On the third day, \(30 = 3.00 + 15.50 + 11.50\): the balance closes with no change of store.

## The balance closes

Over any run, per column and per day:

(13)\[ P_t = \mathrm{ETR}^{\text{col}}_t + N_t + \text{runoff}_t + \Delta\bigl[(1 - f)(S + R + C)\bigr]_t + \Delta\Lambda_t , \]

where \(\Lambda_t\) is the running total of runoff held back by the delay (`runoff_lag`). The function `balance_residual` computes the difference between the two sides. On 400 days of random rain and ETP over three columns, with a sealed share, a bypass, a transit time, a curve number and a delay all switched on, the largest residual is under \(10^{-13}\) mm: rounding error only.

## The starting state

With `spinup = "none"`, the soil starts full and the other stores empty: \(S_0 = \mathrm{RU}\), \(R_0 = C_0 = 0\).

With `spinup = "first_year"`, the default, the first 365 days of rain and ETP are run again and again, starting from that full soil. The loop stops when no store of any column moves by \(0.1\) mm or more over one repetition, or after 20 repetitions. The state at the end of the last repetition is \(S_0\), \(R_0\) and \(C_0\). If 20 repetitions are not enough, the run stops with an error. A run shorter than 365 days is refused with this option.

## Columns and capacity classes

Without `data.soil_capacity`, each cell of the rain and ETP grid is one column and the same RU applies to all. With it, the pixels of the raster in each cell are sorted by capacity and cut into ten classes of equal pixel count. Each class is a column, with a capacity \(\mathrm{RU} \times (\text{class mean} / \text{raster mean})\). The value given in the file is therefore the mean capacity, and the raster only spreads it. The basin value of any flux gives every cell the same weight, and every class of a cell its share of the pixels.

## How much recharge, by capacity

\(\mathrm{RU}\) is the parameter the recharge depends on most. A larger store keeps more of the winter rain for the summer, when the plants take it back, so the recharge falls as the capacity grows.

Fig. 17 Recharge and evapotranspiration against \(\mathrm{RU}\), from `spinup_state` and `run_soil_balance` on a synthetic six-year climate (904 mm of rain and 698 mm of ETP per year, the other keys at their defaults). The two curves sum to the rain over the run.

Example 04 prints the same ladder on its own forcing, the SIM2 rain and ETP of 2015 to 2020 over its catchment:

| \(\mathrm{RU}\) (mm) | 50 | 100 | 150 | 200 | 250 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recharge (mm/year) | 443 | 392 | 356 | 325 | 295 |

Over the same days the rain is 904 mm/year, the ETP 698 mm/year and the gauged discharge 327 mm/year. From 50 to 250 mm the recharge loses a third. To set the capacity, see `ru`.

## Assumptions

- The rain of a day reaches the soil before it evaporates, the same day. The evaporation stress of day \(t\) is computed on the store after the rain.
- The rain and the ETP are constant over the day.
- All the water above RU leaves the soil as drainage. There is no saturation-excess runoff term in the kernel.
- The bypass is a constant share of the infiltrating rain, the same in every season.
- The unsaturated zone is one linear reservoir per column, with one time constant for the whole catchment.
- The sealed share receives rain and nothing else: it neither infiltrates nor evaporates, and its runoff is immediate.
- The curve-number runoff reads the wetness of the day before, not the one after the rain.
- Columns do not exchange water with each other.
- One value of \(\alpha\), \(k_c\), \(f\), \(b\), \(\tau\), CN, \(\tau_q\) and \(L\) applies to the whole catchment and to the whole run. Only RU varies, through the capacity classes.
- The rain is one total grid: snow counts as rain on the day it falls. The file is refused unless `components = ["total"]`.

## Limits

- No feedback from the aquifer. The soil store never reads the water table. A shallow water table does not reduce the capacity. The only link back is the residual ETP, which MODFLOW 6 may draw from the water table (Where the results go).
- Daily forcing only. The rain and the ETP must have one value per day and per cell, with no gap and no negative value, on a standard calendar, with the rain and the ETP on the same grid, in the CRS of the model. Otherwise the run stops before the reservoir is computed.
- No groundwater memory. The transit time is limited to 30 days, so that the slow response comes from MODFLOW 6 and not from this reservoir.
- Curve number and delay. \(\tau_q\) and \(L\) are read only when `curve_number` is set. A fractional delay spreads a one-day pulse over two days. The part of the delayed runoff that falls after the last day of the run is not represented.
- First period. A steady first stress period is refused, since it would hold the recharge of one day only.
- SIM2 drainage is not a summer reference across 2016. Over the catchment of example 04, the SIM2 drainage (DRAINC) never falls below about 0.2 mm/day from 2016 on: its 30-day minimum is 0.29, 0.23 and 0.30 mm/day in 2016, 2017 and 2018, against 0.00 to 0.04 mm/day in 2012 to 2015, on all nine cells of the grid alike. A recharge from this reservoir falls to zero in a dry summer; compare it with the SIM2 drainage period by period, never across that step.
- No other runoff. Water that leaves saturated ground is not a term of this model. In a run, it leaves through the drains of MODFLOW 6.

## Where the results go

The reservoir hands three daily grids to the rest of the run, in mm/day on the cells of the rain grid.

- The recharge goes to the MODFLOW 6 recharge package. A file that also loads a recharge, through `data.types`, is refused.
- The residual ETP goes to the MODFLOW 6 evapotranspiration package, which draws it from the water table. The rate falls linearly to zero at `flow.sinks_sources.etp.extinction_depth` below the drain elevation of the cell. This needs `"etp"` in `flow.active_sinks_sources`.
- The runoff goes where a loaded runoff would go: the stream networks, the lakes, and the discharge that a calibration compares with the gauge. A file that also loads a runoff, through `data.types`, is refused, because the same water would be counted twice.

## Parameters of this page

The fields below are the ones that appear in the equations. Open a row for its card.

[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil]

**Unit**: -

**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.curve_number`

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.runoff_lag`
**More**: Read only when curve_number is set. 0 adds no delay, bit for bit as before; "0.75 days" also reads, interpolated linearly between the neighbouring whole-day shifts. **More**: "first_year" repeats the first 365 days of the run until the storage at the end of that year moves by less than 0.1 mm, 20 times at most; the run must last one year at least. "none" starts from a full soil, the state of a soil in a wet winter.
**Values**:
- `"first_year"` : Repeat the first year until the soil storage settles.
- `"none"` : Start from a full soil and an empty transit store.
**Accepted**: "first_year" | "none"
