# The solvers of the aquifer

HydroModPy integrates the groundwater flow equation with one of three solvers: MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW-NWT or the in-house Boussinesq solver. This page says which packages and options HydroModPy writes for each of them, how it sets the time steps, what happens to a cell that dries, how the two MODFLOW solvers differ, and how a transport run hooks onto a flow run. What each solver supports is listed in Solvers.

Note

Scope. The balance of a cell, (17), is on The groundwater flow problem. The Boussinesq solver is on Boussinesq theory and the XT3D terms on XT3D on irregular meshes.

## Sources

The MODFLOW equations, packages and numerical methods are documented by the USGS. This page does not repeat them. It says which options HydroModPy writes.

- MODFLOW 6 groundwater flow model: control-volume formulation, Newton-Raphson, storage and stress packages [Langevin et al., 2017].
- MODFLOW 6 framework and the IMS linear solver [Hughes et al., 2017].
- XT3D option of the `NPF` package [Provost et al., 2017].
- MODFLOW-NWT, the Newton formulation of MODFLOW-2005 [Niswonger et al., 2011], on the MODFLOW-2005 groundwater flow process [Harbaugh, 2005].
- MODFLOW 6 groundwater transport model [Langevin et al., 2022] and water mover package [Morway et al., 2021].
- The MODFLOW 6 input guide and the MODFLOW-NWT guide, for the definition of each package and option.

## The three solvers side by side

| | MODFLOW 6 | MODFLOW-NWT | Boussinesq |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Name in `solvers` | `modflow6` | `modflow_nwt` | `boussinesq` |
| Grid | DISV for every grid, structured or not | structured grid only (DIS) | triangular cells of a Gmsh mesh |
| Time | backward Euler, equal steps in a period | backward Euler, equal steps in a period | one backward Euler step per period |
| Transport | GWT and particle tracking | MODPATH and MT3DMS | refused |

The names in the first row are the values read by `simulation.process.solvers`. The capabilities of each solver, generated from the code, are on Solvers.

## Time steps

The three solvers read the same time grid, built from `simulation.time`. Each stress period has a length \(\Delta t\) and holds every forcing constant. The two MODFLOW solvers cut it into \(n_\mathrm{sub}\) equal steps, \(\delta t = \Delta t / n_\mathrm{sub}\), with a step multiplier of 1: MODFLOW 6 in its `TDIS` package, MODFLOW-NWT in `DIS`.

Equal steps are a choice with a test behind it. On a confined column against a closed-form solution, `test_stress_period_substepping` finds equal steps more accurate than a geometric growth of the steps, in either direction, and one step per period about ten times less accurate than ten steps (Validation). The unconfined problem is nonlinear, so this holds there only approximately. The same case reports that one step per period moves the monthly discharge of a drained hillslope by tens of per cent against a refined run. One step per period is therefore not a neutral choice.

Fig. 41 The confined column of `test_stress_period_substepping`: 200 cells of 5 m, a head step of 1 m held for 31 days, with the backward Euler equations MODFLOW 6 solves for this linear case. Ten steps that grow or shrink by 2 give the same error, about four times that of ten equal steps.

A period is steady or transient. With `flow.flow_regime` set to `"steady"`, every period is steady. With `"transient"`, only the first period is steady, and only when `flow.first_period_steady` is true. With `modflow6.runtime.mf6_ats`, MODFLOW 6 adds adaptive time stepping to the transient periods: each period starts at the step above, ATS subdivides it only where the solver cannot converge, and it never grows past that step. Steady periods are left out. The starting heads are on The starting heads. In the code: `build_temporal_discretization_from_time_grid`.

## The nonlinear solve

MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT both write the balance (17) for every active cell and every step, and solve the nonlinear system by Newton-Raphson outer iterations, with a linear solve inside each one [Hughes et al., 2017, Niswonger et al., 2011]. The tests that stop the iteration and the percent discrepancy of the budget are the ones of the listing file, defined in the sources above. They do not measure the same thing on the two solvers: MODFLOW-NWT tests a norm of the residual over all cells, MODFLOW 6 a maximum over the cells of the linear solve. What HydroModPy adds:

- The keys that set the tests are `modflow6.runtime.mf6_outer_dvclose`, `modflow6.runtime.mf6_inner_dvclose` and `modflow6.runtime.mf6_inner_rclose` for MODFLOW 6, and `modflownwt.runtime.nwt.headtol` and `modflownwt.runtime.nwt.fluxtol` for MODFLOW-NWT. Heads are in m, flows in m³/s. HydroModPy writes `inner_rclose` with no option, which keeps the absolute largest residual of a cell. When the key is unset, the value of the complexity preset applies.
- The run metrics keep the percent discrepancy of the last step and the worst one of the run. A calibration rejects a trial whose last value is above `calibration.reject_water_budget_above`. The auxiliary steady solve of a `steady_state` start accepts its result only within 0.1 per cent. In the code: `percent_discrepancies`.

## MODFLOW 6, package by package

`run_pre_processing` assembles the FloPy simulation in this order. A package marked “if” is written only when the file asks for it. Each package name links its input-guide page.

| Package | Written |
| --- | --- |
| TDIS, IMS, GWF (the Newton options), DISV, IC, NPF, STO, RCHA, OC | always |
| ATS | if `modflow6.runtime.mf6_ats` is true |
| EVTA (or EVT) | if |
| DRN | if the `drainage` boundary is active |
| CHD | if one is active |
| WEL | if a well exists |
| LAK | if a lake is active |
| HFB | if a barrier exists |
| SFR | if `sfr` is active |
| MVR | if one transfer exists |

HydroModPy writes no UZF, GHB or RIV package. Three notes on the table.

- Storage. STO receives \(S_y\) and \(S_s\) and a steady or transient flag per period. The flags are written only where they change. \(S_s\) matters only where the aquifer is confined, but MODFLOW 6 asks for a value. In the code: `sto_period_settings`.
- Recharge. RCHA gets one rate per column and per period: the value of `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.values`, or the recharge the soil reservoir computes (The daily soil reservoir). The cells of a lake that the model makes inactive receive none, because LAK handles the rain on the lake. The package also carries a `CONCENTRATION` auxiliary variable, which transport uses (Transport coupling). In the code: `mask_recharge_on_lake_cells`.
- Output. OC saves the head at the last step of every stress period and the budget at every step, and prints the budget of every step. The catalog keeps one record per stress period: the head at its end, each flux as the mean of its steps weighted by their length (A period cut into time steps).

### The grid

MODFLOW 6 reads every grid as a DISV grid, structured or not: one code path covers both. A structured model is a DISV grid whose cells are the DEM pixels. A mesh built from Gmsh is, by default, the Voronoi dual of its triangles, which is orthogonal to its connections. `modflow6.sgrid.grid_dual` keeps the triangles as cells instead. The number of layers is `modflow6.sgrid.vertical.nlay`. The mesh is the subject of The mesh.

The computational top. Under Newton, MODFLOW 6 builds the horizontal conductance from the full thickness of the two cells times the saturation of the upstream cell, where MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW-USG use the saturated thickness (`GwfConductanceUtils.f90`, NPF) [Langevin et al., 2017]. Where the thickness \(H\) changes from one cell to the next, the transmissivity is then too low by about \(\Delta H / (2H)\). The grid MODFLOW 6 reads therefore has a computational top \(z'_\mathrm{top} = z_\mathrm{top} + \max H_1 - H_1\), with \(H_1\) the thickness of the top layer under the ground: every cell of the top layer gets the same thickness. A thickness that is the same everywhere gives \(z_\mathrm{top}\) back, so no file changes then. This is a numerical device of HydroModPy, not a USGS practice. Every package elevation (drains, EVT, streambeds, lake banks, barriers, the ocean), the initial heads and the run store keep the ground. Water above the ground stays in the aquifer up to \(z'_\mathrm{top}\), with its specific yield, where a cell topped at the ground would turn confined; the drains at the ground keep that rise to a few centimetres. Two limits. A lake column keeps its ground, since a raised top would reach into the lake, so the thickness still changes at the banks. Only the top of the top layer moves: a lower layer whose saturated part changes from cell to cell keeps the bias. Anyone who opens the native MODFLOW 6 files (flopy, ModelMuse) sees a top above the ground wherever the thickness varies. That is intended; the ground is `topography` in the run store. In the code: `disv_grid_kwargs`.

### Flow between cells, and XT3D

NPF receives \(K\), \(K_z = K/\beta\) and the convertible flag. With the two-point conductance (18), the flux between two cells is exact only when the line between the centres is perpendicular to the shared face and the conductivity is isotropic. XT3D adds the missing terms [Provost et al., 2017]. HydroModPy decides about it once per run; the rule and its trigger are on XT3D on irregular meshes. XT3D makes the matrix non-symmetric, so the IMS preset is promoted when needed (The solution: Newton and IMS). In the code: `resolve_xt3d_decision`.

### Evaporation, drains, lakes and streams

The laws, conductances and worked cells of these exits are on How water leaves the aquifer.

- Evaporation. Under MODFLOW 6, EVTA receives a routed negative recharge (`flow.sinks_sources.recharge.negative_to_evt`) or, in soil mode, the ETP the soil could not meet. The loaded ETP is ignored outside soil mode, with a warning (Drains and evapotranspiration at the top of the model).
- Drains. One drain in the first layer of every active cell that is not an ocean or stream constant-head cell. It sits at the ground surface or half a band depth below it. `solver.sink_fill` sets it to zero in closed depressions (Drains and evapotranspiration at the top of the model). In the code: `build_drain_stress_period_data`.
- Lakes, streams and barriers. LAK, SFR, MVR and HFB exist under MODFLOW 6 only. LAK and SFR are built after the drains, so that the drains that coincide with a stream reach can be removed and the drainage of the hillslope can be handed to the stream or lake it flows to. MVR is built last, because it names the packages it moves water between (Lakes and reservoirs, Streams and the water mover).

### Imposed heads and wells

CHD imposes the head of the ocean, stream and lateral boundaries on their cells. MODFLOW 6 takes one CHD package, so the three supports are merged, and a cell claimed twice keeps the head written last. WEL adds the rate of each well. Under the Newton formulation the code sets `auto_flow_reduce` on WEL, so that a well that dewaters its cell tapers its extraction instead of making the head oscillate across the threshold. MODFLOW 6 reads it as a fraction of the cell height, and the option is one value per package: it is the smallest fraction that keeps the interval within a tenth of the aquifer below the ground in every well cell, 0.1 when the top is the ground. In the code: `assemble_constant_head_stress_period_data`, `well_flow_reduce_fraction`.

### The solution: Newton and IMS

The code writes `NEWTON`, and adds `UNDER_RELAXATION` when `modflow6.runtime.mf6_newton_under_relaxation` is true. Newton is on by default, because every layer is convertible. The `UNDER_RELAXATION` of the Newton option damps the head of a cell that Newton would push below its bottom. It is not the under-relaxation of IMS, which adjusts the update factor of the outer iteration.

The code passes the closure criteria, the iteration limits and the optional `modflow6.runtime.mf6_linear_acceleration`, `modflow6.runtime.mf6_under_relaxation` and `modflow6.runtime.mf6_inner_rclose` to the IMS package. The complexity, `modflow6.runtime.mf6_ims_complexity`, defaults to `COMPLEX`. A configured `SIMPLE` complexity is promoted to `COMPLEX` when XT3D is on, and to at least `MODERATE` under Newton, because `SIMPLE` assumes a symmetric, well-conditioned matrix. Two combinations are refused:

- `modflow6.runtime.mf6_newton` and `modflow6.runtime.mf6_enable_rewet` together stop the run with `[HMPY.E405]` when the NPF package is built, because MODFLOW 6 forbids rewetting under the Newton formulation.
- Conjugate-gradient acceleration under Newton stops with `[HMPY.E406]`, because the Newton Jacobian is not symmetric and CG cannot solve it. The check runs before any grid is built. Use `BICGSTAB`, or leave `modflow6.runtime.mf6_linear_acceleration` unset.

In the code: `resolve_ims_complexity`.

## MODFLOW-NWT, package by package

`ModflowNwt` builds the FloPy model in this order, and `assemble_flopy_packages` adds the stress packages.

| Package | Written |
| --- | --- |
| NWT: the Newton solver and its closure | always |
| DIS: the structured grid and the steps of Time steps | always |
| CHD: head imposed on the transient ocean and side cells | if a transient boundary is active |
| BAS: active cells (`ibound`), starting heads, the no-flow sentinel | always |
| UPW: \(K\), \(K_z\), \(S_y\), \(S_s\) with upstream weighting | always |
| EVT | if an ETP or a negative recharge exists |
| RCH | if a recharge exists |
| DRN | if the `drainage` boundary is active |
| WEL | if a well exists |
| OC: head and budget at every step | always |
| LMT: the link file for MT3DMS | only when an MT3DMS process follows |

The static ocean and side boundaries are not CHD rows. They are cells with a negative `ibound` in BAS, which imposes the starting head on them. Four things differ from MODFLOW 6.

- The grid must be structured. NWT stops with `MODFLOW NWT requires a structured grid`. A `[mesh_catchment]` section does not change that: the solver keeps the grid it builds from the DEM.
- The unconfined law is the upstream-weighted UPW package [Niswonger et al., 2011], with a smoothing of the saturated thickness set by `modflownwt.runtime.nwt.thickfact`.
- EVT uses the topography. The code sets the EVT surface to the top lowered by `flow.sinks_sources.etp.surface_offset` and the extinction depth to `flow.sinks_sources.etp.extinction_depth`, with `nevtop` from `modflownwt.runtime.evt.nevtop`. The field `modflownwt.process_specific.exdp` is declared but nothing in the code reads it. When no ETP is active, a routed negative recharge uses an offset of 2 m and a depth of 1 m.
- No soil reservoir, lakes, streams or barriers. The checks listed under Limits stop the file.

In the code: `assemble_flopy_packages`.

## Wetting and drying

A cell dries when the head falls to its bottom. Under Newton, MODFLOW 6 smooths the saturated thickness near the bottom with a fraction of the thickness that it sets internally, and HydroModPy has no key for it [Langevin et al., 2017]. MODFLOW-NWT does the same in its `SAT_THICK` function, with the fraction read from `thickfact`[Niswonger et al., 2011]. The smoothing keeps the Newton step defined. It does not move the water table. The solvers differ in what they do next.

| Case | What happens | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MODFLOW 6, Newton | The cell stays in the equations. Conductance and storage go to zero smoothly, and `UNDER_RELAXATION` damps the head of a cell that Newton would push below its bottom. | `modflow6.runtime.mf6_newton`, `modflow6.runtime.mf6_newton_under_relaxation` |
| MODFLOW 6, standard formulation with rewet | The cell is rewetted by the NPF rewet test. Newton must be off. | `modflow6.runtime.mf6_enable_rewet` and the four `mf6_rewet_*` keys |
| MODFLOW-NWT | The cell stays in the equations. A dry cell is written with the dry-head value, and the reader of the results turns that value into a missing value. | `modflownwt.runtime.upw.iphdry`, `modflownwt.runtime.upw.hdry` |
| Boussinesq | The saturated thickness is bounded between zero and the cell thickness, without smoothing ((16)). | the runtime, see Boussinesq theory |

Rewetting is off unless `modflow6.runtime.mf6_enable_rewet` is true. When it is on, the NPF package gets `WETFCT`, `IWETIT` and `IHDWET` from the `mf6_rewet_*` keys, and an array `WETDRY` that is zero on inactive cells and the absolute value of `modflow6.runtime.mf6_rewet_wetdry` elsewhere. In the code: `resolve_rewet_npf_options`.

## MODFLOW 6 against MODFLOW-NWT

The same project file can run on either. The solver that runs is the first name in `simulation.process.solvers` of the `flow` process. `solver.backend` is the fallback when no process names one, and the key the compatibility checks of a file are run against. Write the same name in both. The settings live in `[modflownwt]` and `[modflow6]`. This page ranks neither solver.

| Topic | MODFLOW-NWT | MODFLOW 6 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Newton | always | on by default, can be switched off |
| Dry cells | no rewetting (`laywet = 0`) | rewetting off, refused with Newton |
| Non-orthogonal flux | not available | `XT3D`, automatic on irregular meshes |
| Output | head and budget at every step, stored per period | head at the last step, budget at every step, stored per period |
| Loaded ETP | drives `EVT` | ignored outside soil mode |
| Streams, lakes, barriers | refused | `SFR`, `LAK`, `HFB` |
| Restart, cyclic spin-up | refused | supported |

The vertical conductivity is a ratio on both, \(K_z = K / \beta\). The key is `modflownwt.process_specific.vka` for MODFLOW-NWT, with `layvka` set so that `vka` is read as a ratio, and `modflow6.process_specific.vka` for MODFLOW 6.

Sources and sinks. Recharge, wells, drains and constant heads are the same quantities in both. Two points differ.

- The loaded ETP is a sink in MODFLOW-NWT, with its surface at the top minus `flow.sinks_sources.etp.surface_offset` and the extinction depth `flow.sinks_sources.etp.extinction_depth`. MODFLOW 6 draws none outside soil mode, and says so. In soil mode it writes the ETP the soil left unmet (The daily soil reservoir).
- A negative recharge sent to `EVT` by `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.negative_to_evt` follows the same rule in both (Rain and evaporation: the forcing), with a different geometry: the model top and `modflow6.process_specific.evt_extinction_depth` in MODFLOW 6, the two `etp` keys above or fixed constants in MODFLOW-NWT.

Comparing the two. To compare the solvers, set the head test to the same value on both sides (`modflownwt.runtime.nwt.headtol` against the two `dvclose` keys): the residual tests do not measure the same thing. Validation lists the cases that run both solvers against the same closed-form solution, and runs both on the catchment of example 04, where their heads differ by less than a millimetre. Where the cell thickness changes from one cell to the next, the two conductances differ, and the computational top brings MODFLOW 6 back to MODFLOW-NWT: on the circular-island cases, whose top follows the ground over a flat bottom, both sit at the same distance from the closed form. Validation gives the thresholds and the reason for each. A threshold is a bound a test accepts, not a measured error, so it ranks nothing.

## The Boussinesq solver

The in-house solver writes one residual per triangle of a Gmsh mesh. It solves each stress period in `simulation.time.substeps_per_period` backward Euler steps. `flow.runtime_backend` picks the nonlinear solver, `auto` by default: the dense `local` engine up to 400 cells and the sparse `scipy_sparse` above; a dense engine asked by name stops on a larger mesh. `flow.surface_interaction_model` picks the closure for the water that reaches the surface. It builds recharge, wells, the side, stream and ocean imposed heads, and top drainage, and refuses the rest. Its flux between two cells uses the two cell centres only: on triangles far from equilateral it is not consistent, and the patch test of Validation shows the error that refinement does not remove. Its equations and closures are on Boussinesq theory.

## Transport coupling

A transport process attaches to the flow process that came before it. The planner binds each transport run to an earlier flow run of the right solver, in the order written in the file, and stops with `requires an earlier process using flow/<solver>` when there is none. The pairs are declared by each adapter as its `requires` attribute.

| Transport process | Needs the flow solver | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modflow6` (GWT) | `modflow6` | concentration in the flow field |
| `modflow6_prt` | `modflow6` | particle tracking, MODFLOW 6 PRT |
| `modpath` | `modflow_nwt` | particle tracking, MODPATH 6 |
| `mt3dms` | `modflow_nwt` | concentration, MT3DMS |

### MODFLOW 6 GWT

`Modflow6Transport` adds a GWT model to the MODFLOW 6 simulation of the flow run [Langevin et al., 2022]. It reuses the DISV grid and the `idomain` of the flow model, couples the two models with a `GWF6-GWT6` exchange, and gives GWT its own IMS with `BICGSTAB`, because advection makes the matrix non-symmetric. The transport solve is linear, so it uses the configured complexity and no Newton promotion. What HydroModPy sets in the GWT model:

- advection with the scheme of `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.scheme`;
- dispersion only when `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.disp_long` or `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.diffu_coeff` is above zero;
- the mobile storage with `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.porosity`. Without it, the code falls back on the specific yield and warns that this underestimates the pore volume, because the pore velocity is the Darcy flux divided by the porosity;
- decay of order zero or one, from `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.react_order` and `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.rate_decay`.

Recharge is the only source of solute. Its concentration travels as the `CONCENTRATION` auxiliary variable of RCHA, and the source and sink mixing package reads it. Constant-head cells and wells bring water in at concentration zero.

### MODFLOW 6 particle tracking

`modflow6_prt` builds a PRT model on the same flow model. It needs the cell-by-cell velocity that `modflow6.runtime.save_specific_discharge` writes. Its keys are in [transport].

### MODFLOW-NWT: MODPATH and MT3DMS

MODPATH builds a MODPATH 6 input from the NWT run and stops if the flow model is not MODFLOW-NWT. MT3DMS needs the link file that the LMT package writes. NWT adds LMT only when an MT3DMS process is planned after it. The file name is `modflownwt.runtime.lmt.output_file_name`. In the code: `_requires_mt3dms_link`.

## Assumptions

- Flow is saturated, in one phase, and the head is the only unknown. Water above the water table is not modelled: the code writes no UZF package, and the soil reservoir of The daily soil reservoir is a separate daily model that hands a recharge to the solver.
- Every layer is convertible: it can be confined or unconfined from one step to the next.
- The horizontal conductivity is isotropic. The vertical one is the horizontal one divided by one ratio for the whole model, or a per-cell \(K_z\) field.

## Limits

The capability matrix is generated on Solvers. The refusals, with their messages, are these.

- Grid. MODFLOW-NWT works on the structured grid only. The Boussinesq solver works on Gmsh triangles only, and a dense runtime asked by name on a mesh of more than 400 cells.
- Boundaries. Lakes, reservoirs, SFR and barriers need MODFLOW 6. The `stream` boundary needs MODFLOW 6 or Boussinesq. When `solver.backend` names `modflow_nwt`, the file is refused when it is read if it asks for `flow.active_bc` with `sfr`, `lake`, `reservoir` or `stream`, for flow barriers or a dam cutoff wall, or for a head initial condition of type `spinup_cyclic`. `does not support the 'sfr' boundary` is the start of the message for the first case, and `does not support flow barriers / dam cutoff walls (HFB); they require the 'modflow6' backend.` is the whole message for barriers. An unstructured mesh stops the build with `MODFLOW NWT requires a structured grid`.
- Soil reservoir. `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] is wired to MODFLOW 6 only` stops a file that asks for it with another solver.
- ETP. MODFLOW 6 draws no ETP outside soil mode, and only logs a warning. Boussinesq rejects it.
- Hotstart and cyclic spin-up. `flow.restart_from` and a cyclic spin-up need MODFLOW 6, the only solver that declares the two capabilities.
- Newton. Newton with rewet (`HMPY.E405`) and Newton with conjugate gradients (`HMPY.E406`) are refused (The solution: Newton and IMS).
- Not represented. The code writes no unsaturated-zone package (UZF), no variable-density package (BUY), no subsidence package (CSUB), and no GHB or RIV package.

## Parameters of this page

The keys of the solver options of this page. The keys of each transport process are on its reference card.

[[simulation.process]]

`solvers = ‹list of string›` : Ordered list of active flow solver names. required at least 1 item
**Path**: `simulation.process.solvers`
**More**: At least one solver is required for flow processes.
**Accepted**: list of string
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)

[solver.backend]

`name = ‹string›` : Name under which a plugin registered its flow solver. required only if backend = "custom"
**Path**: `solver.backend.name`
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: backend = "custom"

`# backend = "modflow6"` : Flow solver of the run: MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW-NWT, Boussinesq or a plugin.
**Path**: `solver.backend.backend`
**Values**:
- `"modflow6"` : Select the MODFLOW 6 flow backend.
- `"modflow_nwt"` : Select the MODFLOW-NWT flow backend.
- `"boussinesq"` : Select the Boussinesq flow backend.
- `"custom"` : Plugin-registered flow backend identified by a free-form name.
**Accepted**: "modflow6" | "modflow_nwt" | "boussinesq" | "custom"

[simulation.time]

`# substeps_per_period = 1` : Number of solver time steps within each stress period, the one knob that buys transient accuracy. >= 1 dev
**Path**: `simulation.time.substeps_per_period`
**More**: The default of 1 integrates a whole period in a single backward-Euler step, which is not a neutral choice: on a seasonally recharged hillslope drained by DRN cells it moves the monthly discharge by 4 to 28 % against a refined run, across the whole plausible bedrock range, and a calibration scored on discharge absorbs that into the fitted parameters. The right count compares the aquifer response time `tau = L^2 S / (K b)` with the period length, and the solver cost is linear in it; 30 gives daily steps inside monthly periods. Consumed by the MODFLOW backends as DIS NSTP / TDIS nstp, and by the Boussinesq backend, which solves each period in as many backward-Euler steps of equal length. Every solver stores one result per period: the head at the end of the period and each flux as the mean of its steps, weighted by their length.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)

[flow]

`# flow_regime = "transient"` : Whether the flow is solved as one equilibrium state or through time over the stress periods of [simulation.time].
**Path**: `flow.flow_regime`
**See**: simulation.time
**Values**:
- `"steady"` : Solves one equilibrium state, with no storage term: one stress period over the whole [simulation.time] window, whatever its step_value says, with the forcings averaged over the window.
- `"transient"` : Solves the heads through time; it starts from the state [flow.ic] gives.
**Accepted**: "steady" | "transient"
**Example**: `"steady"`, `"transient"`

`# first_period_steady = true` : For transient flow, mark the first solver stress period as steady-state.
**Path**: `flow.first_period_steady`
**More**: Ignored for steady flow, where all solver periods are steady.
**Accepted**: true | false
**Example**: `true`, `false`

[modflow6.runtime]

`# mf6_ats = false` : Enable MODFLOW 6 adaptive time stepping (ATS) on transient periods. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_ats`
**More**: Each period starts at the step simulation.time.substeps_per_period asked for and MF6 subdivides below it only where the solver cannot converge (e.g. littoral wet/dry under Newton); it never grows past that step, so turning ATS on cannot coarsen a run. When on, OC saves per period end so the extraction still sees one record per period. Default off (baseline).
**Accepted**: true | false

`# mf6_newton = true` : Enable the MODFLOW 6 Newton-Raphson formulation. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_newton`
**More**: Catchment cells are always convertible (unconfined), so Newton with under-relaxation is the robust default. Unlike MODFLOW-NWT, it builds the horizontal conductance from the full cell thickness times the upstream saturation. The grid MODFLOW 6 reads therefore has a computational top that gives every cell of the top layer the same thickness, so that this conductance is the one of NWT; the ground stays in every package and in the run store.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# mf6_newton_under_relaxation = true` : Enable MODFLOW 6 Newton under-relaxation when mf6_newton is true. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_newton_under_relaxation`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# mf6_ims_complexity = "COMPLEX"` : IMS complexity preset for MODFLOW 6: SIMPLE, MODERATE, or COMPLEX. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_ims_complexity`
**Values**:
- `"SIMPLE"`no explanation
- `"MODERATE"`no explanation
- `"COMPLEX"`no explanation
**Accepted**: "SIMPLE" | "MODERATE" | "COMPLEX"

`# mf6_outer_dvclose = 0.0001` : IMS outer-iteration head-change convergence criterion. > 0 expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_outer_dvclose`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

`# mf6_inner_dvclose = 0.0001` : IMS inner-iteration head-change convergence criterion. > 0 expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_inner_dvclose`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

`# mf6_inner_rclose = ‹number›` : IMS inner-iteration flow-residual closure (L^3/T in run units). > 0 expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_inner_rclose`
**More**: None keeps the complexity-preset default.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

`# mf6_linear_acceleration = ‹"CG" | "BICGSTAB"›` : IMS linear acceleration: CG for symmetric matrices, BICGSTAB for the non-symmetric Newton formulation. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_linear_acceleration`
**More**: None keeps the preset default.
**Values**:
- `"CG"`no explanation
- `"BICGSTAB"`no explanation
**Accepted**: "CG" | "BICGSTAB"

`# mf6_under_relaxation = ‹"NONE" | "SIMPLE" | "COOLEY" | "DBD"›` : IMS non-linear under-relaxation scheme. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_under_relaxation`
**More**: DBD is recommended with Newton. None keeps the preset default.
**Values**:
- `"NONE"`no explanation
- `"SIMPLE"`no explanation
- `"COOLEY"`no explanation
- `"DBD"`no explanation
**Accepted**: "NONE" | "SIMPLE" | "COOLEY" | "DBD"

`# mf6_enable_rewet = ‹true | false›` : Enable NPF cell rewetting. expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_enable_rewet`
**More**: When left to None, HydroModPy keeps rewetting disabled unless explicitly enabled.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# mf6_rewet_wetdry = 0.1` : MF6 NPF WETDRY threshold used when rewetting is active. > 0 expert
**Path**: `modflow6.runtime.mf6_rewet_wetdry`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

[modflownwt.runtime.nwt]

`# headtol = 0.0001` : Head closure criterion for the NWT nonlinear solver. expert
**Path**: `modflownwt.runtime.nwt.headtol`
**Accepted**: number

`# fluxtol = 0.005787037037037037` : Flux closure criterion of the NWT nonlinear solver, in m3/s: HydroModPy writes MODFLOW-NWT in seconds. expert
**Path**: `modflownwt.runtime.nwt.fluxtol`
**More**: The default is the 500 m3/day of the NWT manual. A value of 500 here would be 500 m3/s, a bound no model reaches.
**Accepted**: number

`# thickfact = 1e-05` : Fraction of the cell thickness over which MODFLOW-NWT smooths the saturated thickness, and so the conductance and the storage, to zero near the bottom and the top of a cell (THICKFACT of the NWT package). [0, 0.5[ expert
**Path**: `modflownwt.runtime.nwt.thickfact`
**More**: Dimensionless.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 0.5[ (refused outside)

[modflownwt.runtime.upw]

`# iphdry = 1` : UPW dry-cell head output flag (IPHDRY). expert
**Path**: `modflownwt.runtime.upw.iphdry`
**Accepted**: integer

`# hdry = -100.0` : UPW dry-cell head value (HDRY). expert
**Path**: `modflownwt.runtime.upw.hdry`
**Accepted**: number

[modflownwt.process_specific]

`# vka = 1.0` : Vertical hydraulic conductivity control passed to the UPW package (VKA). expert
**Path**: `modflownwt.process_specific.vka`
**Accepted**: number

[modflow6.process_specific]

`# vka = 1.0` : Uniform vertical anisotropy ratio kh/kv (dimensionless, > 0); k33 = k / vka. > 0 expert
**Path**: `modflow6.process_specific.vka`
**More**: Default 1.0 is vertically isotropic. For spatial control declare a per-cell 'Kv' flow parameter instead, which is mutually exclusive with a non-unit vka and is a direct conductivity, never a mode-switched value. Vertical anisotropy is grid-aligned and needs no XT3D; a horizontal K22 field or an angle (not exposed here) would auto-activate XT3D.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)

[calibration]

`# reject_water_budget_above = ‹number›` : Percent water-balance discrepancy past which a trial is rejected instead of scored. % >= 0
**Path**: `calibration.reject_water_budget_above`
**More**: The solver reports the figure on every run; unset, it is recorded and nothing acts on it, so a run at twelve per cent is ranked beside one that closed even though part of the water it routed came from nowhere. There is no default because there is no universal value: a steady solve on a coarse mesh closes to a fraction of a per cent, a transient one with a lake and a routed network legitimately sits higher.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: %

Lines generated from the models, as in the reference. Open one for its card.

# From a zone map to the cells

A property such as \(K\) is given per zone of a map: geology classes, bands, rings, or the zones of a raster. The solver needs one value per cell and per layer. This page gives the rule that turns the first into the second, what that rule means for the conductivity, and a worked example. The keys of a value per zone are in [flow.param].

## The rule

A parameter with one value is spread over every cell. A parameter that points to a zone map through its `field_spatial_id` is mapped in three steps.

1. Sample the cell. Each cell \(c\) is covered by a regular set of sample points, \(n_s\) per axis of the cell. A point takes the zone that contains it.
1. Count the zones. \(F_{c,z}\) is the share of the points of \(c\) that fall in zone \(z\), among the points that fall in a zone. A point outside every zone of a geology map or of a raster map is left out of the count.
1. Average, then scale with depth. The value of the cell in layer \(j\) is
(20)\[ u_{c,j} = f(d_j)\,\sum_{z} F_{c,z}\,v_z , \qquad \sum_z F_{c,z} = 1 , \]

with \(v_z\) the value of zone \(z\) and \(f(d_j)\) the depth factor (15) at the depth of the middle of layer \(j\). A parameter with one value \(v\) gives \(u_{c,j} = f(d_j)\,v\).

\(F_{c,z}\) is an estimate of the share of the area of \(c\) that lies in \(z\). Its resolution is \(1 / n_s^2\) of the cell: a zone that covers less than that may get no point. The same rule applies to every property, \(K\), \(S_y\), \(S_s\) or the porosity. The two MODFLOW solvers apply it per layer; the Boussinesq solver applies it once, at the depth \(d = 0\), because it has one layer. In the code: `FieldParam.to_mesh_field`.

A zone of the map with no value in the parameter stops the run, with a message that names the missing keys. A cell where no point falls in any zone gets \(\sum_z F_{c,z} = 0\), so a value of zero, and a zero \(K\) on an active cell is refused.

## What the rule means for the conductivity

(20) is an arithmetic mean weighted by area, the upper bound of the equivalent conductivity of a cell cut by several zones; the harmonic mean is the lower bound, and a random mix lies between [Renard and de Marsily, 1997]. A cell that holds a thin layer of low \(K\) across the flow therefore conducts more in the model than in the ground.

Between two cells, the conductance (18) joins the two cell values in series. A contrast that follows the cell faces is represented in series; a contrast inside a cell is represented in parallel.

## A worked example

Three cells of a row, two zones, \(v_A = 10^{-5}\) m/s and \(v_B = 10^{-7}\) m/s, no depth factor. The interface between the zones crosses the middle cell.

| Cell | \(F_{c,A}\) | \(F_{c,B}\) | \(u_c\) by (20) | harmonic mean, for comparison |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | \(1.0 \times 10^{-5}\) m/s | \(1.0 \times 10^{-5}\) m/s |
| 2 | 0.5 | 0.5 | \(5.05 \times 10^{-6}\) m/s | \(1.98 \times 10^{-7}\) m/s |
| 3 | 0 | 1 | \(1.0 \times 10^{-7}\) m/s | \(1.0 \times 10^{-7}\) m/s |

For a flow along the row, across the interface, the middle cell conducts about 25 times more than its harmonic mean. Refining the mesh at the interface, or aligning the cell faces with it, removes the mixed cell.

Fig. 27 The example above, three rows of it, run through the code. Left: the sample points of each cell (\(n_s = 8\) per axis, the default) take the colour of their zone, and \(F_{c,A}\) counts them. Right: the value `FieldParam.to_mesh_field` gives each cell (dots) lies on the arithmetic mean; the harmonic mean (dashed) is the value for a flow across the boundary. Look at the middle cells: \(5.05 \times 10^{-6}\) m/s against \(1.98 \times 10^{-7}\) m/s.

## Assumptions

- A cell holds one value of each property per layer.
- The zone of a point is the zone of the map that contains it; the map is not smoothed.
- The depth factor is the same function in every zone.

## Limits

- Arithmetic mean only. The aggregation is `weighted_average`; no geometric or harmonic option exists.
- A sampled share. \(F_{c,z}\) is counted on \(n_s\) points per axis, not computed from the exact intersection of the cell and the zone.
- Same rule on every grid. A coarse structured grid and a fine irregular mesh mix the zones differently, so two runs that share a zone map do not share their cell values. Compare them on the same grid, or report the grid with the result.

# XT3D on irregular meshes

The two-point flux of (17) is exact on a grid whose connections are perpendicular to the faces, for a conductivity that is the same in every horizontal direction. On irregular cells it is not. This page gives the error, the correction MODFLOW 6 offers for it, XT3D [Provost et al., 2017], and the rule HydroModPy follows to turn it on. The angle of a connection is defined on 4. Flow between two cells, and the angle.

## The error of the two-point flux

The flux through the face shared by cells \(n\) and \(m\) is the component of the Darcy flux along the normal of the face, \(\mathbf{n}_{nm}\cdot\mathbf{q} = -K\,\mathbf{n}_{nm}\cdot\nabla h\) for an isotropic conductivity. Write the unit vector of the connection, \(\hat{\mathbf d}_{nm} = \mathbf{d}_{nm} / \lVert\mathbf{d}_{nm}\rVert\), as \(\cos\varphi_{nm}\,\mathbf{n}_{nm} + \sin\varphi_{nm}\,\mathbf{t}_{nm}\), with \(\mathbf{t}_{nm}\) the unit vector along the face. Then

(26)\[ \mathbf{n}_{nm}\cdot\nabla h = \frac{\hat{\mathbf d}_{nm}\cdot\nabla h}{\cos\varphi_{nm}} - \tan\varphi_{nm}\;\mathbf{t}_{nm}\cdot\nabla h . \]

The two heads \(h_n\) and \(h_m\) give the first term only. The two-point conductance \(G_{nm}\) keeps it and drops the second, the head gradient along the face times \(\tan\varphi_{nm}\): zero on an orthogonal connection, 0.27 of the tangential gradient at 15 degrees, 0.58 at 30 degrees, 1 at 45 degrees. A conductivity that differs between two horizontal directions, or whose axes are turned, adds a term of the same kind, even on an orthogonal grid. The vertical \(K_z\) is aligned with the layers and needs no XT3D.

## What XT3D computes

XT3D writes the flux through each face with the full head gradient, estimated from the heads of both cells and of their neighbours, so the tangential term is in the balance [Provost et al., 2017]. The price is a wider stencil and a matrix that is no longer symmetric.

On the validation case `dupuit_uniform_recharge_1d` run on irregular triangles, the golden reference of the regression test `test_xt3d_irregular_tri_fast_regression` records a head RMSE of 0.211 m without XT3D and 0.0077 m with it, a factor of 27. The test fails if the factor falls below 10 or the RMSE with XT3D rises above 0.016 m, twice the measurement.

Fig. 37 Left: the share of the tangential gradient that the two-point flux drops, \(\tan\varphi_{nm}\) from (26), with the 30° angle of the rule below. Right: the head errors of the golden reference, read from the test folder at build time.

## When HydroModPy turns it on

The code decides once per run, in this order:

| Case | XT3D | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modflow6.runtime.mf6_enable_xt3d` is `true` or `false` | as written | your value wins; the code logs a warning when the checks below disagree |
| Structured grid | off | the connections are orthogonal and the conductivity isotropic |
| Horizontal conductivity anisotropic or turned | on | the tensor term of The error of the two-point flux |
| More than 5 % of the connections above 30 degrees, or a 95th percentile of \(\varphi_{nm}\) above 30 degrees | on | the dropped term reaches 0.58 of the tangential gradient on a share of the faces |
| Otherwise | off | the dropped term stays small, XT3D would add cost only |

The two limits are the constants `_NONORTH_FRAC_GT30_TRIGGER` and `_NONORTH_P95_TRIGGER_DEG`. The anisotropy row does not fire today: the `NPF` package receives only a horizontal \(K\) and a vertical \(K_z\), so the horizontal plane is isotropic. The default Voronoi dual of a Gmsh mesh is orthogonal by construction (3. The Voronoi dual), so XT3D stays off there; the triangles kept as cells with `modflow6.sgrid.grid_dual` are the usual case where it turns on.

When XT3D is on, a `SIMPLE` IMS preset is promoted to `COMPLEX`, because `SIMPLE` assumes a symmetric matrix (The solution: Newton and IMS).

## The same case on two grids

The circular-island validation case on a structured `DIS` grid (left) and on irregular triangles (right), where the rule above turns XT3D on. Drag the handle to compare.

Structured DISIrregular triangles, XT3D on
One case, two MODFLOW 6 grids. On the triangles the connections are not perpendicular to the faces, which is what turns XT3D on.

## Assumptions

- The conductivity is isotropic in the horizontal plane: `NPF` receives only a horizontal \(K\) and a vertical \(K_z\).
- The angle of a connection is measured in the plan; the layers are an extrusion, so the vertical connections are orthogonal.

## Limits

- MODFLOW 6 only. MODFLOW-NWT runs on structured grids only. The Boussinesq solver has no correction for skewed cells.
- No horizontal anisotropy input. The anisotropy branch of the rule never fires.
- Cost. XT3D widens the stencil and makes the matrix non-symmetric. On a mesh near the trigger, a sweep of many runs pays for it on every run.

## Parameters of this page

# Time alignment of outputs and observations

A run writes one value per stress period. An observation chronicle has its own dates. Before a simulated value and an observed one can be compared, both must mean the same thing on the same interval. This page gives the one convention every reader of a run follows: a stamp closes its period. A flux read at a stamp is the mean over the period before it; a state is the value at the stamp. How the inputs are put on the periods is on Rain and evaporation: the forcing.

## A stamp closes its period

The periods are the intervals \([b_k, b_{k+1})\) of (1). Every solver stamps a period at its end: the time axis of a run is the start of the run plus the elapsed solver time. January 2000 of a monthly run is stamped 2000-02-01. A steady run over 2000 to 2002 has one period, stamped 2003-01-01. The stamp of period \(k\) is therefore \(b_{k+1}\).

What a stamp stands for depends on the quantity. The rule is read from the CF `cell_methods` (`mean` or `point`) of the field in the field registry of the code, or, for a calibration variable the field registry does not hold, from a table of the code. A name that nothing declares is a mean.

| Method | Quantity | The value stamped \(b_{k+1}\) stands for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mean` | recharge, drain and seepage fluxes, discharge, runoff, lake inflow and outflow | the mean of the flux over \([b_k, b_{k+1})\) |
| `point` | head, water table elevation and depth, seepage mask, lake level and volume, soil stores | the state at the instant \(b_{k+1}\) |

For a steady first period, the head is the equilibrium under the forcing of that period, stamped at its end.

### A period cut into time steps

A solver can cut a period into time steps: `simulation.time.substeps_per_period`, adaptive time stepping on MODFLOW 6, or the internal steps of the Boussinesq PETSc closures. The run still stores one value per period, the same way on MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW-NWT and Boussinesq:

- a state is the value at the last step, which ends at the stamp;
- a flux is the mean of the fluxes of the steps, each weighted by its length: recharge, wells, drains, fixed heads, river, stream and lake exchanges, storage and the release at the surface, cell by cell and in the budget tables, and the listing water balance of the period.

With one step a period, that mean is the flux of the step, unchanged. Each step closes its water balance, so the change of storage between the two stamps closes the balance of the period with these means.

Fig. 59 A flux (top) and a state (bottom) on four monthly periods, read by `period_mean_on_index` and `period_point_on_index`. The flux of a stamp is the mean of the period that ends there. The state is read at the stamp, here on a window centred on it because the daily record is finer than the run.

In the code: `time_method_for`.

## An observation on the periods

An observation is put on the periods by the same rule, so a simulated value and an observed one mean the same thing. Observations are stamped at the start of what they average: a daily mean at its day, a monthly mean at its month start.

A mean quantity. Period \(k\) takes the mean of the observations stamped in \([b_k, b_{k+1})\). A period with none takes the last observation stamped at or before \(b_k\) when the interval that observation stands for covers the whole period:

(44)\[ b_{k+1} \leq t_h + \Delta t_o , \]

where \(t_h\) is the stamp of that observation and \(\Delta t_o\) the step of its chronicle. That is a monthly mean on a daily run. Otherwise the period has no value, and a gap in the chronicle stays a gap.

A state. A chronicle finer than the run is averaged on a window centred on the stamp, reaching halfway to the neighbouring stamps. A chronicle as coarse as the run, or coarser, gives the sample nearest the stamp, within the step of the run. Averaging a state over \([b_k, b_{k+1})\) would compare it with a value half a period earlier.

A steady period. One stamp does not say where the period starts. The scorer takes the start of the first period from the time grid of the run, so a steady discharge is compared with the mean of the gauge over the window of the run, not with its last day. A steady head is still read at its stamp.

In the code: `observed_on_periods`.

## A series derived on the periods

A series the run derives from a forcing, such as the catchment discharge built from a drain budget plus the runoff (8. Runoff is not recharge), takes the mean of the samples of each period and holds no value: a period with no sample is a gap, never the previous value. This is the one difference with an observation of the same kind. On the daily record of 1, 3 and 5 mm/day for January, February and March with the days of February removed, the three periods read 1, a gap, and 5.

In the code: `period_mean_on_index`.

## Assumptions

- A stamp closes its period: a flux is a period mean, a state is a value at the stamp. A period cut into time steps stores the mean of its step fluxes and the state of its last step.
- An observation is stamped at the start of what it averages.
- An observation of a mean quantity stands for one step of its chronicle.

## Limits

- A chronicle with gaps has a step taken from the median of its spacings: a period beyond that step after the last observation stays empty.
- A state between two coarse stamps is not interpolated: it takes the nearest sample within the step of the run, or no value.

# Validation

Each check below is a test of `tests/validation/`. It compares a computation with a reference that HydroModPy did not produce: a closed-form solution, a published MODFLOW 6 example, a manufactured solution, or a parameter that a calibration must find again.

For every check the page gives the reference and its equations, the threshold with the size of the signal it is read against, the value the last recorded run measured, the outcome, and the date and commit of that run. A skipped test is shown as skipped: it proves nothing. Where a threshold lets a known discrepancy through, the case says so in a warning box at its top.

The measures come from a results snapshot committed next to this page, `docs/source/theory/validation_results.json`. When the site is deployed, the results the nightly jobs uploaded for the branch, if any, replace older ones. Each case gives the date and commit of the run its numbers come from. “When the checks run” below lists the jobs, read from the workflow files, and the checks that no job runs.

53 test files, 78 test functions, 35 benchmark cases. The results snapshot holds 190 test results from 2 runs (2026-10-12 to 2026-10-13): 190 pass.

## When the checks run

Read from `.github/workflows/`. A job runs a file when one of its paths holds it and its marker expression accepts the markers of the file. A test marked `petsc` is skipped where petsc4py is not installed. The nightly jobs upload what they measured. The deployed page lays the latest nightly results of its branch over the snapshot committed with the documentation.

| Job | When | Selects | petsc4py |

## Case by solver

Each cell is the largest share of its threshold that a metric used in the last recorded run of that solver: 50 % means the worst metric sat at half its threshold. A metric that must stay above its threshold counts the share of the margin it used between its ideal value and the threshold. skipped and not measured prove nothing. A cross marks a failure. gap marks a known discrepancy that the threshold lets through; the section of the case explains it. other gathers the solvers outside these columns and the tests that name none. The columns are `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`, `modflow6_irregular_tri`, `modflow6_voronoi`, `boussinesq` and `boussinesq_local`.

## Closed-form solutions, steady state

### Steady Boussinesq circular-island piecewise-K case

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: `modflow6_voronoi`

Known gap. MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual sits 0.12 to 0.17 m below the reference inside 120 m (radial RMSE 0.12 m). Two errors add up there. The K zone boundaries (70 m and 140 m) pass through node rings, so those cells straddle two zones and take an area-weighted K: without Newton the same input files give 0.076 m, the heads 0.08 to 0.11 m too low inside 120 m and 0.05 m too high on the 140 m ring. Under Newton, the saturation of the upstream cell lowers them further, first order on rings 10 to 30 m apart. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM, and the full-thickness weighting of the Newton conductance raised the heads, which offset the straddled zones: 0.056 m. MODFLOW 6 now reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, and that offset is gone.

Compared with: steady radial Boussinesq solution with concentric piecewise `K`.

\[ \frac{1}{r}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}r}\left(r\,K(r)\,H\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}r}\right)+R=0 \]
\[ U=H^2,\qquad U(r)=U(a)+R\int_r^a \frac{s}{K(s)}\,\mathrm{d}s \]

Why these thresholds

- Thresholds of `boussinesq`: Twice the error measured with PETSc (SNESVI obstacle) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.031 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.044 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.96 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m with a node ring on each K break (70 and 140 m) and on the coast, and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. The ring mesh it replaces (16 sectors cut along one diagonal, half of its ocean triangles capped at the sea floor) read 0.22 m.
- Thresholds of `boussinesq_local`: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine (scipy_sparse on 3155 cells) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.031 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.044 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.96 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m with a node ring on each K break (70 and 140 m) and on the coast, and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. The ring mesh it replaces (16 sectors cut along one diagonal, half of its ocean triangles capped at the sea floor) read 0.22 m.
- Thresholds of `modflow6`: Twice the error measured on the 10 m grid: radial RMSE 0.0282 m, max error 0.0546 m, spread 0.0817 m, and half the measured freeboard of 0.910 m. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell of the layer the same thickness, so its Newton conductance is the one of MODFLOW-NWT, and the two sit at the same distance from the reference (NWT 0.0284 m). What is left is the error of the grid. On a 5 m grid the RMSE falls to 0.0166 m and the max error to 0.0349 m, for MF6 and NWT alike; the spread stays at 0.083 m and the freeboard drops to 0.755 m. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM and the RMSE 0.111 m.
- Thresholds of `modflow6_voronoi`: Measured values with a 10 % margin: radial RMSE 0.1205 m, max error 0.173 m, freeboard 1.99 m. Twice the azimuthal spread of 5.2e-5 m: every cell of the coast ring holds the sea level, so the rings are symmetric. The run reads a 1 m raster whose shoreline lies 1 m inside the coast ring (config_modflow6_voronoi.toml). The profile is read on the node rings (5 m bins). The freeboard is read on the land surface the run was given, at the 196 m ring. This case cannot see the DEM-top bias come back, since that bias lowered its error; the Cartesian islands and tests/integration/test_the_computational_top_changes_only_the_mf6_grid.py do.
- Radial head-profile RMSE: `modflow_nwt` allows 0.35, 7 times the 0.048 of `boussinesq`. No reason is written for this difference.
- Radial head-profile RMSE: `modflow6_irregular_tri` allows 0.35, 7 times the 0.048 of `boussinesq`. No reason is written for this difference.
- Radial head-profile max abs error: `modflow_nwt` allows 0.7, 11 times the 0.063 of `boussinesq`. No reason is written for this difference.
- Radial head-profile max abs error: `modflow6_irregular_tri` allows 0.7, 11 times the 0.063 of `boussinesq`. No reason is written for this difference.
- Azimuthal spread: `modflow_nwt` allows 0.35, 3182 times the 0.00011 of `modflow6_voronoi`. No reason is written for this difference.
- Azimuthal spread: `modflow6_irregular_tri` allows 0.35, 3182 times the 0.00011 of `modflow6_voronoi`. No reason is written for this difference.

Why these thresholds

- Thresholds of `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 8.3e-3 m, max error 1.1e-2 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
- Thresholds of `boussinesq`: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 6.7e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and read a RMSE of 9.4e-2 m. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
- Thresholds of `boussinesq_local`: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 6.7e-05 m, max error 0.00011 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The run goes through the launcher. Before 2026-10-09 the strip had one diagonal everywhere and read a RMSE of 9.4e-2 m. The launcher stores one profile per column and the loader tiles it: the row spread is zero by construction. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
- Thresholds of `modflow6_irregular_tri`: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 1.2e-2 m, max error 1.7e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The K zones change on column faces. ### Steady Boussinesq hillslope-interception benchmark

pass boussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: the exact steady free-boundary solution under Dupuit. Below the emergence point `x_e` the head is the land surface and seeps out; above it all the recharge flows through the aquifer and the water table meets the surface tangentially at `x_e` (322.4 m here).

\[ R\left(x_e-x_{\min}\right)=K\,S\left(z_{\mathrm{top}}(x_e)-z_b\right),\qquad z_{\mathrm{top}}(x)=z_{\mathrm{toe}}+S\left(L-x\right) \]
\[ \left(h-z_b\right)^2=\left(z_{\mathrm{top}}(x_e)-z_b\right)^2+\frac{R}{K}\left[\left(x_e-x_{\min}\right)^2-\left(x-x_{\min}\right)^2\right]\quad (x<x_e),\qquad h=z_{\mathrm{top}}\quad (x\ge x_e) \]

### Steady sloping-substratum constant-thickness case

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: exact steady profile `H(x) = z_b(x) + b*` with `b* = 8 m`.

\[ H(x)=z_b(x)+b^\ast,\qquad z_b(x)=z_{b,0}+\Delta z_b\left(1-\frac{x-x_{\min}}{L}\right) \]
\[ q=-K\,b^\ast\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}x}=K\,b^\ast\,S_0,\qquad S_0=\frac{z_b(x_{\min})-z_b(x_{\max})}{L} \]

### Steady sloping-substratum fixed-head case

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: steady no-recharge Boussinesq relation on `b(x)` above a linear substratum, solved through its implicit integral law.

\[ q=K\,b\left(S_0-\frac{\mathrm{d}b}{\mathrm{d}x}\right),\qquad S_0=-\frac{\mathrm{d}z_b}{\mathrm{d}x} \]
\[ x-x_{\min}=\int_{b_w}^{b(x)} \frac{K\,\eta}{K\,\beta\,\eta-q}\,\mathrm{d}\eta,\qquad \beta=S_0,\qquad H(x)=z_b(x)+b(x) \]

Why these thresholds

- Thresholds of `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 1.9e-2 m, max error 2.9e-2 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells. The max error keeps its previous bound of 0.05 m, still 1.75 times the measurement. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
- Thresholds of `boussinesq`: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 0.00012 m, max error 0.00042 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
- Thresholds of `boussinesq_local`: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 0.00012 m, max error 0.00042 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
- Thresholds of `modflow6_irregular_tri`: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 2.1e-2 m, max error 3.1e-2 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

### Steady circular-island 2D case using the ocean boundary condition

pass, known gap end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Known gap: `modflow6_voronoi`

Known gap. MODFLOW 6 on the Voronoi dual sits up to 0.08 m below the reference inside 120 m (radial RMSE 0.067 m), where MODFLOW-NWT on the Cartesian grid sits 0.050 m away. MODFLOW 6 reads a computational top that gives every cell the same thickness, so the full-thickness weighting of its Newton conductance is gone. What is left is the saturation of the upstream cell, first order on 625 cells whose node rings are 10 to 30 m apart: without Newton the same input files give 0.003 m, the heads within 4 mm of the reference.

Compared with: steady radial Dupuit-Boussinesq solution with fixed coastal head.

\[ \frac{1}{r}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}r}\left(r\,K\,H\,\frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}r}\right)+R=0 \]
\[ H(r)^2=H(a)^2+\frac{R}{2K}\left(a^2-r^2\right) \]
\[ h(r)=z_b+\sqrt{\left(h_{\mathrm{sea}}-z_b\right)^2+\frac{R}{2K}\left(a^2-r^2\right)} \]

Why these thresholds

- Thresholds of `boussinesq`: Twice the error measured with PETSc (SNESVI obstacle) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.033 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.055 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.90 m. PETSc and the default engine agree to 1e-3 m. The mesh has near-equilateral triangles of 10 m, a node ring on the coast and one ring of ocean triangles held at the sea level. Until 2026-10-09 it was a ring mesh of 18 sectors cut along one diagonal: there the two-point flux sat 0.25 m high with the reference imposed beyond 180 m, and refining that mesh made it worse (+1.1 m at 1476 and 5832 cells), while near-equilateral meshes converge (+0.08, +0.07, +0.02 m at 257, 886, 3147 cells). Half of its ocean triangles were capped at the sea floor (-1 m), a coastal sink that hid most of that bias.
- Thresholds of `boussinesq_local`: Twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine (scipy_sparse on 3147 cells) on the triangles themselves, the reference at each centroid: radial RMSE 0.024 m, max error 0.033 m, spread of the error in a 10 m bin 0.055 m, and half the measured freeboard of 1.90 m. - Thresholds of `modflow6`: Twice the error measured on the 10 m grid: radial RMSE 0.0499 m, max error 0.0921 m, spread 0.112 m, and half the measured freeboard of 0.787 m. The freeboard is read on the land surface the run was given, at the 196 m ring. Until 2026-10-12 the top was the DEM and the RMSE 0.102 m. Twice the error would let that bias back unnoticed, hence the 10 % margin.

- Thresholds of `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 5.6e-3 m, max error 6.6e-3 m. Both upstream-weight the saturated thickness between cells, a first-order scheme: refining the grid by 2 halves the error. The heads are posed where the model holds them, at the centres of the boundary cells. The row spread bound is 0.1 times the MODFLOW 6 head closure (1e-4 m).
- Thresholds of `boussinesq`: Twice the error measured with PETSc VI on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 3.3e-05 m, max error 5.5e-05 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: PETSc reads below 1e-14 m; the bound is 1e-8 m.
- Thresholds of `boussinesq_local`: Twice the error measured with the default local engine on 40 columns; PETSc and the local engine agree to 1e-8 m: RMSE 3.3e-05 m, max error 5.5e-05 m. The strip splits each 10 m square into two right triangles, the diagonal alternating like a checkerboard. On it the solver reproduces the h^2 profile at the triangle centroids to 1e-8 m (checked cell by cell with recharge), far below the MODFLOW band of this case. What is left comes from the column average of two triangles, centroids at dx/3 and 2 dx/3, against the reference at the column centre. The heads sit at the centroid of the triangle that owns a side edge, dx/3 inside the face. The strip is uniform across rows, so a row spread is solver noise: the local engine reads below 1e-8 m (its head closure is 1e-9 m); the bound is 1e-7 m.
- Thresholds of `modflow6_irregular_tri`: Twice the error measured on the 176-triangle strip: RMSE 5.9e-3 m, max error 7.5e-3 m. The heads are posed at the mean centroid of the triangles that own a boundary edge, and the reference is averaged over the same x bins as the model. The row spread is zero by construction: the loader tiles one profile.

### Steady Dupuit seepage limit and its invariance in K/R

pass end to endmodflow6

Compared with: Dupuit seepage limit `x_e = L / (1 + slope**2 K/R)` and the free Dupuit water table above it.

\[ x_e=\frac{L}{1+s^2\,K/R} \]
\[ h(x)=s\,x \quad (x<x_e),\qquad h(x)^2=(s\,x_e)^2+\frac{2R}{K}\left(L\,(x-x_e)-\frac{x^2-x_e^2}{2}\right) \quad (x\ge x_e) \]

\(s\) is the slope of the surface, \(L\) the length of the hillslope, \(x\) the distance upslope from the toe, \(K\) the hydraulic conductivity and \(R\) the recharge.

Schedule. This file: runs in Nightly / validation no PETSc, Weekly / Cross Platform, Tests / fast marker. Jobs.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Three claims, in decreasing order of importance:

1. the seepage mask starts where the Dupuit closed form says it does, 2. scaling `K` and `R` by the same factor leaves the mask identical cell for cell and the head equal to a tight band - the property the whole calibration method rests on, 3. the same factor on `K` alone moves the mask, while the total drain discharge does not move at all.

Claim 3 is why claim 2 never looks at the discharge: mass balance pins the total drain outflow at `R * area` whatever the conductance does, so a discharge-based invariance check passes on a model that ignores `K` entirely.

| --- | --- |
| f'{solver} seepage-limit position error' (m) < | 10 |
| f'{solver} head-profile max abs error' (m) < | 0.02 |
| f'{solver} water-table difference vs the reference scenario' (m) < | 0.002 |
| Drain-outflow drift when K alone doubles < | 0.0001 |

Why these thresholds

- Thresholds of `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`, `modflow6_no_newton`: Twice the error measured on the 40-column grid, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: RMSE 5.4e-3 m, max error 7.7e-3 m. Schedule. `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`, `modflow6_no_newton`: runs in Nightly / validation no PETSc, Weekly / Cross Platform. Jobs.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

The case runs through the launcher, the route of `test_dupuit_fixed_head_1d.py`, on copies of its configuration refined twice by 2 (cells of 25, 12.5 and 6.25 m). The slope of the head RMSE against the cell size is the observed order of the scheme.

Without Newton, MODFLOW 6 takes the harmonic mean of the two cell transmissivities, a centred scheme of order 2. A head posed half a cell away from where the reference expects it adds an error of order 1 and drops the observed order to 1. This is the check the MMS tests cannot make: they import nothing from `hydromodpy`.

Under Newton, the HydroModPy default, MODFLOW 6 weights the saturated thickness of the upstream cell, and so does MODFLOW-NWT. That scheme is of order 1 by construction: the RMSE halves when the cells halve (13.3, 6.7 and 3.4 mm here). Both runs are checked against order 1.

Every run closes the head to 1e-9 m, far below the discretization error, so the observed order is the order of the scheme. The bands are those of the MMS orders, `|p - 2| < 0.2` and `|p - 1| < 0.2` (`tests/TOLERANCES.md`).

Run it alone: `python -m validation_cases.analytical.steady.dupuit_fixed_head_1d.run_case`

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

Same closed form as the kernel-level unit test (`tests/unit/physics/test_an_impulse_through_the_transit_store_follows_the_exponential_reservoir.py`), but reached the way a run reaches it: through `compute_soil_forcings`, with a single SAFRAN cell's precipitation and ETP passed in as `FieldRecord` and the recharge read back from the `FieldRecord` it returns.

`spinup = "none"` starts the soil full - "the state of a soil in a wet winter", its own description says - which is exactly the soil a year of rain has already filled. Section 7 gives the closed form for a pulse landing on that full soil and then routed through a linear reservoir of time constant `k`: `Q(0) = 50(1 - k a)`, `Q(t>=1) = 50 k a^2 exp(-(t-1)/k)` with `a = 1 - exp(-1/k)`. `t95`, the day the cumulative recharge first reaches 95 % of the 50 mm pulse, follows the continuous crossing `-k ln(0.05)` within the one day the discretisation can miss it by.

Thresholds from `tests/TOLERANCES.md`

- Row 82: Soil transit store impulse volume, `|sum_t Q - 50|` over `60 k` days, mm: `1e-12`(Machine epsilon. The tail beyond `60 k` days holds `50 exp(-60)`, below 1e-24 mm)
- Row 86: Routed impulse validation case, `t95` against `-k ln 0.05`, days: `1`(Discretisation. Daily steps: the cumulative recharge crosses 95 % within the day that follows the continuous crossing)

### Thin-aquifer Brutsaert recession benchmark

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: nonlinear late recession of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977) for a strip drained on one side, `Q(t) = (Q*^(-1/2) + a t / 2)^(-2)`.

\[ -\frac{dQ}{dt}=a\,Q^{3/2},\qquad Q(t)=\left(Q_*^{-1/2}+\frac{a\,t}{2}\right)^{-2},\qquad a=\frac{C\,\sqrt{K}\,W}{S_y\,(B\,W)^{3/2}} \]

\(K\) is the hydraulic conductivity, \(S_y\) the specific yield, \(B\) the drainage length, \(W\) the outlet width and \(C = 3\,I^{3/2} = 2.4025\) with \(I=\int_0^1 p\,(1-p^3)^{-1/2}\,dp\). Twice \(C\) is the 4.804 of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977), written for a channel drained from both banks (`validation_cases/analytical/transient/brutsaert_reference.py`).

### Deep-aquifer Brutsaert recession benchmark

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_triboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: linearized Boussinesq recession of a deep strip after steady recharge, whose tail is the exponential law of Brutsaert and Nieber (1977).

\[ Q(t)=Q_0\,\frac{B}{B-d}\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{8\cos\!\left(\frac{k\pi d}{2B}\right)}{k^2\pi^2}\,e^{-k^2 a t},\qquad k=2n-1,\qquad a=\frac{\pi^2\,K\,D}{4\,S_y\,B^2} \]

\(Q_0\) is the steady discharge at the end of the warm-up, \(K\) the hydraulic conductivity, \(S_y\) the specific yield, \(D\) the saturated thickness at the outlet, \(B\) the drainage length and \(d\) the length near the outlet that the model does not recharge. The first term alone is the late exponential law (`validation_cases/analytical/transient/brutsaert_reference.py`).

### MODFLOW 6 GWT first-order decay against its closed form

pass modflow6

Compared with: the first-order decay `C(t) = C0 exp(-k t)` of a closed cell.

Last measurement

| Variant | Metric | Measured | Threshold | Share used | Share of the signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| - pass | Largest relative concentration error at 3 times | 0.00265 | < 0.01 | 27% | |

Measured on 2026-10-13, commit `344a70185`, version 2.0.0a5, the nightly CI job (job log).

Schedule. This file: runs in Nightly / validation no PETSc, Weekly / Cross Platform. Jobs.

What the test does, all thresholds, the file

With no advection and no dispersion, a uniform initial concentration decays as `C(t) = C0 * exp(-k t)` under the MF6 MST first-order decay term. The MF6 GWT clock is SECONDS, so the decay rate `k` is in `1/s`. This guards the per-second unit contract for `transport.modflow6gwt.parameters.rate_decay`: a per-day value would be ~86400x too large and annihilate the solute.

Tolerance rationale - `tests/TOLERANCES.md` row 35: max relative concentration error < 1 % (decay is exact in MST; the allowance covers finite time-stepping).

Thresholds from `tests/TOLERANCES.md`

- Row 35: MF6 GWT first-order decay 0D, max relative concentration error vs `C0*exp(-k t)`: `< 1 %`(First-order decay is exact in MF6 MST with no advection or dispersion; small allowance for finite time-stepping)

### Growth of a groundwater mound under a rectangle of recharge against Hantush (1967)

pass end to endmodflow_nwtmodflow6modflow6_irregular_trimodflow6_voronoiboussinesqboussinesq_local

Compared with: Hantush (1967) mound under a rectangle of uniform recharge, linearized with the mean saturated thickness `b = (hi + hm(t)) / 2` taken at the centre `hm`, solved at each time; `S*` integrated with `scipy.integrate.quad_vec`. Carleton (2010, USGS SIR 2010-5102) gives the same form.

\[ h^2-h_i^2=\frac{w}{2K}\,\nu t\left[S^*\!\left((l+x)n,(a+y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l+x)n,(a-y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l-x)n,(a+y)n\right)+S^*\!\left((l-x)n,(a-y)n\right)\right] \]
\[ S^*(\alpha,\beta)=\int_0^1\operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)\operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)d\tau,\qquad \nu=\frac{K\bar b}{S_y},\qquad n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\nu t}},\qquad \bar b=\frac{h_i+h_m(t)}{2} \]

Why these thresholds

- Thresholds of `modflow_nwt`, `modflow6`: Twice the error measured against the Theis drawdown, MODFLOW-NWT and MODFLOW 6 alike: space-time RMSE 4.4e-3 m, max error 9.8e-3 m, final RMSE 5.3e-3 m. The azimuthal spread bound is ten times the MODFLOW 6 head closure, 1e-6 m: the grid is symmetric about the well. Until 2026-10-09 the reference evaluated E1 by an asymptotic series that is wrong between u = 1 and 8, which doubled the space-time error at the outer monitor points.
- Thresholds of `boussinesq_local`: About twice the error measured with the default 'auto' engine, which runs scipy_sparse on the 10082 triangles of 71 x 71 squares (397 m2, the cell area of the MODFLOW grid) with one backward-Euler step a period: space-time RMSE 0.0048 m, max error 0.0140 m, final RMSE 0.0035 m, final max error 0.0045 m, azimuthal spread 0.0012 m. MODFLOW on its 101 x 101 grid, with the same single step a period, reads a space-time RMSE of 0.0044 m: the error is the time step and the fixed-transmissivity Theis reference. The reference is read at the centroid of the triangle each monitor point reads, with the well at the centroid of the triangle that holds it, 6.6 m off the well point. Read from the well point, that offset alone gave an azimuthal spread of 0.136 m on the former 31 x 31 mesh. Until 2026-10-10 the surface closure sent up to 3.4 m3/day of the pumping out of the well cell, 10 m under the top: space-time RMSE 0.0043 m, final max error 0.0064 m.
- Thresholds of `modflow6_irregular_tri`: Twice the error measured on the refined triangle mesh: space-time RMSE 4.4e-3 m, max error 1.45e-2 m, final RMSE 3.4e-3 m, final max error 5.0e-3 m, azimuthal spread 0.020 m. The reference is read at the centroid of the triangle each monitor point reads, with the well at the centroid of the triangle that holds it. The well point is a mesh node, and MODFLOW 6 puts the well in the first triangle that holds it, whose centroid lies 15.4 m away: read from the well point, that offset gave an azimuthal spread of 0.087 m. The spread left, 0.020 m at 60 m where the drawdown is 0.85 m, is the asymmetry of the gmsh refinement (165 to 221 triangles per quadrant within 300 m).
- Thresholds of `modflow6_voronoi`: Twice the error measured on the Voronoi dual of the refined mesh, the reference read at the node of the cell each monitor point reads: space-time RMSE 9.4e-3 m, max error 2.3e-2 m, final RMSE 6.3e-3 m, final max error 7.7e-3 m, azimuthal spread of the error 2.2e-3 m. A node sits on the well, so the cell that holds the well is centred on it. Read at the monitor radius instead, 1 to 18 m from that node, the error was twice as large. Until 2026-10-10 the spread was taken on the drawdown, not on the error, and read 0.040 m: the cells read sit at different radii.
